scenes.prose:
> The fitter's words had been dropped into the fitting-room chatter like a pin into a cushion — careless, sharp, and exactly where it would be found.
> *(Evening. Hartwell House, the small parlor. Rose alone with her pocketbook, the rout still two hours off. She writes: *Trelawney & Sons, Bath — discounts émigré notes for particular London houses.*)*
> (T1 · look closer) *She studies the phrase — "particular London houses." Houses, not men: names on doors, clerks in counting-rooms, a cut or a principal behind the discount.* — remembered: *houses, not men.*
> (T2 · choice — the filing:)
> - **The front page** — *War+.* The active page, where the war is; the name lives beside the de Valcourt endorsement.
> - **The back page** — *Debt+.* Where the debts are, where it might be billing; the name waits its turn.
> *(She sets it on the front page, beside Alder's Bath direction and the de Valcourt endorsement copied from Quill's paper. The trail was forming its own geography: Bath, a banking house, a discount window, and above it all the particular houses of London, doing particular business in émigré paper.)*
> (T3 · stance) *She decides what "uphill" means — Rackham's scattered debts had not scattered at random; they had scattered uphill, and uphill ended at a door with a brass plate on it.* — remembered: *uphill, to a brass plate.*
> (T4 · look closer) *She copies the endorsement from memory — *L. de Valcourt — to be settled against the Hartwell account* — and underlines the fitter's "particular" twice.* — remembered: *the London end, underlined.*
> "Particular London houses." She said it aloud to the empty parlor. A banking house does not discount foreign paper out of sentiment. It discounts it for a cut — or for a principal.
> (T5 · tone) *She speaks the name once more before closing the book — like a creditor naming a debtor, cold and exact; or like a hunter naming quarry, warm and alive.* — remembered: *the naming, chosen.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *She closes the pocketbook on the front page — the ticking page — and sets it in her reticule for the rout.* — remembered: *the page, ticking.*
> (T7 · stance) *She fixes the evening's order: Honoria launched, dances spent, capital converted — and underneath, the pocketbook spending itself on Bath.* — remembered: *the evening's order.*
> (T8 · choice — the clock:)
> - **Dress at once** — *Ready+.* The rout in two hours; the thesis, the pins, the transformation begun.
> - **One more minute** — *Resolve+.* The parlor, the name, the quiet — the war, acknowledged before the performance.
> *(She takes the minute. "Trelawney," she says — hunter, not creditor; the quarry had a pulse and she meant to feel it — and goes up to dress for a rout in which she will spend her evening launching someone else, while her pocketbook spends itself on Bath.)*

scenes.synopsis: The invitations, redirected — Honoria's card fills; Rose's own thins; the price itemized in paper. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> The morning room table was covered in cards — Rose's week and Honoria's week, laid side by side like two ledgers, and the arithmetic between them was not flattering to either.
> (T1 · look closer) *She studies the two piles — Honoria's growing with every card Rose redirects; her own thinning by the same measure. Letitia presides, marking each transfer in red.* — remembered: *the arithmetic.*
> "The Musgrave musicale — Honoria, with you. The Aldous at-home — Honoria, with you. The Crayke rout — both of you. And Thursday's dinner at the Porters' — " Letitia hesitated. "You are asked. She is not. The question is whether you are asked *enough* to carry her in."
> (T2 · choice — the Porters' dinner:)
> - **Carry Honoria in** — *Sponsorship+.* Spend the invitation; Drummond's terms say visibly and repeatedly.
> - **Hold the Porters' for herself** — *Reserve+.* The one evening she keeps; her own week, kept.
> *(She carries her. "Drummond's terms say visibly and repeatedly. A dinner unshared is a term unmet.")*
> "It is also," said Letitia, marking the transfer in red, "a dinner you will not enjoy — the Porters seat their guests by precedence of gossip. But very well. The price is the price." She surveyed the piles. "Honoria's card is now fuller than yours was at the height of your first Season."
> (T3 · social maneuver) *She rewrites her own replies — the acceptances declined, the regrets sent — and chooses their tone.*
> - **Warm and vague** — *Grace+.* No one offended; the declines, deniable.
> - **Honest and brief** — *Candor+.* The dragon's business, unnamed; the truth, trimmed.
> - **Strategic** — *Leverage+.* A reason that improves her; every regret, a purchase.
> (T4 · stance) *She decides what the week's thinning means — the ton will do the arithmetic, and the ton is better at arithmetic than anyone admits.* — remembered: *the ton's arithmetic.*
> (T5 · look closer) *She touches Honoria's pile — ribboned in Drummond burgundy — and her own, thin and unbound. What she feels: satisfaction, and theft, and the honesty to admit the second.* — remembered: *satisfaction and theft.*
> "Both," she said. "Satisfaction, and theft, and the honesty to admit the second." She stood. "Send the acceptances. And Letitia — put the Porters' reply in my own hand. If I am to spend the invitation, the ton may as well see the signature."
> (T6 · tone) *She chooses the week's register — the patron's, unapologetic; the spending will be read, so let it be read in her own hand.* — remembered: *the register.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She keeps the Porters' card on the desk until the footman comes — the signature, drying; the commitment, visible.* — remembered: *the signature, drying.*
> (T8 · stance) *She sets the week's terms: the invitations are paper, and paper is spent; what matters is what the spending buys.* — remembered: *the terms.*

scenes.synopsis: Honoria fears the rout — the wallflower's terror of the crush; Rose teaches her the room is a machine with levers. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> Honoria arrived at noon with the Crayke rout's card held like a summons and her courage visibly packed for a different, smaller evening.
> "Two hundred people," she said. "Mrs. Crayke's rooms hold two hundred. I have counted the chairs twice, and there are not two hundred chairs, which means one stands, and standing is where one is *seen* — " She stopped, breathless. "Miss Hartwell, I cannot. A rout is only *people*, and people have eyes, and I have never once survived being looked at by more than twelve."
> (T1 · tone) *She chooses her answer's register — the general's, the friend's, or the patron's; Honoria will hear the register and remember it.*
> - **The general's** — *Command+.* "Then we take the room in sections."
> - **The friend's** — *Warmth+.* "I was afraid too, once."
> - **The patron's** — *Authority+.* "Nonsense, you are ready."
> *(She chooses the general — the friend would have lied and the patron would have been believed by no one.)*
> "Then we take the room in sections," Rose said. "A rout is not two hundred people, Honoria. It is twenty groups of ten, and you will never face more than one group at a time, and you will face each group exactly as long as you choose, because you will have somewhere else to be — me, the retiring room, the supper table, the next group. Nobody at a rout is ever *in* the room. They are *passing through* it."
> "And if a group asks me something I cannot answer?"
> (T2 · social maneuver) *She teaches the deflection — and demonstrates each; the game remembers which Honoria practices.*
> - **The return question** — *Deflect+.* "And what does *your* family think of it?"
> - **The honest deferral** — *Candor+.* "I don't know — do tell me."
> - **The strategic retreat** — *Escape+.* "Oh, look — Miss Hartwell is signaling."
> (T3 · look closer) *She studies Honoria's face — the girl is taking notes, mentally, the way she once took notes on pianoforte fingering; terror, converting to logistics.* — remembered: *the conversion.*
> "The return question," Rose said, demonstrating. "People at routs do not want answers. They want audiences. Give them the stage for one sentence, and they will remember you as the best conversationalist of the evening — having heard you say nothing at all."
> "Is that — honest?"
> (T4 · stance) *She decides what honesty costs at a rout — the evening, nothing, or the wrong question entirely.*
> - **It costs the evening** — *Plain+.* Say it plainly; honesty has its hours.
> - **It costs nothing** — *Theater+.* The room runs on theater, and theater is honest about being theater.
> - **The wrong question** — *Survival+.* Survival first, philosophy after midnight.
> *(She chooses the wrong question. "Ask it of me again at one in the morning, when the crush has thinned. That is when honesty is affordable.")*
> (T5 · tone) *She sets the lesson's close — brisk, like a drill; or gentle, like a confidence.* — remembered: *the drill.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *She assigns the first set — Mr. Fenwick, kind and dull, who will not step on her; the second, with Rose herself; the sections, practiced.* — remembered: *the sections.*
> "You will dance the first set with Mr. Fenwick — he is kind, he is dull, and he will not step on you, which in a crush is the highest praise a partner can earn. The second with me. We will practice the sections."
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She gives Honoria the evening's map — the hostess, the dowagers, the young set; the order of the sections, committed to memory.* — remembered: *the map.*
> (T8 · stance) *She watches Honoria stand — straighter than at noon; the terror, not gone, but drilled.* — remembered: *the straightening.*
> *(Honoria stands straighter than she had stood at noon. "The second with *you*?" she says — and Rose smiles, and means it, mostly: "Consider it the tussie-mussie of dances, Honoria. The thorns are stripped. I come unarmed — and so, tonight, do you.")*

scenes.synopsis: Letitia's logistics — the dance card as a battle plan; partners assigned, dances budgeted like coin. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> The dance card, when Letitia had finished with it, looked less like an evening's pleasure and more like a quartermaster's manifest.
> *(Afternoon. The morning room. Letitia rules lines across a spare card in pencil, assigning Rose's dances the way a general assigns rations.)*
> "First set — Honoria with Mr. Fenwick, you with Mr. Crayke, who is the host's son and must be flattered. Second — the practice set, you and Honoria. Third — you give your dance to Mr. Allardyce, and Miss Penn takes *your* third, and you take a turn about the room with Lady Aldous, who must be seen to forgive you the leash remark."
> (T1 · look closer) *She studies the card — her name penciled beside dances she will not dance, for partners she has not chosen, in service of a girl who is not her. The erasures say: the price, itemized; the work, organized; the evening, already spent.* — remembered: *the card, read.*
> "It says the evening is already spent," Rose said, "and it is not yet four o'clock. Is that the record?"
> "The record was your first Season's Almack's. You were seventeen and generous by nature. You are twenty-one and generous by contract." Letitia set down the pencil. "There is one dance I have left blank."
> (T2 · choice — the blank dance:)
> - **Keep it for herself** — *Self+.* One set, unspent, unaccounted; the purse with legs, walking.
> - **Give it to Honoria's weakest hour** — *Launch+.* The supper set, when the crush is cruelest; a reserve, spent where the wilting is worst.
> - **Leave it blank** — *Chance+.* Let the evening decide; the card, uncommitted.
> *(She gives it to the supper set. "That is when the crush is cruelest and the wallflowers wilt fastest. A blank dance at supper is a reserve — and even Drummond keeps a reserve.")*
> "Drummond," said Letitia, writing it in, "keeps several, and calls them nieces." She surveyed the card. "You will dance perhaps four sets of your own, stand up for two you give away, and spend the rest being seen to enjoy the spending. The ton watches the spending — it is the only part of an evening that cannot be counterfeited."
> (T3 · social maneuver) *She chooses their entrance time — and the statement it makes.*
> - **Early** — *Visible+.* Seen arriving with Honoria; the sponsorship visible from the first minute.
> - **Fashionably late** — *Event+.* The room already full; the entrance, an event.
> - **Exactly on time** — *Neutral+.* No statement at all.
> (T4 · stance) *She decides what the card's arithmetic proves — the evening is spent before it begins, and that is the point; the spending is the strategy.* — remembered: *the strategy.*
> (T5 · look closer) *She examines Letitia's pencil work — the ruled lines, the erasures, the blank supper set; a battle plan, in pencil.* — remembered: *the battle plan.*
> (T6 · tone) *She names the evening to herself — a campaign, not a pleasure; the word steadies her.* — remembered: *the campaign.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She pockets the spare card — the battle plan, carried; the evening, mapped.* — remembered: *the card, pocketed.*
> (T8 · choice — the evening's first move:)
> - **The hostess, first** — *Permission+.* Mrs. Crayke flattered; the room's permission, granted.
> - **The dowagers, first** — *Softened+.* The queens courted early; the verdicts, softened.
> *(She chooses early, and the hostess first. "If I am to be seen spending, let the spending be visible from the first minute. The ton prices what it sees. Let it see all of it.")*

scenes.synopsis: Texture — the merge board: the standing order queue, the free-income engine; the atelier funds the season while Rose spends it. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(System: merge-board texture scene — the standing order queue. Orders wait, merge, and complete in the background — the free-income engine that funds the season's coins.)*
> At Élise's workroom, between the card-sorting and the rout, the great order board told its own story — commissions pinned in rows, each at its own stage, each advancing while Rose advanced hers.
> Three standing orders waited: a widow's grey silk being softened for half-mourning, a debutante's ball gown awaiting its final fitting, a gentleman's waistcoat — cut for a wedding, recut for a funeral — moving through its stages like a small, dignified tragedy. Each completion would drop its coins into the Hartwell purse.
> (T1 · choice — the purse:)
> - **Collect the completed orders now** — *Coin+.* Coins in hand for the rout's costs; the purse, fed.
> - **Let them ride** — *Compound+.* The queue compounds; patience pays.
> (T2 · look closer) *She studies the board's arithmetic — pins, stages, the patient columns; the board never empties, and that is the point.* — remembered: *the board's arithmetic.*
> Élise moved a pin — the widow's silk, done, its coins counted into the purse with the soft chink of honest arithmetic. "The queue never empties, chérie. While you are spending dances in ballrooms, the board is earning them back in coin. You spend the evenings; the atelier spends the mornings."
> (T3 · stance) *She decides what the workroom is — the season's honest engine, turning thread into money while she turns money into standing.* — remembered: *the engine.*
> (T4 · look closer) *She examines the burgundy merino offcuts — her own, from the Drummond-call ritual — advancing along the chain toward becoming somebody's trim.* — remembered: *the offcuts.*
> (T5 · choice — the offcuts' meaning:)
> - **Nothing wasted** — *Doctrine+.* The season's doctrine; even the armor gets reused.
> - **The price, recycled** — *Economy+.* The Drummond-call's cost, returned as somebody's trim.
> - **A private satisfaction** — *Hers+.* Hers, and no one else's.
> *(She chooses nothing wasted. "We spend the dances, we keep the coins, and the offcuts become somebody else's trim.")*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *She sets the workroom's orders — keep the queue moving; the rout tonight will cost her everything but coin, and the coin the board can replace.* — remembered: *the orders.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She advances one pin herself — a small merge, completed; the board hums, the coins drop.* — remembered: *the merge, made.*
> (T8 · stance) *She leaves the workroom with the season's division of labor fixed: she spends the evenings; the atelier spends the mornings; between them, the house stays solvent.* — remembered: *the division.*
> *("The board," said Élise, pinning with finality, "replaces everything but the dances. The dances are yours to lose, chérie. Spend them well.")*

scenes.synopsis: Élise's Bath clients gossip by post — the Trelawney name again; fashion as intelligence, arriving with the pins. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> The letter came with the afternoon's parcel from the workroom — folded into the tissue with the rout's gloves, in the fitter's hurried hand, half gossip and half invoice.
> "Read it," Élise said, "and then tell me it is nothing, so I can tell the fitter she imagines things, and we can all be comfortable." She did not look comfortable.
> Rose read. The Bath clients — wives of bankers, daughters of discounters — gossiped the way clients always gossiped: about money, disguised as talk of muslins. *Mr. Trelawney's house discounts the French paper, and the London houses take it up — V— something, the new house, the one with the brass plate — and the discount is too kind for the risk.*
> (T1 · look closer) *She studies the fragment — "V— something, the new house, the one with the brass plate." A banker's wife, being pinned for a morning dress, says what her husband says at breakfast.* — remembered: *the fragment.*
> (T2 · stance) *She decides what the breakfast-table sourcing means — a Bath banker is saying, at breakfast, that a London house with a brass plate takes up French paper at too kind a discount; either the paper is better than it looks, or the house is worse.* — remembered: *the breakfast table.*
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *She copies the fragment into the pocketbook beside *Trelawney & Sons* and *particular London houses*.* — remembered: *the fragment, filed.*
> (T4 · social maneuver) *She sets the atelier's standing orders — the fitter's ears, the workroom's arrangement.*
> - **Listen harder** — *Tasked+.* The fitter tasked, the channel formalized; the risk, taken.
> - **Listen as usual** — *Steady+.* No change, no risk; the channel, unforced.
> - **Listen less** — *Cautious+.* The channel too close to the war; the ears, lowered.
> *(She chooses as usual. "A fitter who listens harder starts asking questions, and a fitter who asks questions stops being told things. The atelier hears everything because the atelier is furniture. Keep it furniture, Élise. Furniture with excellent hearing.")*
> (T5 · look closer) *She examines Élise's face — the modiste is not comfortable; the letter has frightened her, a little, and she is hiding it behind business.* — remembered: *the fright, hidden.*
> (T6 · tone) *She steadies Élise — the ally's register, not the general's; the workroom is not the war.* — remembered: *the steadying.*
> (T7 · stance) *She decides the channel's value — the atelier's oldest arrangement: the pins go in, the gossip comes out; fashion as intelligence.* — remembered: *the arrangement.*
> (T8 · choice — the fragment's weight:)*
> - **The trail's next link** — *War+.* The brass-plate house, named by a banker's wife; the pocketbook's front page, warming.
> - **Gossip, for now** — *Reserve+.* Filed, not pursued; the war has its order, and the rout is tonight.
> *("Furniture," Élise agreed, "with pins." She turned back to the gloves. "And tonight you are not furniture, chérie. Tonight you are the room's most generous exhibit. Try to enjoy the spending. It photographs better.")*

scenes.synopsis: ★ FASHION-SELECTION — the rout gown's thesis: shine, but launch another. No coin cost, remembered. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(System: fashion-selection — diegetic, no coin cost. The choice is remembered and will surface in Gazette and caller dialogue.)*
> "The rout," said Letitia, laying three sketches across the bed, "is the week's great crush. The gown must shine — and launch another. Choose the thesis, and the atelier will build the argument: motif, colorway, thread, every accessory."
>
> **A. The Generous Star** — rose-gold silk; she outshines everyone and spends the shine on Honoria, like largesse. *Motif:* star-jasmine embroidery across bodice and overskirt — largesse as botany. *Colorway:* rose-gold, blush to apricot at the hem. *Thread:* gold — copper and polychrome weighed. *Accessories:* ivory gloves; gold star-drop earrings; fine gold chain, one star-jasmine pendant; gold wheat-star hairpins; ivory fan with gold sticks; rose-gold reticule on gold cord.
> **B. The Setting** — deep sapphire velvet, quiet and exact; she is the setting, Honoria the stone. *Motif:* moon-vine whitework circling neckline and hem — restraint as ornament. *Colorway:* deep sapphire, near-black in candlelight. *Thread:* ivory whitework — silver and steel weighed. *Accessories:* ivory gloves; silver moon-drop earrings; no necklace; silver crescent comb; deep blue fan with silver sticks; sapphire velvet reticule, silver clasp.
> **C. The Hartwell Signal** — Hartwell burgundy, unapologetic; the house that pays, dressing like it. *Motif:* climbing-rose embroidery ascending the overskirt — the house, climbing. *Colorway:* Hartwell burgundy, claret, deep and warm. *Thread:* gold — copper and black silk weighed. *Accessories:* ivory gloves; gold rose-drop earrings; gold necklace, rose clasp; burgundy rose hairpins, gold leaves; burgundy fan with gold sticks; burgundy velvet reticule, gold cord.
>
> *(System: no coin cost. The selection is remembered — the Gazette will judge the thesis, and callers will quote it.)*
> (T1 · choice) *She chooses — A, B, or C; the evening's thesis, remembered.*
> (T2 · look closer) *She studies the three sketches under the lamplight — how each reads at distance; the ton judges at twenty paces, and the thesis must speak that far.* — remembered: *the distance, judged.*
> (T3 · stance) *She weighs the risks — the Star risks outshining the launch; the Setting risks invisibility; the Signal risks the dragon's reading, for Drummond will count the burgundy as hers.* — remembered: *the risks, weighed.*
> (T4 · look closer) *She examines the embroidery — star-jasmine in gold (generosity); moon-vine in whitework (restraint); climbing rose in gold (power). The atelier notes which language she speaks.* — remembered: *the language.*
> (T5 · social maneuver) *She considers the accessory suites — the Star's public gold; the Setting's exact silver; the Signal's gold-and-burgundy — and how each photographs at a rout.* — remembered: *the suites.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *She runs her hand over the chosen sketch — the cloth imagined, the thesis felt; the decision, made by touch.* — remembered: *the touch.*
> (T7 · stance) *She sets the thesis like a seal — shine, but launch another; the gown will be the argument, and the evening the proof.* — remembered: *the seal.*
> Rose ran her hand over the three sketches — and chose. "Well chosen," said Letitia. "Ninety minutes to become the thesis. The pins are waiting."
> "I have dances to spare," Rose said, "because I have decided to. There is a difference, and the difference is the whole of the evening."

scenes.synopsis: ★ DRESSING RITUAL — preparation for the Crayke rout. Twenty-five decomposed micro-decisions at 5 coins each (~125 coins). Jewels from owned pieces only; the jewel shelf is always open, never a ritual step. (Turns: 26 — direction + 25 pins)
scenes.prose:
> *(System: the occasion brief is published.)*
>
> **Occasion brief — A London Rout**
> *Mrs. Crayke's rout, this evening — two hundred people, no chairs, all eyes. The brief is* shine while launching another: *evening dress for a woman who must be the room's light and another girl's lamp, both at once. Every choice is judged on whether it says* generosity that photographs *without saying a word about the price. Outshining the launch is failure; dimming for it is also failure; the exact middle is everything.*
>
> Élise reads the brief twice, nods once, and clears the fitting table.
> "The thesis is chosen," she says. "Now we build the argument — pin by pin, and the room will read every one."
> *(System: the ritual runs 25 micro-decisions, 5 coins each. Each decision releases the next story morsel. Re-picks free in session; re-styling after the scene always free. No Crown SKU touches the ritual.)*
>
> (T1 · choice — the direction) *She commits: A. The Generous Star, B. The Setting, or C. The Hartwell Signal — the evening's thesis, remembered.*
>
> **Pin 1 (T2 · micro-decision) — The brief, confirmed:** shine while launching another — the thesis read against the occasion, the exact middle aimed at. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 2 (T3 · micro-decision) — The dress silhouette:** full-skirted ball gown — the rout's architecture, built to move through a crush. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 3 (T4 · micro-decision) — The bodice cut:** fitted and boned — the thesis's foundation, exact. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 4 (T5 · micro-decision) — The bodice fabric:** satin, silk, or velvet — the hand of the evening. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 5 (T6 · micro-decision) — The bodice color:** rose-gold, sapphire, or burgundy — the thesis's first declaration. *5 coins.*
>
> *(Story morsel: the fitter on Mrs. Crayke's crush — "two hundred, miss, and the supper room holds forty — the arithmetic of a rout is *standing*.")*
>
> **Pin 6 (T7 · micro-decision) — The sleeve style:** short and puffed, or long and fitted — the arm's statement. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 7 (T8 · micro-decision) — The sleeve fabric:** matching the bodice, or a contrast that catches candlelight. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 8 (T9 · micro-decision) — The sleeve color:** tone with the bodice, or a shade deeper for depth. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 9 (T10 · micro-decision) — The neckline:** low and draped, or modest — the evening's daring, calibrated. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 10 (T11 · micro-decision) — The overskirt:** present, caught up to show the underskirt — the thesis's drama; or absent, the line unbroken. *5 coins.*
>
> *(Story morsel: Letitia through the door with the dance card's final revision — "the supper set is yours to give, my love — spend it where the wilting is worst.")*
>
> **Pin 11 (T12 · micro-decision) — The skirt style:** full and trained — the crush parts for it. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 (T13 · micro-decision) — The skirt fabric:** silk, satin, or crape — the rustle, chosen. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 13 (T14 · micro-decision) — The skirt color:** the thesis's ground — rose-gold blush, deep sapphire, or Hartwell claret. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 (T15 · micro-decision) — The trim:** embroidered, ruched, or edged — the thesis's handwriting. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 (T16 · micro-decision) — The shoes:** satin slippers, dyed to match — the dance's foundation. *5 coins.*
>
> *(Story morsel: Honoria's note, delivered by hand — *"I am afraid. — H."* — and Rose's reply, written between pins: *"Then be afraid in the right gown. — R.")*
>
> **Pin 16 (T17 · micro-decision) — The stockings:** silk, clocked or plain — the ankle's quiet. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 17 (T18 · micro-decision) — The gloves:** ivory, elbow-length — the hand, gloved for the evening's business. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 (T19 · micro-decision) — The hair:** dressed high, curled and pinned — the crown of the thesis. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 19 (T20 · micro-decision) — The hair piece:** star pins, crescent comb, or rose pins — the thesis's signature. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 20 (T21 · micro-decision) — The earrings:** star-drop, moon-drop, or rose-drop — the candlelight's answer. *5 coins.*
>
> *(Story morsel: Augusta's card slipped under the door — *"Shine, child. The launching is the shining.")*
>
> **Pin 21 (T22 · micro-decision) — The necklace:** the fine chain with its pendant — or none, the neckline left to speak. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 22 (T23 · micro-decision) — The bracelet:** worn, a glint at the wrist — or foregone, the restraint itself an ornament. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 23 (T24 · micro-decision) — The beauty:** powder, a touch of rouge — the rout's face, the thesis worn on skin. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 24 (T25 · micro-decision) — The fan:** ivory with gold sticks, blue with silver, or burgundy with gold — the hand's punctuation. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 25 (T26 · micro-decision) — The finishing accessory:** the reticule on its cord — the thesis's seal, carried into the crush. *5 coins.*
>
> *(Story morsel: the Gazette's morning paragraph on yesterday's calls, read aloud by Élise's girl; the pocketbook, open on the table — *Trelawney & Sons* catching Élise's eye, and her one raised eyebrow, and Rose's one shake of the head: not now; the pins first, the war after.)*
>
> **Reveal coda:** the mirror moment — the lamp light, the thesis made cloth; Letitia's verdict from the doorway ("The room will read it, my love. Now go and let it."); the look saved to the season lookbook; the profile portrait struck.
> *(System: 25 pins × 5 coins = 125 coins drawn from play earnings. The completed direction is remembered. Owned jewels may be added freely from the open shelf at any point, never as a step.)*

ritual.occasionBrief: A London Rout. Mrs. Crayke's rout, this evening — two hundred people, no chairs, all eyes. The brief is* shine while launching another: *evening dress for a woman who must be the room's light and another girl's lamp, both at once. Every choice is judged on whether it says* generosity that photographs *without saying a word about the price. Outshining the launch is failure; dimming for it is also failure; the exact middle is everything.

scenes.synopsis: Texture — the rout's doors; the room's hum before the crush; Rose arrives early, with Honoria, the sponsorship visible. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> Mrs. Crayke's rooms were already humming when they arrived — early, as planned, the sponsorship visible from the first minute.
> *(Evening. The rout. Rose enters with Honoria on her arm; the room's hum changes pitch, the way a room does when it has been given something to price.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *She reads the room — the candles, the tuning musicians, the supper room already too small; two hundred people expected, none of the chairs that do not exist.* — remembered: *the room, read.*
> (T2 · social maneuver) *She chooses their first circuit — the hostess, the dowagers, the young set; each group of ten, faced and passed through like a section of the siege.*
> - **The hostess first** — *Permission+.* Mrs. Crayke flattered; the room's permission, granted.
> - **The dowagers' corner** — *Softened+.* The queens courted early; the verdicts, softened.
> - **The young set** — *Launch+.* Honoria's peers; the launch where it matters.
> *(She chooses the hostess first. "Mrs. Crayke flattered is a room permitted. The queens can wait — queens always can, it is their profession.")*
> (T3 · tone) *She sets her manner for the evening — bright and easy, warm and deliberate, or brilliant and just tired enough.*
> - **Bright and easy** — *Effortless+.* The spending looks effortless.
> - **Warm and deliberate** — *Chosen+.* The spending looks chosen.
> - **Brilliant, just tired enough** — *Honest+.* The spending looks costly, and honest.
> (T4 · stance) *She decides the circuit's doctrine — nobody at a rout is ever *in* the room; they are passing through it, and so is she.* — remembered: *the doctrine.*
> (T5 · look closer) *She watches Honoria mid-circuit — the girl laughs at something Mr. Fenwick says, and the laugh is unguarded, and the room hears it.* — remembered: *the laugh.*
> (T6 · choice — the moment:)*
> - **Mark it** — *Noted+.* A glance, a nod — *well done*; the girl, seen.
> - **Spend it** — *Leverage+.* Two more partners steered toward the girl at once; the moment, multiplied.
> - **Let it be** — *Trust+.* Say nothing; let the room do the work.
> *(She lets it be. The room was doing the work now — the launch, launched; the discovery, discovering itself.)*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She spends the entrance, the circuit, the first of the evening's capital — and notes the dances still to spend, the supper set still blank.* — remembered: *the capital, spending.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She files the evening's first arithmetic: the girl is shining, the shine is catching, and the ton is pricing it fair.* — remembered: *the pricing.*
> *(For one circuit, at least, the arithmetic was simple: the girl was shining, and the shine was catching, and the ton was doing what the ton did best — pricing it, and finding the price fair.)*

scenes.synopsis: The rout — Honoria's near-disaster; the crush's cruelty finds the wallflower at the supper table. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> It happened at the supper table, as these things do — where the crush was cruelest and the chairs, had there been any, would have been fewest.
> *(The rout, near midnight. The supper room, forty places for two hundred people. Honoria, separated from Rose in the press, finds herself at a table with three young ladies of the sharpest kind.)*
> "Miss Drummond," said the sharpest — a Miss Ollerton, all bright eyes and brighter malice — "we were *so* interested to hear of your sponsorship. One wonders what she *receives* for it. A dragon's niece does not come without a dragon's terms, after all."
> (T1 · look closer) *Rose, across the room, sees it happen — the flush, the silence, the cats with their string; the one question Honoria has asked herself in private every night for a month, asked in public.* — remembered: *the question, asked.*
> (T2 · choice — the crossing:)*
> - **At once** — *Visible+.* The rescue immediate; the power, visible.
> - **Through the crowd** — *Natural+.* A minute's delay; the arrival, natural.
> - **Via Lady Aldous** — *Deniable+.* The dowager sent first; the rescue, deniable.
> *(She crosses at once — through the crowd, which parted for her the way crowds part for women who have decided.)*
> "Miss Ollerton," she said, "you are monopolizing the evening's most interesting guest, and I must insist on my turn." She turned to Honoria, her voice carrying across the supper room's sudden quiet. "My dear, Lady Aldous has been asking after you — she wishes to know whether the Hartwell sponsorship extends to opinions on the new Italian opera. You will tell her the sponsorship covers everything, including opera. Won't you?"
> (T3 · social maneuver) *She executes the rescue — and chooses its method.*
> - **The promotion** — *Elevate+.* Honoria elevated; the question, buried.
> - **The deflection** — *Starve+.* The table's attention turned; the malice, starved.
> - **The counter** — *Teach+.* Miss Ollerton answered in kind; the cats, taught manners.
> *(It is the promotion, with the deflection folded inside it: Honoria elevated to Lady Aldous's inquisitor, the table's malice starved of its audience. The supper room laughs — *with*, this time, not *at*.)*
> (T4 · tone) *She chooses her parting line to the table — light, pointed, or silent.*
> - **Light** — *Charm+.* "Do save me some syllabub — I am spending the evening, and must keep my strength."
> - **Pointed** — *Edge+.* "Miss Drummond's conversation improves every table — I recommend the experience."
> - **Silent** — *Mystery+.* A smile, and gone.
> *(She chooses light. The table laughs, the danger passes, and the launch — which had nearly run aground on a supper table — rights itself and sails on.)*
> (T5 · look closer) *She watches Honoria rise — steadier than she has any right to be — and go to Lady Aldous on Rose's arm.* — remembered: *the rising.*
> (T6 · stance) *She decides what the rescue cost — a dance, a crossing, a line about syllabub; and what it bought — a room's decision.* — remembered: *the cost, the purchase.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She notes Miss Ollerton, left holding her string with no cat to play with — the lesson, delivered; the cat, unharmed.* — remembered: *the lesson.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She files the evening's rule: rescues done well become the evening's story, and the story becomes Honoria's.* — remembered: *the rule.*

scenes.synopsis: Aftermath — the room re-prices Honoria; the ton's cruelty and kindness both arrive, and both must be managed. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> The supper room's laughter had done what no sponsorship could: it had made Honoria *interesting*.
> *(The rout, past midnight. The word travels the room faster than any footman: Miss Drummond has spirit. The cats retreat; the kind ones advance.)*
> (T1 · social maneuver) *She manages the evening's edges — the girls who were cruel at supper, now approaching with smiles; the kind ones, emboldened.*
> - **Let them come** — *Open+.* The converts, welcomed; the room, united.
> - **Hold them off** — *Guard+.* The girl, protected; the cats, watched.
> - **Make them ask** — *Price+.* Apology with an entry fee; forgiveness, priced.
> (T2 · look closer) *She studies Honoria's face — the girl is smiling, and the smile is her own, not the drilled one; it has survived supper, and that makes it real.* — remembered: *the smile, survived.*
> (T3 · tone) *She chooses the register for the rest of the evening — warm and steady, the launch's captain; the girl, sailing.* — remembered: *the captain's register.*
> (T4 · stance) *She decides what the room's re-pricing means — the ton is fickle, but it is honest about fickleness; kindness and cruelty are both performances, and both must be directed.* — remembered: *the directing.*
> (T5 · look closer) *She notes who advances — the kind ones, who were kind before it was fashionable; the remembered kindness, the only kind that counts.* — remembered: *the kind ones.*
> (T6 · choice — the evening's close:)*
> - **Leave at the peak** — *Wisdom+.* The triumph, banked; the girl, not overdrawn.
> - **Stay till the end** — *Completeness+.* Every dance spent; the ledger, balanced.
> - **Slip away unmarked** — *Mystery+.* The room wondering where they went; the exit, a statement.
> *(She leaves at the peak. "Triumph," she tells Honoria, "is like syllabub — it curdles if you keep it too long.")*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She choreographs the departure — the hostess thanked, the dowagers saluted, the girl's exit as triumphant as her entrance.* — remembered: *the choreography.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She files the evening's verdict: the launch, launched; the room, re-priced; the price, paid in dances she will not dance again.* — remembered: *the verdict.*
> *(In the carriage home, Honoria is quiet for a full minute — and then: "I did not wilt." "No," says Rose. "You did not." And the girl's smile, in the dark of the carriage, is the evening's truest currency.)*

scenes.synopsis: The dragon's debrief — Lady Agatha hears the rout's report; the creditor counts her collateral. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> Lady Agatha received the rout's report the way she received everything: as a creditor receiving an accounting.
> *(Morning. Drummond House. Lady Agatha behind her desk, the week's ledger open; Rose reporting, as the sponsored report to the sponsor.)*
> "The supper room," Rose said, "produced one incident of the sharp kind. Miss Ollerton asked, in company, what the sponsorship *costs* me."
> (T1 · tone) *She chooses the report's register — the creditor's, exact; the dragon counts collateral, not feelings.*
> - **Exact and complete** — *Ledger+.* Every dance, every incident; the accounting, full.
> - **Exact and edited** — *Managed+.* The incident included, the terror omitted; the collateral, presented.
> - **Warm and defended** — *Loyal+.* The girl defended first; the accounting, second.
> *(She chooses exact and complete. "Miss Ollerton asked the question. Honoria answered it — by surviving it. The room re-priced her by midnight.")*
> "Hmph." Lady Agatha made a note. "And the dances? The afternoons? The invitations — the Porters' dinner, specifically. I am told you carried her in."
> (T2 · social maneuver) *She presents the week's agenda — every term of Drummond's price, itemized and met.*
> - **The full accounting** — *Compliant+.* Every term, visibly met; the dragon, satisfied.
> - **The highlights** — *Confident+.* The victories, presented; the compliance, assumed.
> - **The forward look** — *Strategic+.* The week's wins, the next week's plan; the creditor, courted.
> *(The full accounting. "The Porters' dinner — carried, as instructed. The invitations — redirected. The dances — spent. The afternoons — hers.")*
> (T3 · look closer) *She studies the dragon's face — the satisfaction is real, and so is the surprise; the creditor had priced the collateral lower than it performed.* — remembered: *the surprise.*
> "You have done," said Lady Agatha slowly, "better than the terms required. I had priced the girl lower. You have made her — " she searched for the word, visibly annoyed at needing it — "interesting."
> (T4 · stance) *She decides what the compliment costs — nothing, from the dragon; which makes it the most expensive thing in the room.* — remembered: *the compliment's cost.*
> (T5 · tone) *She accepts it the way one accepts dragon-gold — carefully, with both hands, and no sudden moves.* — remembered: *the acceptance.*
> (T6 · choice — the ask:)*
> - **Ask for nothing** — *Reserve+.* The credit, banked; the dragon, owed nothing.
> - **Ask for the next week's terms, early** — *Forward+.* The agenda, seized; the creditor, led.
> - **Ask for Honoria's freedom, a little** — *Mercy+.* One unchaperoned afternoon; the girl, trusted.
> *(She asks for nothing. "The credit will keep," she says. "Dragons remember debts better than debtors do.")*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She takes her leave — the debrief closed, the ledger balanced, the dragon's door closing behind her with the soft sound of a vault.* — remembered: *the vault.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She files the morning's lesson: the creditor's praise is the rarest coin in London, and she has just been paid in it.* — remembered: *the payment.*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — LAVINIA'S ADVICE. Rose decides what to do with the cynic's counsel. (Turns: 3 — the decision itself)
scenes.prose:
> Lavinia Crane received her in the little sitting room with the air of a woman who had been expecting exactly this visit, from exactly this girl, for exactly this reason.
> *(Afternoon. Lavinia Crane's lodgings. The cynic pours tea like she pours counsel — strong, bitter, and precisely measured.)*
> "You are spending your Season like a fortune, my dear, and the ton is letting you — because the ton loves nothing so much as watching a girl spend herself. So here is my advice, free and therefore worthless: stop spending. Hoard the dances. Marry the money. The Hartwell estate was rebuilt by men who understood that generosity is a luxury of the solvent — and you, my dear, are not yet solvent. You are *performing* solvency."
> Rose set down her cup. The advice was cynical, self-interested — and, she hated to admit, priced exactly like the truth.
> *★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — Lavinia's advice:*
> - **Take it** — *Cynic+, Lavinia trusted.* Rose hoards the dances, marries the money, and treats generosity as the luxury of the solvent. Lavinia becomes the season's quiet counselor — and the ton notices the new coldness, and prices it.
> - **Refuse it** — *Idealist+, Lavinia rebuffed.* Rose spends on, generous by contract and by choice; Lavinia withdraws, amused and disappointed — and the ton notices the warmth, and prices that too.

> After Laurent left, Rose did the measuring — the de Varenne bankers' trade, laid against the trail's facts.
> *(The campaign book, a fresh page: "de Varenne.")*
> Twenty years of discounting émigré notes. Every émigré house in London — the trade, as Laurent had said. Saint-Ange's notes, called in a week. The eleven's notes, bought for pennies, held for years. The London interests, directing the advances. The head, giving the order.
> (T1 · look closer) *She examines the overlap — the bankers' trade and the trail's facts, superimposed; the nearness, undeniable.* — remembered: *the overlap.*
> (T2 · stance) *She decides what the overlap does NOT prove — proximity is not complicity; hands are not the head.* — remembered: *the distinction.*
> "Hands," she said, writing it. "The bankers were the hands. The question is whether they knew whose hands they were."
> (T3 · choice — the possibilities:)*
> - **Knowing hands** — *Dark+.* The bankers knew the head, served it; the family, implicated.
> - **Used hands** — *Pale+.* The bankers served the trade, blind; the head used them as it used Rackham.
> (T4 · look closer) *She studies Laurent's fear — "the bankers fear the head more than the exposure"; fear of the head suggests knowledge of it.* — remembered: *the suggestion.*
> (T5 · stance) *She decides the fear is data — bankers do not fear abstractions; they fear men they have met.* — remembered: *the data.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *She writes both possibilities in the book — in pencil; the bankers, unjudged, for now.* — remembered: *the pencil.*
> (T7 · choice — the day's question:)*
> - **Warn Laurent** — *Protective+.* Tell him what the trail is finding; let him prepare his family.
> - **Investigate first** — *Thorough+.* Facts before warnings; the bankers, examined before they are alarmed.
> *(The pencil holds both possibilities. The book holds the overlap. And Rose Hartwell — who must decide what to do about the bankers, and about Laurent — puts the decision off until the facts are fuller, which is itself a kind of decision.)*

> *(The square, the nursemaids, the pigeons; the most un-ruined scene in England.)*
> Saint-Ange: ruined in a week, his notes called in concert. The eleven: harvested over six years, bought for pennies, held like a hand at a throat. Herself: the Hartwell debts, called in concert, the ruin engineered — Rackham's hands, the Network's head.
> (T1 · look closer) *She lays the three ruins side by side — the French week, the French harvest, the English season; the conducting, identical.* — remembered: *the conducting.*
> (T2 · stance) *She decides the identity is the point — not similar ruins, the same ruin; one kitchen, one recipe.* — remembered: *the recipe.*
> "The same ruin," she said aloud, and a pigeon startled. "French and English. The Network eats émigrés too."
> (T3 · choice — the meaning:)*
> - **The Network is indiscriminate** — *Cold+.* It eats whoever is on the table; no hatred, only appetite.
> - **The Network is systematic** — *Colder+.* The ruin is a method, applied; the table is set deliberately.
> (T4 · look closer) *She examines "systematic" — the scheduling, the harvesting, the conducting; a method needs a practitioner.* — remembered: *the practitioner.*
> (T5 · stance) *She decides the practitioner is the head — the de Valcourt interest, living; the method's author.* — remembered: *the author.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *She turns for home — the walk done, the pattern fixed; the afternoon's thinking, banked.* — remembered: *the banking.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She writes in the book, on the walk home, in pencil: "One kitchen."* — remembered: *the kitchen.*
> (T8 · choice — the evening:)*
> - **Augusta** — *Counsel+.* The Dowager, the French kin; the pattern, laid before the wisest woman she knows.
> - **The notes** — *Work+.* The eleven, again; the pattern, tested against the paper.
> *(She chooses Augusta. The note goes — "I need your French memory, Grandmama. Tomorrow." — and the pattern walks home with her, fixed and filed: one kitchen, one recipe, the same ruin in two languages.)*

Investigate them — the bankers' books, the discounting records, the Saint-Ange week, examined before anyone is alarmed; the thorough road, and the slow one. Keep him out of it — spare Laurent the knowledge, spare the family the fear, walk the trail alone where the de Varennes are concerned; the kind road, and the lonely one.

> (T2 · stance) *She weighs investigating — thoroughness against time; the trail will not wait for perfect facts.* — remembered: *the investigating, weighed.*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — LAURENT'S BANKERS. Warn him, investigate them, or keep him out of it. (Turns: 3 — the decision itself)
scenes.prose:
> "The de Varenne bankers," Rose said aloud, to the empty room. "Twenty years of émigré notes. Near the trail — how near, I do not yet know."
> The lamp burned. The book lay open to the pencil's two possibilities — knowing hands, used hands. Laurent's crack, unpolished, in her memory. The family's "be careful," gentle and absolute.
> Three roads. And the trail would not wait.
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — Laurent's bankers:*
- **Warn him** — *Laurent+, trusted.* Tell him everything the trail has found; let him prepare his family. Honest — and the bankers, warned, may hide what the trail needs.
- **Investigate them** — *Information+, thorough.* The bankers' books, the discounting records, examined before anyone is alarmed. Thorough — and slow, and Laurent unwarned in the meantime.
- **Keep him out of it** — *Laurent+, sheltered.* Spare him the knowledge; walk the trail alone where his family is concerned. Kind — and lonely, and a little dishonest.
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the tone of the telling, or the silence; the words to Laurent, or the words withheld. The bankers' fate is the chapter's second seal.)*

scenes.synopsis: the decision — Bath; Augusta's French memory; where the notes' holders and the ruined families can be found, bought out, or turned. (Turns: 9)
scenes.prose:
> Augusta received her in the morning room at Ravencroft House — the Dowager's own ground, the light, the order, the spectacles.
> "Your French memory, Grandmama." Rose laid the precis's copy on the table. "The de Valcourt papers. A dead financier's files. I need you to read the names the way only you can."
> Augusta read. The spectacles came down. The silence lengthened — the particular silence of a woman encountering a name she knows.
> (T1 · look closer) *Rose watches the silence — the Dowager knows the de Valcourt banking branch; the kinship, kept light, flickers.* — remembered: *the flicker.*
> "The banking branch," Augusta said at last. "Distant kin — very distant — of my French family. They fell, in the nineties. The details — " She removed the spectacles. "The details were never told to me. A branch falls; one does not ask the tree for particulars."
> (T2 · stance) *Rose decides not to press — the kinship is light, and Augusta's "never told" is a door, not a wall; some doors open later.* — remembered: *the door, noted.*
> "And the notes?" Rose asked. "The holders — the ruined — where are they, Grandmama? The eleven are paper. I need the people."
> "Bath." Augusta said it without hesitation. "The ruined go to Bath, child. It is what Bath is for — the waters, the cheap lodgings, the company of the equally diminished. The notes' holders — Trelawney and Sons, among others. All of them, in one town, taking the waters."
> (T3 · look closer) *Rose examines "taking the waters" — the whole of the trail's human material, in one spa town.* — remembered: *the town, the quarry.*
> (T4 · choice — the strategy:)*
> - **Buy them out** — *Money+.* The notes' holders, purchased; the paper, gathered.
> - **Turn them** — *Intrigue+.* The carriers, the ruined; witnesses, made.
> - **Both** — *General+.* Bought or turned, as each requires; the town, worked.
> "Both," Augusta said, reading her face. "You were going to say both. Good." The Dowager leaned forward. "And hear me, child — Bath is not London. In London you are the Hartwell heiress, watched. In Bath you can be — " she smiled, thinly — "whoever the waters require."
> (T5 · stance) *Rose takes the counsel — the second self, authorized by the Dowager.* — remembered: *the authorization.*
> (T6 · tone) *She chooses how to ask the last question — about the living interest.*
> - **Directly** — *Bold+.* "Is there a living de Valcourt, Grandmama? In London?"
> - **Lightly** — *Careful+.* "The precis speaks of a living interest. Do the gossips name one?"
> "The gossips," Augusta said, "name no one. Which, in London, means everyone is afraid to." She stood — the audience, ending. "Go to Bath, child. Find the holders. Turn the ruined. And mind Drummond's leash — it is long, but it is a leash."
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She writes in the book: "Bath — the holders, the ruined, the carriers. Buy or turn."* — remembered: *the orders.*
> (T8 · stance) *She names it — the decision is Bath; the chapter's first seal, awaiting only the formal choosing.* — remembered: *the naming.*
> *(The audience ends. The precis is gathered. And Rose Hartwell walks out of Ravencroft House with the war's destination named: Bath.)*

> *(System: the occasion brief is published.)*

> **Occasion brief — A Farewell London Dinner**
> *The last London evening before the Bath road — a dinner, the ton's farewell, every eye that matters in the room. The brief is leave them wanting more: evening dress for a woman departing at the height of her powers, to be remembered in her absence. Editorial criterion — every choice is judged on luminous restraint: shine, but softly; the room should feel her going, not her glittering. Pastels carry the thesis — blush, lavender, butter — the palette of a promise, not a triumph.*
>
> Rose reads the brief twice, and lays out three directions on the table:
>
> **A. The Blush Farewell** — blush silk, luminous and warm; the promise of return, worn.
> **B. The Lavender Leave-Taking** — lavender crape, cool and haunting; absence, made beautiful.
> **C. The Butter Departure** — butter-yellow sarsenet, light as morning; the road ahead, gilded.
>

ritual.occasionBrief: A Farewell London Dinner. The last London evening before the Bath road — a dinner, the ton's farewell, every eye that matters in the room. The brief is leave them wanting more: evening dress for a woman departing at the height of her powers, to be remembered in her absence. Editorial criterion — every choice is judged on luminous restraint: shine, but softly; the room should feel her going, not her glittering. Pastels carry the thesis — blush, lavender, butter — the palette of a promise, not a triumph.

scenes.prose:
> The morning after the farewell dinner, Rose woke to rain on the area windows and the smell of Letitia's determination, which was lavender water and a briskness that preceded lists the way thunder precedes rain.
> "Bath," Letitia said, without preamble, setting the breakfast tray, "is decided. The banker is named. The road is decided. Everything is decided except the order of things, which is precisely the part that matters, and the order is this." She sat, poured, and fixed Rose with the look she reserved for battle plans. "The ball comes first. Lady Agatha Drummond's autumn ball — Thursday. Half the ton already dresses for it, and the other half is having its hair done in anticipation. And you, my love, will pay the first installment of her price under those chandeliers, in front of everyone, before you so much as pack a trunk for Somerset."
> Rose poured the tea. "You do not leave London owing the dragon a public debt," Letitia continued. "You pay it where she can count it. In daylight. In silk. With witnesses."
> "And Honoria?"
> "Honoria will be launched at that ball like a ship — by you, publicly, with your name on the bottle and your hand on her arm." Letitia buttered her toast with unusual vigor. "Drummond means the ton to watch you spend. Very well. We shall give them something worth watching — something they will talk about until Christmas."

scenes.prose:
> The card arrived with the second post, on the same heavy paper as the summons had been — and like the summons, it wasted no courtesy on softness, and no ink on explanation.
> *Lady Agatha Drummond's ball, Thursday. Miss Honoria Drummond will be presented to the ton by Miss Hartwell. The carriage at eight.*
> "Eight," Letitia said faintly, reading over Rose's shoulder. "She sends the carriage — the black crested carriage, at eight, when the street will be full."
> "A compliment?" Rose asked, though she knew the answer.
> "A chain. A gilded one, but a chain." Letitia set the card down as though it were warm to the touch. "Arriving in Drummond's carriage announces the arrangement before you so much as cross the threshold. Everyone will know, before the first dance, that Miss Hartwell is the dragon's instrument — and that Miss Honoria Drummond is the dragon's niece, and that the Hartwell name has been spent to buy her a Season. There will be no mistaking it. That is the point. There is to be no mistaking it."
> Rose turned the card over. Nothing on the back. Of course nothing on the back. Drummond never explained herself twice, and rarely once.
> "Then we shall not mistake it either," Rose said. "We shall arrive in her carriage, at eight, and we shall make the arrival worth the announcing."

> Honoria arrived at eleven, in a grey carriage with Drummond's crest, looking like a girl being led to a charming execution: neat, pale, resigned.
> "Miss Hartwell." The curtsy was too deep again — the practice showing, the way it shows in the terrified. "Aunt Agatha says Thursday. She says I am to be — to be *launched*. She used the naval word. I have been reading about ships. They are christened with wine, and sometimes they sink, and the wine is wasted."
> "You will not sink," Rose said, and took both the girl's hands, which were cold as river stones. "Sit. We are going to do what navies do before a launching. We are going to inspect the hull — plank by plank, fear by fear — until there is nothing left unexamined."
> "The hull?" Honoria sat, obedient and bewildered.
> "You." Rose poured the tea herself — no one, evidently, ever had. "Tell me the worst of Thursday, exactly as you picture it. Out loud. Fears lose half their teeth in daylight."
> Honoria's worst was comprehensive: the stammer, the wrong fork, a partner's laugh, her aunt's face like a judge. Rose listened, refilling the cup, and said: "Good. Now we take them one at a time, and fit each with a plank."

scenes.prose:
> Élise arrived at noon with her basket and the expression of a woman who had been waiting all season for permission to be magnificent.
> "The ball," Élise said. "The dragon's ball. The installment. And you will not buy a new gown for it."
> "Élise — " Rose began, amused and apprehensive in equal measure.
> "You will not *buy*," said Élise, with the finality of a judge passing sentence, "because buying would be the wrong sentence entirely. You are not a girl with a new fortune spending it in the shops. You are a house, restored, wearing its own restoration." She opened the basket — folded lengths of old silk, soft with years in a press. "The Hartwell stores. Silk old enough to have danced at your mother's wedding — better than anything in the shops, because it is *yours*."

> "Sit," Élise commanded, spreading the gold silk across the table. "Before I cut a thread, you must know what you are wearing. This is not cloth, *chérie*. This is evidence."
> The silk had come to Hartwell Park forty years ago — bought by Rose's grandfather in a year of good harvests, laid by for a daughter's wedding that never came, pressed with lavender, overlooked by every creditor. It had survived the whole engineered collapse — overlooked, like the house itself.
> "It survived the ruin because it was overlooked," Rose said slowly. "Like the house. Like — " She stopped, the parallel completing itself.
> "Like you, at the start of the season." Élise was remorseless, and right. "Yes. That is the sentence the gown will say, and the ton will hear it without being told. *Overlooked, not ruined. Kept, not spent. Old, and the better for it.* That is the brief, *chérie*. That is what Thursday wears."

scenes.synopsis: Merge-board texture — the standing order queue; the free-income engine turns beneath the masterwork.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: merge-board texture scene — the standing order queue. Orders wait, merge, and complete in the background; the atelier's patient arithmetic funds the season's coins.)*
> At the workroom that afternoon, the great order board had been cleared at its center for the masterwork — the gold silk pinned at the top like a proclamation, its card lettered in Élise's best hand — and around it the standing orders waited in their patient rows: a widow's mourning silk softening toward second mourning, a debutante's ball gown in its final fitting, two spencers, a riding habit, a christening robe for a grandchild not yet born and already, by all accounts, furious.
> Élise moved three pins along their stages with satisfaction. "The queue never empties, *chérie*. That is the point of it. While you are paying the dragon in ballrooms, the board is paying me in coin. The masterwork takes the center — but the edges keep turning. Thread into money, money into standing. It is the only honest alchemy in London, and I invented it."
> Rose watched a length of ivory — Honoria's Thursday silk — advance one stage toward a bodice, the girls' hands moving over it with the care they gave everything. Nothing wasted. Everything merged, mended, moved forward, the workroom's patient arithmetic answering the ballroom's extravagant sums.
> "Then keep it moving," she said. "We shall need every coin. The season is long, the creditors are patient, and the ton — " she smiled, a little grimly — "the ton is always hungry, and it dines out on other people's installments."

scenes.synopsis: Augusta's counsel — the ball as installment; the dragon's arithmetic, translated.
scenes.prose:
> Augusta received her at Ravencroft House with tea strong enough to stand a spoon in.
> "The ball," said the Dowager. "Agatha's. Thursday. You are to launch the niece — in her carriage, at eight, before the ton." She poured. "Sit. You look like a girl told to swallow a live fish. Chew, child. It is the only way."
> "She sends her carriage."
> "Of course she does. The carriage is the signature on the contract. Now listen. The first installment is not the sponsorship. The sponsorship is the *price*. The first installment is the *public payment* — the part the ton witnesses. Agatha needs the ton to *see* you launch her. The seeing is the installment. The witnessing is the payment."
> Rose frowned. "Then Thursday is theatre."
> "Thursday is *banking*," Augusta corrected. "Theatre is what the ton calls banking when it is done in a ballroom. Spend where every creditor can watch — and every creditor will conclude, correctly, that a house which can spend like that can pay. That is the dragon's arithmetic."

> ◇ **examine** — *Augusta's face, at "correctly"* — the Dowager's own creditors, long ago *(noted: Augusta has paid this price herself)*
> ◇ **choice** — *tone* — the pupil / the fellow banker *(remembered: Augusta's respect)*
