> ◇ **examine** — *the tea, too strong* — Augusta's nerves, showing *(noted: even the Dowager feels Thursday)*
> ◇ **choice** — *the parting* — a kiss on the cheek, un-English and entire *(remembered: Augusta+)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *"chew, child"* — the counsel, taken *(remembered: her Thursday stomach)*
> "One more thing," Augusta said at the door, holding her arm a moment. "When Agatha nods — and she will nod, child, she will not be able to help herself — do not smile. Accept it the way you would accept a receipt. It *is* a receipt. Smiling at a receipt suggests you did not expect to be able to pay."

scenes.synopsis: Letitia's ball strategy — the choreography of a public payment.
scenes.prose:
> That evening Letitia produced, with the gravity of a quartermaster issuing arms before a campaign, a sheet of paper covered in her neat, furious hand — the ink still fresh, the crossings-out evidence of serious thought.
> "The order of battle," she announced. "Eight o'clock — Drummond's carriage, which we accept with grace and arrive in with better grace. The anteroom — you present Honoria to the receiving line yourself; your hand on her arm, your voice carrying just far enough that the second rank hears it too. The first set — you dance its opening with Honoria's first partner, whoever he is, to show the room that the Hartwell endorsement is not ornamental. The second set — you give away. Yes, give. You will be seen giving your own dance to the wallflower's wallflower, and the ton will talk of nothing else for a week."
> "You have planned my generosity," Rose said, amused and touched in equal measure.
> "I have *scheduled* it," Letitia corrected, unrepentant. "Generosity unplanned is merely luck, and luck is not a strategy. Now — supper. You sit Honoria between the two most eligible men in the room who can be trusted not to laugh. I have made a list." She produced a second sheet. "It is short. Do not look at it and weep. I wept making it."
> Rose looked at the list. It was short. She did not weep — quite — but she understood, suddenly and completely, what the sponsorship cost in afternoons of thought: not just her dances, but Letitia's.
> ◇ **choice** — *her verdict on the plan* — brilliant / terrifying / both *(remembered: Letitia's confidence)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *the amendment she proposes* — Honoria's laugh, deployed deliberately *(remembered: the plan's best weapon)*
> ◇ **examine** — *the short list of trustworthy men* — shorter than hoped *(noted: the supper seating, a risk)*
> ◇ **choice** — *the dance she gives away* — the second set, as planned / the supper dance, bolder *(remembered: the Gazette's paragraph)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *the question* — and if Honoria falters? *(remembered: the rescue protocol — Rose's hand, the retiring room, no fuss)*
> ◇ **examine** — *Letitia's handwriting, furious* — love, in list form *(noted: the aunt's devotion)*
> ◇ **choice** — *the toast, with the last of the tea* — to the ship / to the bottle *(remembered: the private joke, carried to Thursday)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *the crossings-out, studied* — the thought behind the plan *(remembered: her trust in the strategy)*

scenes.synopsis: Julian — rebuilding, present; will he come Thursday?
scenes.prose:
> She found him in the library at dusk, bent over his brother's papers, squaring the edges as though order on the desk could order the accounts, the lamplight catching the mended gloves on the blotter.
> "The debts," he said, before she asked — he knew her step now, and her questions. "Nearly gathered. The tailor in Calais is paid — his French, in the receipt, was almost warm, which I take as a professional compliment. The man in Dieppe took his money with the air of a tragedian denied his final act. There remains — " he consulted a list, shorter than last time — "one note. Small. Held by a man who does not answer letters, which I choose to interpret as shyness rather than strategy."
> "And Thursday?" Rose asked. "Drummond's ball. Will you come?"
> He looked up, and the late charm arrived on time for once — and stayed, which was newer. "To watch you launch a wallflower in the dragon's carriage, wearing, no doubt, something that will make Bell reach for new adjectives and the ton reach for its smelling salts? Rose, I would not miss it if the bailiffs were at the door. Which, the debts being nearly gathered, they are not. I checked. Twice."
> "You are rebuilding," she said quietly. "In the open. Where everyone can see."
> "I am." He stacked the last paper with particular care. "It is slower than ruin. It is also, I find, better lit — and the company is superior."
> ◇ **choice** — *her answer to his lightness* — matching wit / quiet pride in him *(remembered: Julian+)*
> ◇ **examine** — *the list, shorter than last time* — one note remaining *(noted: the unanswered letters — a thread)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *the question, gently* — may I help with the last note? *(remembered: his refusal, or his acceptance — trust, tested)*
> ◇ **choice** — *tone about Thursday* — ask him to come early / let him choose his hour *(remembered: his Thursday arrival)*
> ◇ **examine** — *his hands on the papers* — steadier than last month *(noted: the rebuilding, real)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *a hand, briefly, on his* — the library, dusk, no witnesses needed *(remembered: the route's warmth)*
> ◇ **choice** — *the parting line* — "be there" / "I shall look for you" *(remembered: his Thursday post)*
> ◇ **examine** — *the mended gloves, laid aside* — retired, or merely resting *(noted: a detail for the lookbook)*

scenes.synopsis: The ask — Laurent dances with Honoria; the ask costs him, and he pays it.
scenes.prose:
> Laurent called the next morning, all polish, and Rose — who had rehearsed this twice, in front of the glass — made the ask before the tea was poured.
> "Thursday. Drummond's ball. I am launching her niece — Miss Honoria Drummond. Dull, deserving, terrified. I need a partner for her first set who will not laugh, will not condescend, and will make the room believe she is worth dancing with. I need *you*."
> The polish flickered — the briefest catch. "You ask me," he said carefully, "to dance the first set with a wallflower. At the dragon's ball. Before the ton."
> "I ask you," said Rose, "because you are the best dancer in London, and the room will read your attention as a verdict. If you dance with Honoria and are seen to enjoy it, she is launched. There is no one else I can ask."
> He was silent. The ask cost him — she could see it, the calculation running behind the polish: what it would cost him in the clubs, in his family's estimation, in the currency of being seen to enjoy a dull girl's company at the season's most watched ball. And then, slowly, he inclined his head — the continental bow, exact.
> "For you," he said, "I shall enjoy it. Or at the very least, I shall be seen to." A smile then, real this time, breaking through like sun. "Perhaps I shall surprise myself. Dull girls have surprised greater men than I. It is practically the history of France."
> ◇ **choice** — *how she asked* — bluntly, before tea / with full context *(remembered: Laurent's respect for the directness)*
> ◇ **examine** — *the flicker in the polish* — the cost, honestly seen *(noted: the ask's true price)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *the thanks* — a hand on his arm, unhurried *(remembered: Laurent+)*
> ◇ **choice** — *what she promises in return* — a dance / nothing; the ask is the bond *(remembered: the Thursday ledger between them)*
> ◇ **examine** — *his family's estimation, mentioned* — the de Varenne bankers, near the trail *(noted: the pressure, sharpening)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *the intelligence shared* — Honoria's laugh, her courage *(remembered: his Thursday kindness, armed)*
> ◇ **choice** — *the farewell* — "surprise yourself" / "I shall owe you" *(remembered: his Thursday manner)*
> ◇ **examine** — *"the history of France"* — the wit, recovered *(noted: the polish, intact)*

scenes.synopsis: The waltz question — she asks; the refusal protects her, and costs them both.
scenes.prose:
> The next afternoon brought a card that made Letitia go very still — Lord Frederick Ashcombe, requesting Miss Hartwell's company for a drive in the Park at four, when the serious people walked.
> She went — and found him by the Serpentine with the air of a man who had abandoned three speeches, which she recognized.
> "Thursday," he said, without preamble, falling into step beside her. "Drummond's ball. I shall not be there."
> Rose had been about to ask him to open the waltz — the words arranged in her mouth — and closed her mouth on them. "You — " she began.
> "I cannot dance with you, Rose. Not Thursday. Not in that ballroom, before that company, with Bell watching through her lorgnette and Agatha Drummond watching through everything." His voice was low, and raw at the edges in a way she had never heard it. "It would be — " he searched, and found the honest word — "conspicuous. And conspicuous, Thursday, would undo everything you are spending the evening to buy. The ton is already counting your dances. They must not count *ours*."
> She understood completely, which was the worst of it — the refusal was a kindness; dancing with Frederick would have turned the installment into gossip. It cost him; she could see it in his shoulders, in the way he would not meet her eyes.
> "Then you will come late," she said, "and stand where I can see you. And that will be our dance."
> ◇ **choice** — *her answer to the refusal* — grace / a flash of hurt, honestly shown *(remembered: Frederick+, and the hurt, remembered too)*
> ◇ **examine** — *his voice, raw at the edges* — the cost, honestly seen *(noted: the refusal's price)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *the counter-proposal* — come late, stand where she can see *(remembered: his Thursday post, fixed)*
> ◇ **choice** — *what she does not say* — the waltz ask, swallowed *(remembered: the unasked question, carried)*
> ◇ **examine** — *the Serpentine, at four* — the serious hour, the serious people *(noted: the walk's discretion)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *a hand on his arm, brief* — the Park, witnesses, propriety intact *(remembered: the route's ache)*
> ◇ **choice** — *the parting* — "Thursday, then" / "I shall look for you" *(remembered: his Thursday manner)*
> ◇ **examine** — *what Bell would have written* — the scandal, averted *(noted: the wisdom of the refusal)*

scenes.synopsis: Henry's counsel — Bath; the money trail; his steady hand on her shoulder, literal and otherwise.
scenes.prose:
> He came at dusk, as he always did — the dust of the day's business on his boots — and found her in the morning room with Letitia's battle plan spread like a general's map.
> "Thursday," he said, reading the sheet upside down with the ease of a man accustomed to reading dispatches. "The dragon's ball. The installment." He looked up. "And after — Bath. Trelawney & Sons."
> "You have heard."
> "I have *seen* the ledger." His voice dropped, and the steadiness in it was the steadiest thing in the room. "Rose. The Bath bank is older than London suspects, and deeper. The émigré notes in that counting-house were not the whole of it — they were the edge of it. When you go, go carefully. Bankers in Bath smile more than bankers in London, and mean it less."
> She told him, then, what she had not told Letitia — the fear underneath the battle plan, the small cold place where the courage ran thin: that the trail might lead nowhere, that the money might be gone past finding, that she might pay Drummond's price and still lose the house.
> He listened. And then he put his hand on her shoulder — the literal hand, warm through the muslin — and said: "Then we find what we find. And what we find, we use. You are not alone in this counting-house, Rose Hartwell. You have never been alone in it. You have only been the only one keeping the books."
> ◇ **choice** — *what she confesses* — the fear, entire / the fear, edged with defiance *(remembered: Henry's trust, deepened)*
> ◇ **examine** — *his hand on her shoulder* — the steadiness, literal *(noted: the route's anchor)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *the question* — will you write to Bath ahead of me? *(remembered: Henry's letters, preceding her)*
> ◇ **choice** — *tone* — the fellow campaigner / the girl, briefly *(remembered: Henry+)*
> ◇ **examine** — *"the only one keeping the books"* — the truth of it *(noted: her season's loneliness, named)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *the intelligence shared* — Letitia's battle plan, shown *(remembered: his Thursday counsel — "trust the plan")*
> ◇ **choice** — *the farewell* — a hand held a moment longer *(remembered: the dusk, the room, the steadiness)*
> ◇ **examine** — *the dust on his boots* — the day's business, wherever it took him *(noted: Henry's own campaign, running parallel)*

scenes.synopsis: Honoria's gown — three diegetic options, remembered; the sponsorship's visible half.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: [F] — 2–3 diegetic gown options; free, remembered, worn by Honoria Thursday.)*
> The fitting was Thursday's first business — Honoria arrived pale and punctual, and Élise laid out three silks on the morning-room table like evidence for a jury she meant to convince.
> "For the ship," Élise announced. "Three hulls. Choose."
> **A.** *The ivory silk, plain and luminous* — rosebuds embroidered tone-on-tone at the hem — ivory whitework, silver, gold, or polychrome silk; long ivory gloves, pearl drops, a thin gold chain, ivory hair ribbon, an ivory fan. Severe, honest: no disguise needed, and the ton will not know what to do with it.
> **B.** *The deep rose, softened with the forty-year-old lace* — the Hartwell lace the ornament, deep-pointed at neckline and hem, a rosebud edging beneath in gold, copper, or ivory whitework; lace-edged gloves, a gold locket, rose hair ribbon, a fan edged in that lace, a rose reticule. The girl is cherished, and cherished things are never dull.
> **C.** *The pale blue, caught with silver ribbon* — ribbon-work bands at waist and hem in silver, steel, or black silk thread, the neckline modest; a silver sash, pearl-and-silver earrings, blue hair ribbon, a blue fan, an ivory reticule. The girl is young, and youth, properly framed, is its own ornament.
> Honoria touched each in turn, her hands steadier than Tuesday. "The rose," she said quietly. "With the lace. If — if I am to be launched, I should like to be launched *cherished*."
> Élise smiled — the jury had returned the right verdict. "The rose with the lace. *Chérie*, the ship shall sail cherished."
> ◇ **choice** — *Rose's counsel on the choice* — endorses the rose (and the copper thread) / suggests the ivory's boldness *(remembered: Honoria's Thursday confidence)*
> ◇ **examine** — *Honoria's hands, steadier* — the coaching's work *(noted: the girl's growth)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *the lace's provenance, told* — forty years in the Hartwell press *(remembered: Honoria's awe — "your grandmother's lace")*
> ◇ **choice** — *the fitting's tone* — brisk efficiency / unhurried kindness *(remembered: the workroom's warmth)*
> ◇ **examine** — *Élise's jury metaphor* — enjoyed *(noted: the atelier's Thursday high spirits)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *a word to Honoria's maid* — the girl's hair, arranged *(remembered: the coiffure)*
> ◇ **choice** — *"launched cherished"* — the phrase, taken up *(remembered: the sponsorship's motto)*
> ◇ **examine** — *the rejected silks, folded away* — the ivory, the blue — for another ship, another Thursday *(noted: the atelier's stores)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — "How do we launch Honoria?" Launch her boldly (center stage) / launch her gently (shielded) / launch her as one of us (Hartwell's circle).
scenes.prose:
> ★ **KEY DECISION 1/3 — "How do we launch Honoria?"**
> Wednesday evening, Letitia laid out the question — Honoria present, per Rose's insistence, sitting very straight with her hands folded like a petitioner.
> "Three ways. **First** — we launch her *boldly*: you present her at the height of the arrivals, her name on the air like a toast. The risk — " she glanced at Honoria — "is the stammer, in the glare."
> "**Second** — *gently*: you present her in the lulls, and let the evening accumulate her acquaintances like a tide. The risk is invisibility — launched so gently the ton does not notice."
> "**Third** — " Letitia paused — "we launch her *as one of us*. She arrives with us, stands with us, is seen laughing with us. The ton reads belonging — the one currency that cannot be counterfeited."
> Honoria's hands had tightened in her lap. "I — " she began, and stopped, and looked at Rose with the expression of a girl who has been asked to choose her own christening.
> ◇ **choice** — *the decision* — **boldly** (center stage, the toast) / **gently** (the tide, the lulls) / **as one of us** (belonging, uncounterfeitable) *(remembered: the launch's means — the ton's reading, Honoria's trust, the Gazette's paragraph — all three pay the installment)*
> ◇ **examine** — *Honoria's face, at "choose"* — the girl's terror, and her courage beneath it *(noted: whichever way, she will try)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *the question she asks Honoria first* — what does the ship want? *(remembered: the girl's voice, consulted)*
> ◇ **choice** — *tone of the decision* — brisk command / collaborative counsel *(remembered: the room's feeling)*
> ◇ **examine** — *Letitia's "I have looked"* — the aunt's thoroughness, entire *(noted: no fourth way exists)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *the plan's details, assigned* — who stands where, who speaks when *(remembered: Thursday's choreography)*
> ◇ **choice** — *the reassurance to Honoria* — "we launch together" / "you are ready" *(remembered: the girl's eve-of-battle sleep)*
> ◇ **examine** — *the evening light in the morning room* — the eve of the ball, the quiet before *(noted: the chapter's turning point)*
> *(Decision locks: the launch's means. The installment is paid Thursday regardless — but the ton will remember* how *it was paid.)*

scenes.synopsis: Pre-ball nerves — the household rallies; Honoria arrives transformed.
scenes.prose:
> The house at seven was a campaign headquarters in the last hour before the battle — Letitia in full armor (the puce silk, the cameo like a general's star), the servants moving with the hushed efficiency of people who know the stakes, the air smelling of lavender water and hot irons and nerves.
> Honoria arrived at half past, in Drummond's grey carriage, and the girl who stepped down was not the girl of Tuesday's terror — the deep rose silk with the forty-year-old lace sat on her like confidence borrowed and already being repaid, her hair dressed in soft order, her hands — Rose checked — warm.
> "Well?" Honoria said, turning slowly, and there was a laugh underneath the question, the unguarded laugh from the fork-lesson, already deployed.
> "The ship," said Letitia, with the satisfaction of an admiral inspecting a fleet, "is seaworthy. More than seaworthy. Rose — " she turned, and her eyes were bright — "look at what the sponsorship has built. Not a wallflower, launched. A girl, *found*."
> Rose adjusted a fold of the rose silk, unneeded and necessary both. "Remember the plan," she said quietly. "The anteroom. My hand on your arm. The first set — Laurent. He will be kind; be kind back, and the room will do the rest."
> "And if I stammer?"
> "Then you stammer," said Rose, "and you smile, and you go on. The ton forgives a stammer in a girl it has decided to like. Tonight, we give them no choice but to like you."
> ◇ **choice** — *her inspection of Honoria* — the admiral / the sister *(remembered: the girl's Thursday nerve)*
> ◇ **examine** — *Honoria's hands, warm* — the terror, managed *(noted: the coaching's harvest)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *the last instruction* — Laurent's name, his kindness, her kindness back *(remembered: the first set's foundation)*
> ◇ **choice** — *tone with Letitia* — shared pride / shared nerves *(remembered: the household's unity)*
> ◇ **examine** — *Letitia's puce silk, the cameo* — the aunt's armor *(noted: the household's battle dress)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *the unneeded adjustment of the rose silk* — the gesture, maternal *(remembered: Honoria's devotion)*
> ◇ **choice** — *"no choice but to like you"* — the promise, and its boldness *(remembered: her Thursday audacity)*
> ◇ **examine** — *the house's smell — lavender, irons, nerves* — the campaign's perfume *(noted: the evening's texture)*

scenes.synopsis: The carriage — eight o'clock, the black crested carriage, the street full; the arrival.
scenes.prose:
> At eight, to the minute, the black crested carriage drew up — the horses' breath smoking in the cold air, the coachman's face impassive as a monument, the crest on the door catching the lamplight like a seal on a warrant.
> "It is larger than I remembered," Honoria whispered, staring at it. "Carriages should not be larger on the inside of an evening than they are in the morning. It is unnatural."
> "It is Drummond's," said Letitia, settling her skirts with the air of a woman boarding a ship of the line. "Everything of Drummond's is larger in the evening. It is the hour when her power is at full tide."
> They rode in silence through streets already full — the ton's carriages converging on the square like ships to a harbor, the pavements crowded with onlookers, the air sharp with cold and expectation. Rose watched Honoria's face in the lamplight — pale, composed, the rose silk glowing against the carriage's dark interior like a lantern — and thought: *the ship is under way. There is no recalling her now. There was never any recalling her. That was the price, and the point.*
> The carriage turned into the square. The house blazed — every window lit, the steps crowded, the doors open like a mouth about to speak. The coachman descended. The door opened. The night air came in, cold and bright and smelling of rain and horses and perfume.
> "Together," Rose said, and took Honoria's hand, and stepped down into the light.
> ◇ **choice** — *her step from the carriage* — measured grace / bright defiance *(remembered: the Gazette's first line)*
> ◇ **examine** — *the crest on the door, lamplit* — the seal on the warrant *(noted: the arrangement, announced)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *Honoria's hand, taken* — the gesture, public *(remembered: the sponsorship, visible)*
> ◇ **choice** — *her face for the onlookers* — serene / quietly triumphant *(remembered: the crowd's reading)*
> ◇ **examine** — *the blazing house* — every window lit *(noted: the dragon's theatre)*
> ◇ **maneuver** — *Letitia's skirts, settled* — the aunt's boarding *(remembered: the household's unity)*
> ◇ **choice** — *"together"* — the word, said aloud *(remembered: Honoria's courage, anchored)*
> ◇ **examine** — *the night air — rain, horses, perfume* — the evening's first breath *(noted: the ball's overture)*

scenes.synopsis: The first set — Laurent dances with Honoria; the ask, honored; the room, convinced.
scenes.prose:
> The first set formed, and Laurent — true to his word, to the cost he had counted and paid — crossed the floor to Honoria with the continental bow, exact, and offered his hand as though she were the belle of the ballroom and he the fortunate one.
> "Miss Drummond," he said, "I believe this set is ours. I warn you — I am a demanding partner. I expect to be *amused*."
> Honoria — bless the girl, bless the fork-lessons and the hull-inspections and the rose silk with the forty-year-old lace — laughed. The unguarded laugh, deployed exactly as planned, bright and genuine and entirely unwallflower-like. "Then I shall do my best, Monsieur le Comte. Though I warn you in return — I am a demanding partner too. I expect not to be dropped."
> "A hard bargain," said Laurent, with the air of a man reconsidering his entire evening's expectations, "but I accept." And he led her out, and the room — Rose watched it happen, watched the recalculation ripple outward like rings from a stone — *watched*. Laurent de Varenne, the best dancer in London, dancing with Honoria Drummond, and — this was the miracle, or the acting, or both — *seen to enjoy it*.

scenes.synopsis: Cecilia at the ball's edge — watching, pale; the thread tightens before it vanishes.
scenes.prose:
> She found Cecilia at the ball's edge — not dancing, not conversing, standing by a pillar with a glass of negus going warm in her hand and the look of a girl watching a play whose ending she already knows and dreads.
> "Cecilia." Rose crossed to her, Letitia's plan permitting this one deviation — some threads could not wait for choreography. "You are not dancing."
> "No." Cecilia's smile was a thin, bright thing, stretched over something else. "I find I am — tired, this evening. Of the dancing. Of the — " she gestured, vaguely, at the glittering room — "of all of it. You are magnificent, by the way. The gold. The *old* gold. Bell will have to invent a new verdict, and I almost pity her the effort. Almost."
> "Cecilia — " Rose began, and then stopped, because the girl's hand was shaking — the negus trembling in the glass, the thin bright smile trembling with it. "Are you unwell?"
> "Unwell?" Cecilia laughed — a sound like glass tapped too hard. "No. No, I am — " She looked across the room, toward the doors, toward the night beyond them. "I am *expected* — somewhere. Elsewhere. Soon." She set down the glass, untouched. "Enjoy the ball, Rose. Enjoy being — " the smile stretched thinner — "*seen*. It is a luxury. One does not always appreciate it until — " She did not finish. She curtsied, a quick uncertain dip, and was gone into the crowd before Rose could follow — swallowed by the glitter, the music, the three hundred recalculating guests.

scenes.prose:
> Supper was served at midnight in the long gallery — the tables groaning, the chandeliers doubled in the mirrors, the whole ton converging with the purposeful air of people who had danced up an appetite and intended to do justice to the dragon's kitchen.
> Letitia's seating plan held. Honoria sat between the two trustworthy men — the elder a widowed baronet with kind eyes and a stammer of his own (Letitia's genius: the girl would never fear a stammer in his company), the younger a guardsman with more honor than conversation — and Rose, watching from three places down, saw the girl *manage*: the soup taken without incident, the fish fork identified by the baronet with a conspiratorial whisper, the laugh — the unguarded laugh — deployed at exactly the right moment over exactly the right nothing.
> "She is doing it," Letitia murmured, behind her fan. "Look at her. She is *doing* it."
> "She is," said Rose, and felt something in her chest loosen that had been tight since Tuesday — the sponsor's fear, the specific dread of having promised a launching and produced a sinking. "The ship is not merely afloat, Aunt. The ship is *racing*."

scenes.prose:
> The supper dance found her, as supper dances do, in the crush between the gallery and the ballroom — and Henry was there, as he had said he would be, steady as a landmark, his hand extended with the particular gravity of a man who does not offer dances lightly.
> "Miss Hartwell," he said, formal before the company, and then — quieter, for her alone — "you are doing it. The whole room knows it. *She* knows it." A glance, barely perceptible, toward the dragon's end of the room.
> They danced. And it was — Rose thought, moving through the figures with the steadiness beside her like a wall to lean on without leaning — the easiest dance of the evening: no performance in it, no calculation, only the particular comfort of a partner who asks nothing and offers everything, whose hand at her back was the same hand that had been on her shoulder at dusk.
> "Bath," he said, in a quiet figure that brought them close. "When you go — write. Not the intelligence. *You*. The road, the rooms, the rain. I shall want to know the rain."

scenes.synopsis: The nod, absorbed — the installment paid; the household's triumph, quiet.
scenes.prose:
> "She nodded," Letitia whispered, in the retiring room, with the dazed air of a woman who has witnessed a natural phenomenon — a comet, a coronation, a dragon's approval. "Rose. She *nodded*. Twice in one evening — the anteroom, and now the alcove. I have seen Agatha Drummond nod twice in one evening exactly — " she counted on her fingers, a brief, glorious arithmetic — "never. Never in forty years."
> "It is a receipt," Rose said, sitting — her knees had, unaccountably, gone a little uncertain, now that the evening's weight was lifting. "Augusta said to accept it like a receipt. I accepted it like a receipt."
> "You accepted it like a *banker*," Letitia corrected, pressing a glass of negus into her hands with the air of a nurse administering medicine. "Drink. You are pale. Triumph pales people; it is the exertion leaving the body all at once. I have seen it after weddings and wars."
> Rose drank. The negus was warm and sweet and entirely restorative. Through the retiring-room door came the music — another set forming, the ball rolling on without them, the ton's evening continuing on the capital she had just spent.
> "The first installment," Letitia said softly, "is paid."
> "The first installment is paid," Rose agreed. And then, quieter: "Aunt — the second. Held. Unnamed. What does she want?"
> Letitia was silent for a moment — a rare thing. "I do not know," she said at last, honestly. "But I know this: whatever it is, you will pay it the way you paid this one. In daylight. In silk. With witnesses. It is your way now. The ton has seen it. *She* has seen it."

scenes.prose:
> He found her after the retiring room — Julian, materializing at her elbow with the particular ease of a man who has been watching for his moment, and offering his arm with a bow that was half-mockery and half the real thing.
> "The waltz," he said. "I am told — by sources I shall not name, who wept making a list — that the supper dance was given away, and that a certain set remains unclaimed. I claim it. Unless," he added, with the late charm arriving exactly on time, "you have promised it to the chandelier."
> "The chandelier," said Rose, taking his arm, "has been very understanding. But it will have to wait."
> They danced — and it was the waltz Frederick had refused, danced with the man who asked instead of declining, and Rose felt the difference in her bones: not the ache of the unasked question, but the warmth of the asked-and-answered, the particular pleasure of a partner who *wanted* the dance and said so.
> "You are rebuilding," she said, in a turn that brought them close — the library at dusk, the debts nearly gathered, the mended gloves laid aside. "In the open. Where everyone can see."
> "I am," he said. "And you — " a turn, the chandeliers blurring — "you are *restoring*. In the open. Where everyone can see. It is the same verb, Rose. We are conjugating it together."

scenes.synopsis: The dragon's favor — a public word; the installment's seal.
scenes.prose:
> It came near one o'clock — the hour when balls begin to thin at the edges and the real business of the evening gets done in the thinning: Lady Agatha Drummond, rising again, and this time speaking — not in an alcove, not in private, but *across the room*, her voice carrying with the particular authority of a woman whose lightest remark is treated as policy.
> "Miss Hartwell," said the dragon, "has done my family a service." A pause — the room, thinning, *listening*. "The ton has seen what the Hartwell name, spent well, can build. I am — " the slightest pause, the weight of forty years in it — "satisfied."
> *Satisfied.* The word went around the room like a toast. Bell's pencil — Rose could see it, across the floor — was moving furiously.
> Rose curtsied — exact, unhurried, the old gold silk catching the candlelight — and said, clearly: "Lady Agatha honors me. And Miss Drummond — " a glance to Honoria, shining in her rose and lace — "honors us all."
> The applause — for there was applause, scattered and then general, the ton's rare and genuine kind — was like rain after a drought. And the dragon, having spoken, sat down again, having sealed the installment with the only seal that mattered: her public word.

scenes.synopsis: Honoria's triumph — the ship, come into harbor; the sponsorship's human half.
scenes.prose:
> She found Honoria in the anteroom afterward — the girl surrounded, *surrounded*, by a ring of admirers three deep: the guardsman, the baronet, two debutantes who had decided, with the sudden unanimity of the young, that Miss Honoria Drummond was the evening's discovery.
> "Miss Hartwell!" Honoria broke through them like a ship through a light sea, and seized Rose's hands — warm, steady, entirely transformed. "Did you *see*? The Comte — he *enjoyed* it, truly, I could tell — and the baronet knew about the fish fork, and — " she stopped, breathless, shining. "I did not stammer. Not once. Not *once*, Rose."
> "I know," said Rose. "I was watching. The whole room was watching. That was rather the point."
> "The ship," Honoria said solemnly, and then — the unguarded laugh, bright as a bell — "the ship has come into harbor, and the harbor is *applauding*." She sobered, suddenly, the laughter giving way to something deeper. "Thank you. Not for the ball. For — " she gestured, vaguely, at herself — the rose silk, the steady hands, the shining — "for *this*. For the hull-inspection. For the tea you poured yourself. For — everything."
> Rose embraced her — quickly, fiercely, before the ton could see and make a paragraph of it. "You did it," she said. "The sponsorship built the occasion. *You* built the girl."

> The black crested carriage brought them home at two — the streets empty now, the rain returned, the horses' breath smoking in the lamplight, the whole of London asleep except the ball-goers rattling home with their triumphs and their slippers in their hands.
> "Count it," Letitia said, in the carriage's dark, with the air of a quartermaster after a campaign. "The anteroom — the nod. The first set — Laurent, enjoying it. Supper — the baronet, the fish fork. The alcove — the second installment, held, unnamed, and *answered*. The dragon's word — *satisfied*, before the ton." She ticked them on her fingers. "Five. Five receipts. Rose — " her voice caught, just slightly — "it is paid. The first installment is *paid*."
> Rose leaned her head against the carriage's dark velvet and watched the lamplit streets go by — the old gold silk folded around her like the evening itself, the press-marks steamed into softness, the forty years worn and vindicated.
> "It is paid," she agreed. "And Aunt — " she turned, in the dark — "thank you. For the battle plan. For the list that made you weep. For — everything."

scenes.synopsis: The sting, verbatim — restoration as fashion; the ton has no verdict, yet.
scenes.prose:
> The Gazette arrived with the morning post — and Bell, Rose thought, reading it over Letitia's shoulder with the toast going cold in her hand, had outdone herself. The paragraph was the talk of the breakfast tables before the breakfast things were cleared:
> *"Miss Hartwell wore her house's old silk, remade. Restoration, as fashion. The ton has no verdict for that — yet."*
> "Yet," Letitia said, with the air of a woman tasting a fine wine. "*Yet*. She does not know what to do with you, Rose. Bell — the great Bell, the proprietor, the judge — does not know what verdict fits a girl who wears her grandmother's silk to the dragon's ball and is *applauded* for it. The old verdicts were made for new gowns. You have broken her taxonomy."
> "I have broken nothing," said Rose, but she was smiling — the tired, triumphant smile of the morning after. "I have only — worn the house. The house did the rest."
> "The house," Letitia agreed, "and the girl who knew to wear it." She folded the paper with ceremony. "This one we keep. The lookbook — the archive — this paragraph goes in, lettered, like the silk's provenance. *Restoration, as fashion.* It is the season's sentence, Rose. It is what Thursday *meant*."

scenes.synopsis: The morning after — Bath preparations resume; the road, waiting.
scenes.prose:
> Friday morning. The ball's glitter had settled into memory, the old gold gown hung in the press with its story lettered on the card, and the house — with the particular resilience of households that have survived worse than triumphs — turned its face toward Bath.
> "The trunks," Letitia announced, with the air of a woman opening a second campaign on the heels of the first. "Trelawney & Sons. The banker. The émigré notes." She produced a list — shorter than the battle plan, but with the same furious hand. "We leave Monday. The lodgings — I have written. The letters of introduction — Augusta is providing. The road — " she paused, and her face changed, just slightly — "the road, Rose. We have paid the dragon. Now we pay the *road*."
> Rose stood at the window, looking out at the London street — the ordinary Friday street, the costers crying, the rain washed clean — and thought of the counting-house in Bath, the ledgers, the faded continental hands, the whole unmapped country waiting west.
> "Monday," she said. "The road." And felt — underneath the triumph, underneath the five receipts and the dragon's *satisfied* — the old pull: the money trail, the house's ruin, the question underneath every question. *Where did it go? Who moved it? And who is moving it still?*

scenes.prose:
> The note arrived with the afternoon post — no crest, no seal, only Frederick's hand, hurried and unhurried both:
> *I came late, as instructed. I stood where you could see — the pillar by the long windows, behind the palm. I saw the anteroom. I saw the first set. I saw the alcove, and the nod, and the dragon's* satisfied. *You were — there is no word but the true one — magnificent. The old gold. The old house. The new girl. Forgive the waltz. It was the only gift I could give you Thursday: my absence from your card. — F.*
> Rose read it twice. And then a third time, standing at the morning-room window with the Friday light going gold on the street, and felt the ache and the warmth together — the unasked question, and the answer it had received: *he had come. He had stood where she could see. He had given her the only gift he could.*

> Saturday's post brought Honoria's letter — the girl's hand, round and careful, the paper scented faintly with the rose silk's lavender:
> *Dear Miss Hartwell — Rose — May I call you Rose? Aunt Agatha says I may, having been launched, which is apparently a condition of harbors. I have had three callers. THREE. The baronet brought his sister. The guardsman brought flowers — carnations, which mean* fascination, *I looked it up. I did not stammer. Not once, all evening, and only twice since, both times at Aunt Agatha, which does not count as it is a medical condition. Thank you for the hull. Thank you for the tea. Thank you for the lace — forty years kept, and now* worn. *I shall keep it all my life. — Your ship, Honoria.*
> Rose laughed — out loud, in the morning room, to Letitia's delight — and then, unexpectedly, felt her eyes sting. *Three callers. Carnations. Fascination.* The sponsorship had built the occasion. The girl had built the rest.

scenes.prose:
> Élise arrived Saturday afternoon with champagne — actual champagne, which she produced from her basket with the air of a conjurer, and two glasses, which she produced with the air of a woman who had planned this for weeks.
> "To the Hartwell silk," she announced, pouring with ceremony. "To the forty years. To the ton, which has no verdict — *yet*." She raised her glass. "And to *you*, *chérie* — who wore the house, and let the house do the rest."
> They drank. The champagne was cold and bright and entirely deserved.
> "The orders," Élise said, refilling, "are *tripled*. Since Thursday. Three new commissions — all of them asking, in various degrees of discretion, for *old* silk. Remade. Restored. *Chérie*, you have started a fashion. Restoration — as fashion. Bell named it, but *you* did it." She leaned forward, her eyes bright. "The workroom is calling it *the Hartwell*. The masterwork. The season's first signature. It is in the order book, lettered, like a christening."
> Rose turned her glass slowly. "The Hartwell," she repeated. "The season's first signature."
> "The first," Élise agreed, "of many. The road now — Bath. The banker. The money trail." She raised her glass again. "And when you come back, *chérie* — we shall make the second signature. And the ton will *still* have no verdict. It will take them the whole season to catch up. By which time — " her smile was sharp as a pin — "we shall be three signatures ahead."

scenes.synopsis: Augusta's farewell counsel — Bath; the letters of introduction; the Dowager's blessing.
scenes.prose:
> Sunday. Ravencroft House. Augusta received her in the small parlor — the intimate room, the honor of it not lost on Rose — and pressed into her hands a packet of letters, sealed with the Ravencroft arms.
> "Introductions," said the Dowager. "Bath. Three houses — the right three. The kind that know bankers and invite them to dinner, which is the only way bankers are ever truly known." She held Rose's hands a moment, the packet between them. "And one more thing — not a letter. Counsel. The Bath bank — Trelawney & Sons — is older than London suspects. The émigré notes were the edge. The middle — " she paused — "the middle is where the money went, child. And the middle is guarded by men who smile."
> "Henry said the same," Rose said quietly. "About the smiling."
> "Henry is right. Henry is *always* right, which is his most irritating quality and his most valuable." Augusta's eyes were bright — not with tears; Augusta did not weep; with something fiercer. "Go carefully. Go *brilliantly* — you have the silk for it, you have the verdict for it, you have the *way* for it now. Daylight. Silk. Witnesses. It works on bankers as well as dragons. I have tested it. Extensively."

> ★ **KEY DECISION 3/3 — "What do we do about Cecilia's disappearance?"**

> "Gone," Letitia said flatly. "Since Thursday. The pillar, the negus, the *expected — somewhere. Elsewhere. Soon*." She looked at Rose. "We leave for Bath in the morning. The trunks are packed. The banker waits. And Cecilia — " she spread her hands — "Cecilia is *gone*."
> The room was very quiet. The rain had returned, soft on the area windows. scenes.synopsis: The Trelawney letter — the banker will see her; the road, confirmed.
scenes.prose:
> The letter arrived with the last post Sunday — the Bath postmark, the unfamiliar hand, the seal she did not recognize: *Trelawney & Sons, Bath.*
> Rose broke it with hands that were not quite steady — Letitia watching, the trunk straps forgotten — and read:
> *Miss Hartwell — Your letter of introduction, forwarded by the Dowager Marchioness of Ravencroft, has been received. Mr. Trelawney will see you. Thursday next, at the counting-house, at eleven of the clock. The matter of the émigré notes — and the older matter — may be discussed. — J. Trelawney, for Trelawney & Sons.*
> "Thursday next," Letitia breathed. "Eleven of the clock. The *older matter*." She looked up, her eyes bright. "Rose. He names it. *The older matter.* The middle — Augusta's middle, the guarded middle — he is willing to *discuss* it."
> Rose read the letter again — *will see you, may be discussed* — the banker's careful language, the door opening by exactly the width of a ledger. And felt the road — the real road, the Monday road, the westward road — settle under her like a ship settling into water.
> "Monday," she said. "We go Monday. And Thursday next — " she folded the letter with care — "Thursday next, at eleven of the clock, the counting-house. The older matter. *May be discussed*." A smile then — the campaigner's smile, the books-keeper's. "We shall discuss it, Aunt. Oh, we shall *discuss* it."

> Sunday night. The house was quiet — the trunks corded in the hall, the Bath letters in the writing case, the old gold gown in the press with its story lettered, Honoria's letter in the archive, Frederick's note folded small — and Rose walked through the rooms with a candle, the way she had walked them at the season's start, checking: the windows, the doors, the small certainties.

> "Thinking." Rose set down the candle. "Thursday — the installment. Paid. The dragon — *satisfied*. Honoria — launched, applauded, *fascinated* over. The silk — *the Hartwell*, the season's first signature." She ticked them, like Letitia's receipts. "And then — Cecilia, gone. The road, Monday. Trelawney, Thursday next. The older matter." She looked up. "It is a great deal, Aunt. For one chapter."
> "It is a great deal," Letitia agreed, sitting beside her, "for one *girl*. But you are not one girl, my love. You are a house. Houses contain multitudes." She took Rose's hand. "Sleep. The road will keep. It has kept for forty years — the silk proves it. It will keep one night more."

scenes.synopsis: The night thought — restoration, as fashion; the season's sentence, owned.
scenes.prose:
> She did not sleep — not at once. She lay in the dark and thought: of the gold silk, forty years pressed, worn into the dragon's ballroom; of Bell's paragraph — *restoration, as fashion; the ton has no verdict for that, yet*; of Honoria's laugh, bright as a bell; of Frederick's note — *it was our dance*; of Henry's hand on her shoulder — *you have never been alone in it*; of Julian's *conjugating it together*; of Laurent's bow, exact, and the cost he had paid with grace.
> And of Cecilia — the pillar, the negus going warm, *expected — somewhere. Elsewhere. Soon* — gone, the lease surrendered, the direction none. The thread underneath every thread. The question that would keep.
> *Restoration, as fashion.* The season's sentence. But lying in the dark, Rose understood what Bell had not yet understood — what the ton, with its no-verdict-yet, had not yet grasped: that restoration was not the fashion. Restoration was the *fact*. The fashion was merely how the fact had chosen to dress for the ball. The house had never been ruined. Only resting. Only waiting. Only kept. And now — now it was *awake*.
> *Monday, the road. Thursday next, Trelawney. The older matter. May be discussed. We shall discuss it.*

> "I walked," she announced, falling into step beside Rose for the last hundred yards to the carriage. "Do not look at me like that. I am a married woman of unimpeachable standing, walking one hundred yards on a public street at dawn. The scandal will be *enormous*. I shall dine out on it for weeks."
> Rose laughed — and then, suddenly, did not want to laugh at all. Octavia — who had been the season's first real friend, the one who had seen through the ruin to the girl underneath, who had held her hand through the dragon's summons and the ball's glitter — Octavia, staying in London, while she went west into the unknown.
> "Write," Octavia said, fiercely, at the carriage door. "Not the Gazette's Rose. *You*. The road, the rooms, the rain — Henry's rain, I know about the rain, he told me — the banker, the waters, all of it. I shall be your London. Someone must keep your London for you while you're gone."

> "I will keep it *brilliantly*," Octavia corrected. "Now go. Bath awaits. The waters taste of iron. The bankers smile. And you — " she stepped back, her eyes bright — "you are *ready*."

> At the carriage door, with the horses stamping and Letitia tactfully inspecting a strap for the seventh time, Octavia held Rose's hands and asked the question the whole season of sittings had been circling: "The sittings — all spring, my studio, your face — what *were* they, Rose? Before you go west, name it. I would rather have the true name than the pretty one."
> Rose had not expected the question — and then, suddenly, could not imagine the parting without it. The sittings: the long afternoons, the watching, the being-watched, Octavia seeing through the ruin to the girl underneath and putting it — all of it — into paint.
> "Three names," Rose said — she had learned that from her aunt. "**First** — a *romance*. Not the ton's romance — the heart's. The season's one true love story, whatever the world would call it. You saw me, and I — " she stopped — "I let myself be seen."
> "**Second** — a *friendship*. The deepest kind. No more, no less — the name the world would believe, and the world would be right."
> "**Third** — " Rose paused — "we leave it *unnamed*. No word at all. The sittings were what they were; the farewell is what it is. Some things — " she smiled — "some things are truer without a name."
> Octavia's eyes were very bright. "Romance," she said slowly, "friendship — or the unnamed."
> "Whatever it was," said Rose, "you are my London. Name, or no name."

scenes.synopsis: Élise's farewell — the packing; "flattering invisibility" as a commission.
scenes.prose:
> Élise came to the carriage at the last moment — breathless, triumphant, bearing a bandbox like an offering and a packet of letters like a weapon.
> "The Bath commission," she announced, pressing the bandbox into Rose's hands. "Not the silk — the silk stays, pressed, archived, *worshipped*. This — " she tapped the box — "is the opposite commission. The *invisibility*. Three carriage dresses, two muslins, a spencer — all of them designed, *chérie*, to be seen at a distance and remembered not at all. Flattering invisibility. It is the hardest thing I have ever made. Beauty that *erases* itself. I am — " she drew herself up — "extremely proud, and slightly horrified."
> Rose opened the box. The dresses within were — plain. Quiet. Grey, brown, a dull blue. And yet — the cut, the drape, the *fit*: Élise's hand, unmistakable, making even erasure elegant.
> "They are perfect," Rose said. "They are — " she searched — "they are *forgettable*, beautifully."
> "Beautifully forgettable," Élise corrected, radiant. "It is a new category. I am inventing it. *L'oubli élégant*." She pressed the packet of letters into Rose's hands. "And these — the intelligence. My London eyes, my Bath ears. Write to me. Not the Gazette's Rose. *You*. The muslins, the waters, the banker — and *him*, whoever *him* is that week. I shall be your atelier-in-exile."

scenes.synopsis: On the road — the London road west; the texture of travel.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: road texture scene — the journey as lived experience. The story clock moves slowly; the road is the chapter's first country.)*
> The London road west unrolled like a bolt of good cloth — the turnpike smooth, the hedgerows high with late summer, the sky a vast, indifferent blue. They changed horses at the first stage, and the second, the postilions' calls ringing out, the carriage swaying into the rhythm that Rose remembered from childhood journeys: the particular hypnosis of wheels, the particular freedom of being *between*.
> Letitia read. Dozed. Woke. Read again — a novel, smuggled, of which she was deeply ashamed and deeply fond. "The heroine," she confided, at the third stage, "has just discovered that the duke is *not* her brother. I am *invested*, Rose. Do not judge me."
> "I would never," said Rose, watching the country go by — the fields, the distant church spires, the sheep like scattered pearls. "The duke is not her brother. It is the best news I have heard all week."
> And underneath the rhythm, the thought: *west. Bath. Thursday next, eleven of the clock. The older matter. May be discussed.* The road, carrying her toward it, mile by mile.

scenes.synopsis: The inn at dusk — Julian's letter, waiting; the route's warmth, at distance.
scenes.prose:
> The first night's inn — a posting-house of creaking respectability, the yard full of ostlers and steam — brought the first post from London: a letter, redirected, in Julian's hurried hand.
> *The debts are gathered. All of them. The last note — the man who did not answer letters — answered, in the end, to a personal call, which I recommend as a strategy for all unanswered correspondence. I am solvent, Rose. Entirely, boringly, respectably solvent. I thought you should know first — before the Gazette, before the clubs, before my mother. You kept the books with me, in the library, at dusk. You should hear the closing of them. — J.*
> Rose read it twice, standing in the inn's low parlor with the fire smoking and Letitia negotiating supper in the background, and felt the warmth spread: *solvent. Entirely, boringly, respectably solvent.* The rebuilding, complete. In the open. Where everyone could see.
> She wrote back by the fire — four lines: *Solvent. Boringly, respectably, entirely. I am glad I kept the books with you. Conjugate it well. — R.*
> "The library at dusk," Letitia observed, returning with the supper news, "has produced a solvent gentleman. You have a talent, my love. You should take it to Bath. The bankers will be *thrilled*."

scenes.synopsis: The second night — Laurent's letter; the Thursday ledger, honored at distance.
scenes.prose:
> The second night's inn brought Laurent's letter — the continental hand, the faint scent of his cologne, the polish intact across a hundred miles:
> *The ball is still talked of. Honoria is still applauded. And I — I have been asked, twice, by mothers of impeccable standing, whether I intend to make a habit of dancing with wallflowers. I told them, both times, that I make a habit only of dancing with* interesting *young women, and that the ton's definition of a wallflower requires revision. The ask cost me nothing, in the end — or rather, it cost me exactly what it was worth. I am in your debt, which is, I find, a pleasant place to be. — L.*
> Rose smiled — the whole letter, the polish, the *pleasant place to be* — and wrote back: *The ton's definitions always require revision. That is what we are for. Spend the debt wisely. — R.*
> "The Comte," Letitia said, reading over her shoulder with the shamelessness of aunts, "is *charmed*. Entirely charmed. And you — " she studied Rose's face — "you are *pleased*. Entirely pleased. It is a satisfactory state of affairs, all around."
> "It is," Rose agreed. "The ask cost him. He paid it. And now — " she folded the letter — "now he finds the debt pleasant. It is the best possible outcome. For everyone. Especially Honoria."

scenes.synopsis: The third night — Frederick's silence; the unasked question, carried west.
scenes.prose:
> The third night's inn brought no letter from Frederick — and the absence was a presence, the way his absence from the waltz had been a presence: the pillar by the long windows, the palm, the *it was our dance*.
> Rose stood at the inn's window, looking out at the dark yard, and thought: *he gave me the only gift he could — his absence from my card. And now his absence from the post is — what? Discretion? Distance? The same gift, extended?*
> Letitia, coming in with the supper tray, read her face — aunts always read faces — and said, quietly: "He will write. Or he will not. Either way, my love — the pillar stands. The palm stands. The dance was danced, in the only way it could be."
> "I know," said Rose. "It is only — " She stopped. It was only that the road was long, and the night was dark, and the unasked question had followed her west like a second shadow.
> She did not write. There was nothing to write that would not have been — conspicuous. Instead, she stood at the window a while longer, and then turned in, carrying the silence like a letter unopened.

> The fourth night's inn — the last before Bath — brought Henry's letter: the soldier's hand, plain and exact, the steadiness in it like a wall.
> *I have written ahead. Two letters: one to a man of business in Bath, who will receive you; one to a friend in the Assembly Rooms, who will see you are not without company. The bank — Trelawney & Sons — is as I described: old, deep, smiling. Go carefully. Go brilliantly. And write — not the intelligence. You. The road, the rooms, the rain. I am holding you to the rain. — H.*
> Rose read it with the particular gratitude of a campaigner receiving supplies before a battle: *a man of business, who will receive her. A friend, who will see she is not without company.* Henry's ground, prepared ahead of her, mile by mile, the way he had prepared everything — quietly, completely, without being asked.
> She wrote back: *The rain, so far: two soft days, one hard. The rooms: posting-houses, creaking, respectable. The road: almost done. The banker: Thursday. I am careful. I am brilliant. Both, I promise. — R.*

scenes.synopsis: Arrival — Bath, seen first; the crescents, the stone, the waters' smell.
scenes.prose:
> Bath announced itself before it was seen — the smell first, mineral and faintly sulphurous, the waters' breath on the air; then the stone, honey-colored in the afternoon light; then the crescents, curving like a held breath, the whole city composed as if for a portrait it had been sitting for for a hundred years.
> "Well," said Letitia, leaning out of the carriage window with the air of a critic at a first night. "It is — *composed*. Aggressively composed. Every street a crescent, every crescent a composition. I feel — " she settled back — "I feel as though the city is *posing*, and expects to be admired, and will be *wounded* if one does not admire it correctly."
> "Admire it correctly, then," said Rose, smiling — but her eyes were on the streets, the chairmen, the visitors with their Bath chairs, the whole machinery of the taking of the waters: a city built around invalids and idlers, around *restoration* of the bodily kind.
> *Thursday next, eleven of the clock. The older matter. May be discussed.* Four days. Four days to learn the city, take the waters, be seen at distance and remembered not at all — and then, the counting-house.

scenes.synopsis: The lodgings — Mrs. Plumtree; the rooms; the base established.
scenes.prose:
> The lodgings were in a quiet street off the Circus — a tall, narrow house, the door opened by Mrs. Plumtree herself: a woman of formidable respectability and even more formidable curiosity, who looked Rose up and down with the practiced eye of one who has assessed ten thousand visitors and been wrong about none of them.
> "Miss Hartwell. Mrs. Hartwell." The curtsy was exact. "The first floor. Sitting room, two bedchambers, the small parlor for letters. The waters — " she gestured, vaguely west — "the Pump Room is seven minutes. The Assembly Rooms, twelve. The shops — " a glint — "four."
> The rooms were clean, plain, and honest — the sitting room with its bow window overlooking the street, the bedchambers small but sweet, the whole of it smelling of beeswax and discretion.
> "It will do," Letitia pronounced, with the air of a queen accepting a tribute. "It will do *very* well. Mrs. Plumtree — " she fixed the landlady with the full Hartwell charm — "we are quiet people. We take the waters. We write letters. We are *dull*, Mrs. Plumtree. Delightfully, completely dull."
> "Of course, ma'am," said Mrs. Plumtree — with the air of a woman filing the statement under *pending verification*.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — "How do we arrive in Bath?" Arrive as the Hartwell heiress / arrive quietly / arrive unannounced.
scenes.prose:
> ★ **KEY DECISION 2/3 — "How do we arrive in Bath?"**
> *(System: key decision. All three arrivals end with Rose established in Bath — the difference is the means, and the means are remembered: the city's reading, the banker's first impression, the Gazette's paragraph.)*
> That evening, over tea in the sitting room with the bow window darkening onto the quiet street, Letitia laid out the question: "Bath society. It is not London — it is smaller, older, and *watchful*, the way small cities are. Everyone knows everyone, and everyone knows it. The question is not whether we arrive — we have arrived — but *how* we are *seen* to arrive."
> "Three ways," Rose said — she had learned that from her aunt. "**First** — as the *Hartwell heiress*. The name, carried openly. We call, we are called upon, we take our place. The city knows exactly who we are — and the banker, when I walk into his counting-house Thursday, has already heard the name in the Pump Room."
> "**Second** — *quietly*. We take the waters. We are dull, delightful, completely unremarkable. No cards, no calls, no stir. The city does not notice us — which is precisely what the carriage dress was made for."
> "**Third** — " Rose paused — "*unannounced*. No cards sent, no name carried, no introduction sought. We simply — appear. In the Pump Room, in the Assembly Rooms. A new face, unexplained. The city will invent its own story — and inventing, Aunt, is *work*, and work makes people careless."
> Letitia considered. "The heiress way risks the *Gazette's* interest — which we do not want in Bath. The quiet way risks invisibility — though invisibility, well made, is a weapon. The unannounced way — " she smiled — "the unannounced way is *cheek*. Magnificent, dangerous cheek."
> ◇ **choice** — *the decision* — **the Hartwell heiress** (the name, carried openly) / **quietly** (the waters, no stir) / **unannounced** (no cards, no name — simply there) *(remembered: the means — the city's reading, the banker's first impression, the Gazette's paragraph — Rose is established in Bath regardless)*

> *(Decision locks: the means of arriving. Bath will know her — but the city will remember* how *she came.)*

scenes.synopsis: The Pump Room — the waters, taken; Bath society, observed.
scenes.prose:

> "Bath," Letitia pronounced, over breakfast in the sitting room — the bow window open onto the quiet street, the waters' hour approaching — "is a *village* with *pretensions*. > Letitia read the note with the grim air of a woman reading a declaration of war — which, she observed, it was: "The waters are not for Hartwells. *Go home*. My love — someone in this *composed* little city knows exactly why we are here, and does not want us here."

> "Burning," Letitia said, "is brave. Showing is *war* — it tells Bath we are not merely taking the waters. Keeping — " she weighed it — "keeping is *wise*. And wisdom, my love, is the weapon we can afford." She watched Rose slip the note into the writing case, beside Trelawney's letter. "Filed. Dated. Witnessed — by me. Let the frightened write. > Mr. Aldercroft called on Wednesday evening — Henry's friend, the man of business with kind eyes and the professional discretion — and over tea in the sitting room, briefed her with the thoroughness of a man who had been asked, by a friend he respected, to prepare a lady for a banker.

Mr. Trelawney himself — " he chose his words — "Mr. Trelawney smiles, Miss Hartwell. It is his profession to smile. Behind the smile — " a pause — "behind the smile is a man who has kept other men's secrets for forty years, and kept them *well*. He will see you. He will discuss — *may* discuss. But he will decide, in the first five minutes, how much of the older matter you are *ready* for. Be ready."
> "How," Rose asked, "does one *be* ready — for a banker?"
> Aldercroft smiled — the professional's smile, kindly meant. "By knowing what you want, and not wanting it too *visibly*. Bankers lend to the calm. They *confide* in the calm. Be the calmest person in the counting-house, Miss Hartwell, and Mr. Trelawney will tell you — " he paused — "whatever he has decided you are ready to hear."

scenes.prose:
> Wednesday evening. Rose came in from the Assembly Rooms — the corners worked, the talk gathered, the underestimation holding — and stopped in the sitting-room doorway.
> On the table — centered on the polished wood with deliberate theatre — lay a stripped thorn stem. The thorns intact, the leaves and bloom torn away. No card. No note. No direction.
> *Once said.* A thorn stem, stripped bare, speaks one word in the flower language: *danger*. Not the threat of danger — the *fact* of it, stated botanically. And it had been left *inside* — not at the door, not in the post — on the sitting-room table. Past Mrs. Plumtree's keys, past the bolted back door, past everything. Someone knew she read the flower language. Someone knew her campaign's grammar — and had gotten *in*.
> ★ **KEY DECISION 3/3 — "The thorn stem"**
> *(System: key decision. All three dispositions end with the stem kept and carried into the next chapter — the difference is the means, and the means are remembered: who knows, who doesn't, and what the showing costs.)*
> "Three ways," Rose said to Letitia, low. "**First** — I show it to *no one*. It stays between us — on the table, the answer displayed, the author watching to see it kept. No letter, no banker, no stir."
> "**Second** — I show it to *Augusta*, by letter. The rear guard, informed — described exactly, thorn by thorn, with the question: who in London knows I read flowers?"
> "**Third** — " she paused — "I show it to *Trelawney*. I lay it before the banker — in his city, on his counting-house desk — and ask him what danger, stated botanically, means in Bath."
> Letitia was quiet. "No one — is discipline. Augusta — is family. Trelawney — " she weighed it — "Trelawney is *war*, my love. It tells the banker we are not merely taking the waters. Choose carefully."

> Three threads. One loom: the émigré notes, discounted in Bath, carried to London, for particular houses. And Élise's fitters, with pins in their mouths, hearing all of it — the atelier as the campaign's second listening post, after the furniture.
> And the price — *what it costs* — Rose set down the letter and did the arithmetic the way Quill had taught her: in risk, not coin. Élise, twenty-two, with a workroom of girls and a Bath book full of bankers' wives. Every letter from the atelier was a letter that could be intercepted, read, traced. The intelligence was real. The danger was real. And the decision — pay, keep casual, or cut — was hers, and could not be unmade once the war reached the workroom.

> ★ **KEY DECISION 1/3 — "What are the atelier's terms?"**
> *(System: key decision. All three terms end with Élise's letters continuing — the difference is the means, and the means are remembered: the atelier's safety, the channel's honesty, the war's reach into the workroom.)*
> The Bath book was intelligence — real, regular, and dangerous. Élise's fitters heard what Bath said while pinned; Bath said everything, believing no one was listening, believing a fitting room was a confessional. But the channel had a price, and Rose stood at the study's window with the letter in her hand and weighed it the way she weighed everything now: in means, not ends.
> "Three ways," she said aloud — to Letitia, to the room, to herself. "**First** — I *pay* the atelier. A standing arrangement, honestly paid: the Bath book becomes a budgeted intelligence service. Élise is safer for the money — and deeper in the war for the purpose. Protected and exposed, both at once."
> "**Second** — I keep it *casual*. No instructions, no payment. The letters come as they come; gossip as gossip. The channel stays deniable, and Élise stays a modiste who happens to hear things — uncompromised, unprotected, unasked."
> "**Third** — " Rose paused — "I *cut* it. Too dangerous. I tell Élise to write of muslins only — and I lose the best ears in Bath, and she keeps her workroom innocent."
> Letitia was quiet — a rare thing. "Paying," she said at last, "is honest. Keeping it casual is *kind*. Cutting it is — " she weighed it — "cutting it is safe, my love. For her. Not for you. Choose carefully — the workroom has girls in it, and Élise is twenty-two."

A week of the cheapest disguise in the world — and Rose stood at the study's window, looking over the rooftops toward the Abbey, and weighed what the underestimation had bought: the room's geography, the bankers' knot, the bouquets' language, Henry's roads. The beau, emboldened by her modesty, talked — about the season's thinness, about Trelawney's nerves, about the London houses — and Rose listened with the furniture's perfect attention, gathering, gathering, while the chandeliers burned lower and the queens glittered on.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — "What is the discarded friend — to us?" Confront her / watch her / warn no one and wait.
scenes.prose:
> ★ **KEY DECISION 3/3 — "What is the discarded friend — to us?"**
> *(System: key decision. All three answers end with Cecilia in Bath and the campaign continuing — the difference is the means, and the means are remembered: the household's nerve, the thread's handling, the solitude or counsel of the choice.)*
> A week in Bath, and the primrose girl was everywhere and nowhere: the lodging off the Crescent, the assembly's edge, the Pump Room's far colonnade. Watching the lodging. Watching the bankers. Watching *her*. Cecilia Vane — the discarded friend, the seller of secrets, the girl who had palmed folded paper with the ease of long practice — was in Bath, and Rose had to decide what the discarded friend was.
> "Three ways," she said — to Letitia, in the sitting room, the week's evidence between them. "**First** — I *confront* her. The lodging off the Crescent, the direct question: *who pays you, Cecilia?* She answers, or she flees — but the watching ends, one way or another. Nerve, and rupture."
> "**Second** — I *watch* her. The patient way: no contact, her lodgings watched, her callers noted, her movements mapped. Cecilia's game will name its own players — the buyers will call on her, and I will be there to see them."
> "**Third** — " Rose paused — "I tell *no one* and wait. Not you, not Augusta, not Trelawney. The knowledge stays in my pocketbook with the single thorn stem, and Cecilia plays unwatched — by everyone but me. Solitude, and patience."
> Letitia considered. "Confronting," she said, "is brave. Watching is *wise*. Waiting alone is — " she looked at her niece — "waiting alone is the hardest, my love. Whatever you choose — do not carry it the way you carried the silence on the road west. Not alone. Not this time."

scenes.synopsis: Letitia's Bath social life — the gossip division, delivering. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> Letitia's Bath social life was a campaign in itself — the calls, the teas, the promenades, the whole machinery of a sociable aunt deployed with military precision — and that week, over tea in the sitting room, the gossip division delivered.
> "The bankers," Letitia announced, with the satisfaction of a general reporting a position taken. "Trelawney's — sound, frightened, holding too much French paper; the whole town says so, which means the whole town is either right or repeating itself. The London houses — Voss & Hallett's man was here last month, asking after obligations. *Hartwell* obligations, my love — I had it from a matron who had it from a clerk who had it from the waters themselves, or near enough." She poured, triumphant. "And the primrose girl — walking the Crescent at dusk, watching the lodgings. Watching *ours*, Rose. I have had it from two separate promenades, which in Bath constitutes *proof*."
> "Two separate promenades," Rose said. "The gossip division is thorough."
> "The gossip division," said Letitia, "is *magnificent*. Now — " she set down the pot with decision — "what do we do with it?"
> "We do," Rose said, "what the campaign always does: we file it, we follow it, and we frighten the right people with the right parts of it. The bankers' fear — for Trelawney, tomorrow. The London houses' curiosity — for Quill, by post. And the primrose girl — " she looked at her aunt — "for us. The gossip division's next assignment: Cecilia's lodgings, her callers, her hours. Two separate promenades was proof. Let us have four."

scenes.synopsis: Honoria's letter — the sponsorship by letter; the wallflower, blooming. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> Honoria's first Bath letter — four pages, the round careful hand, the stammer nowhere in evidence even in ink:
> *Dearest Rose — the baronet walked with me in the park. *Walked.* Where people could see. And Aunt Agatha — you will not believe it — *smiled*. At me. A real smile, not the assizes one. The sponsorship continues, she says, and I am to write everything, and you are to write back the truth. So here is the truth: I am happy. I did not know I could be. — H.*
> Rose read it twice, standing at the bow window with the Bath street below, and felt the London campaign's dividend arrive by post: the wallflower, blooming. The price — Drummond's price, the sponsorship, the spent dances — worth paying, again, at a distance. The baronet walked with her *where people could see*. The dragon *smiled*. The girl who had stammered through a season was happy, and did not know she could be.
> She answered that evening — the truth, as promised: *You are doing well. You were doing well before I arrived. The baronet has excellent taste in walking companions. Bath is damp and full of bankers. Write everything. — R.*
> She sealed the letter with the Hartwell crest — the small defiance of it, the house's arms on a letter to a girl who had been taught to be ashamed of wanting things — and gave it to the post with the morning's others. The sponsorship, by letter: the wallflower blooming at a distance, the heiress watching from Bath, the baronet walking Thursdays like a standing order of the heart.

scenes.synopsis: Quill's letter — the de Valcourt papers; London's watch. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> Quill's Bath letter — the solicitor's hand, exact, the paper folded with legal precision:
> The paper was folded with legal precision, the seal exact — Quill's care visible even in the creases, the solicitor's exactness traveling two hundred miles by post to reach her.
> *The de Valcourt papers continue to point to Bath. Alder copies — under supervision, beautifully; the double channel holds. The London end: Voss & Hallett's credit is sound and their curiosity is not — they have asked after Hartwell obligations in two quarters. Mind the counting-house, Miss Hartwell. Bankers are careful, which is to say frightened of exactly the right things. Frighten him of the right things.*
> *Frighten him of the right things.* Rose smiled — Quill's counsel, translated from solicitor into strategy: show Trelawney the notes, hold the papers, let the banker ask the questions, and answer only the ones that frighten him correctly. The counting-house was tomorrow, ten o'clock; the dove-grey was laid out; the approach was set. And London's watch held — Alder copying beautifully, the front curious in two quarters, the papers pointing west like a compass needle.
> She filed the letter with the memorandum, and wrote in the pocketbook: *Quill: frighten him of the right things. Tomorrow: the notes shown, the papers held.*
> And the London end — *their curiosity is not sound* — the solicitor's warning folded into the solicitor's report. Voss & Hallett, asking after Hartwell obligations in two quarters. Two quarters: the counting-house, and — where? The question sat in the pocketbook with the memorandum, unanswered, until Bath supplied the answer. Which, Rose reflected, Bath was in the habit of doing — usually over the waters, usually unguarded, usually before ten o'clock.

scenes.prose:
> The day before the appointment, Rose walked past Trelawney & Sons — the counting-house, observed from the street like a battery's position, the dove-grey muslin doing its beautiful forgetting among the afternoon shoppers.
> *(System: the counting-house, reconnoitered — the appointment is tomorrow; today, the street.)*
> It was smaller than she had expected — a honey-stone front, a brass plate worn by two hundred years of weather and discretion, windows of ground glass that gave nothing back. Clerks came and went with the particular hurry of men carrying other people's money. A carrier's cart stood at the side door — sealed packets, she guessed, remembering Henry's sketch: the stations, the riders, the Bath end of the line, the western road's commerce made visible in canvas and twine. Henry's sketch, confirmed in three dimensions.
> She did not go in. Tomorrow, ten o'clock, the dove-grey, the notes shown and the papers held — Quill's counsel, rehearsed. > She took a turn along the street — the honey-stone glowing, the afternoon shoppers thinning — and marked the counting-house's rhythms the way she had marked the Pump Room's: the clerks' hours, the carriers' calls, the brass plate's discretion. A battery's position, mapped. Tomorrow she would walk through the ground-glass doors and into the smell of money gone quiet — but today, the street was enough. scenes.synopsis: A banker's clerk, talkative — the coffee-house; the line, overheard. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> The coffee-house across from the counting-house was the clerks' hour at four — the low room full of bankers' clerks unwinding, the air thick with coffee and indiscretion, the clerks' parliament in session — and one clerk, young, talkative, three cups in, was holding forth on the subject nearest every banker's clerk's heart: other people's money.
> Rose took a table in the corner — dove-grey, unremarked, furniture, the coffee ordered and barely touched — and listened.
> "...the French paper," the clerk was saying, expansive, gesturing with his cup. "The widows' notes, the émigré notes — Trelawney holds too much of it, everyone says so. Discounted — " he lowered his voice, which made it carry further across the low room — "discounted for particular London houses. That's the trade. The notes come in from the carriers, we discount them, the London houses take them up. Particular houses. You understand."
> The table understood — nodding, chuckling, ordering another round, the laugh of men who understood perfectly and were paid not to. Rose — in her corner, over her coffee, the quiet heiress no one had noticed arrive — understood better. *Particular London houses.* The phrase, in a clerk's mouth, in a coffee-house, in the open. The trail's language, confirmed by its own machinery.
> The room was all clerks and coffee and the particular looseness of men off duty — and Rose, in her corner, understood suddenly why Élise's fitting rooms worked: people confessed to furniture. The clerk, the fitters' clients, the bankers themselves — everyone talked past the unremarkable. The underestimation was not a disguise. It was a *profession*.
