scenes.prose:
> When the clerk's table thinned — the others drifting back to the counting-house, the round finished — Rose did what furniture never does: she spoke.
> "Forgive me," she said, in the quiet heiress's voice — the one Bath had filed under *unremarkable*, soft and curious and entirely harmless. "I could not help overhearing — the French paper. My aunt holds some small notes — a legacy, you understand — and we wondered where such things were discounted. *Particular London houses,* you said?"
> The clerk — flattered to be consulted by a lady, however quiet, however plain — expanded, the way young men expand when asked about their expertise. "Voss & Hallett, mostly. The London banking house. They take up the French paper — the émigré notes — discounted here, carried up by the carriers. Particular houses, particular terms." He leaned in, confidential, the fourth cup arriving. "Between us, ma'am — Trelawney's been nervous. Holding too much of it. If the London houses called the notes — "
> He stopped — the indiscretion catching up with him, the professional instinct surfacing through the coffee — but the line was out, and Rose had it whole: *Voss & Hallett, mostly. Particular houses, particular terms. If the London houses called the notes.*
> "Thank you," she said — the grateful girl, the legacy explained — and left him to his cup, unalerted, unremarkable, already forgetting her.
> She crossed the street with the line whole — *Voss & Hallett, mostly; particular houses, particular terms; if the London houses called the notes* — and felt the morning's fragment from the Pump Room lock into place beside it: *asking after — *. After the Hartwell obligations. The two lines, together, made a door. Tomorrow, ten o'clock, she would knock.

scenes.synopsis: The partial answer — what the clerk knows, and what he doesn't; the pattern's edge. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> She left the clerk to his fourth cup — no more questions; furniture does not interrogate, and the grateful girl had already learned enough — and walked the Crescent with the line whole in her head, the honey-stone glowing in the late afternoon:
> *Trelawney & Sons discounts émigré notes for particular London houses. Voss & Hallett, mostly. Particular houses, particular terms. Trelawney's nervous. Holding too much of it.*
> What the clerk knew: the mechanism — notes in from the carriers, discounts out to London, the trade described with a clerk's pride in the machinery. What he didn't: *why* the London houses wanted the French paper — what they bought with it, besides interest; what "particular terms" meant; and why a London banking house would send its man to Bath to ask after *Hartwell* obligations. And the unasked question, the one that had followed her from the assembly's corners like a second shadow: *asking after the Hartwell obligations.* Voss's man, in Bath last month — asking after *her* family's paper.
> The pattern's edge — sharp, personal, cold. Tomorrow, ten o'clock, the counting-house — and Trelawney himself, smiling, with forty years of kept secrets. She would show him the notes. She would hold the papers. And she would ask — calmly, the calmest person in the room — about particular houses.
> And beneath the questions, the deeper one — the one she would not ask aloud, not yet, not in the counting-house: *what does the Network want with French widows' paper?* The notes were wartime money, displaced persons' money. Discounted, carried, taken up — for *particular terms*. The terms were the story. The terms were what Trelawney was frightened of. And frightened men, in her experience, talked.

scenes.synopsis: The walk home — piecing the pattern; the general's view, refined. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(System: the walk home — the pattern, pieced; the map room, refined.)*
> The Crescent at dusk, the honey-stone glowing rose-gold: Rose walked home slowly, piecing it, the clerk's line turning in her mind like a key in a lock.
> The émigré notes — wartime money, French names, widows' paper — discounted at Trelawney & Sons, carried up the western road by the carriers, taken up in London by Voss & Hallett. *Particular houses, particular terms.* The Network's money, moving like dispatches — regular, profitable, mapped, the stations the same inns Henry's riders had used. And at the pattern's center, the new intelligence, cold and personal: Voss's man, asking after the Hartwell obligations. Not the French paper in general — *her family's paper*. The mortgages. The forced sale Rackham had started — the acquisition, continued by other hands.
> They wanted her family's paper. Lucien de Valcourt's want, glimpsed through the mechanism like a face through ground glass: *Hartwell Park itself.* The house, the land, the whole of it — bought up in pieces, through notes and obligations, until the Park belonged to the Network.
> She stopped on the Crescent, in the dusk, and felt the campaign's true shape settle: she was not following money. She was following *an appetite*.
> The Crescent's lamps were coming on, one by one, and the honey-stone held the day's last light like a memory. An appetite — for Hartwell Park, for her family's paper, for the whole of it, bought up in pieces through notes and obligations. De Valcourt's want. The Network's want. She walked home through the dusk with the appetite's shape in her mind, and the thorn stem in her pocketbook, and the calm that came from finally seeing the board.

scenes.synopsis: The thorn stem, remembered — the warning threading through the week. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> That night, Rose took the thorn stem from the pocketbook — stripped, sharp, a week old, the thorns still intact — and looked at it in the lamplight, laid out on the desk beside the week's account.
> A week of plain muslin. A week of being looked through. A week of bouquets and bankers and talkative clerks — and the warning had not repeated. No second stem. No card. The author — whoever knew her flower language, whoever had come past Mrs. Plumtree's vigilance — had said it once and fallen silent. *Danger. Beware. The path is watched.*
> She had proceeded — carefully, as advised — and the path had led her here: to the counting-house's door, to the clerk's line, to the pattern's edge, to the appetite at the pattern's center. If the warning had meant to stop her, it had failed. If it had meant to *arm* her — then it had succeeded, and the author was — what? A friend, warning in the only language they shared? The Network, courteous, preferring she leave before she was *made* to leave? Cecilia — the primrose girl, fluent, watching the lodging?
> She laid the stem back in the pocketbook, beside the memorandum. Tomorrow, ten o'clock, Trelawney — and whatever the warning had meant, she would walk in armed: with the notes, the papers, the clerk's line, and the calm.
> The lamp burned low. The week's account lay closed beside the stem — the campaign's log, the warning's grammar, her own steadier hand. *Proceed. Carefully. As advised.* The author's silence was itself a message: the warning had been given; the rest was up to her.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — TRELAWNEY. On the counting-house step: how far does she take the frightened banker — into confidence, as a source, or shielded from the trail? (Turns: 3 — the decision itself)
scenes.prose:

> "Miss Hartwell." On the step, in the Milsom Street air, the iron-grey man looked suddenly older, and suddenly less like an account book. "A word — not as your banker's, but as a man who has daughters. The London houses — Voss and Hallett — they are not merely respectable. They are particular. And particular men, when they learn that a young lady is asking after their traffic, do not send notes. They send collectors. Be careful what you write down, and where you write it."

- **Take him fully into confidence** — *Trelawney ally, risk shared.* Rose tells him what she is really tracing — Rackham's scattered paper, the Network's money, the Hartwell mortgages being gathered — and asks him to watch the London traffic for her. - **Use him as a source only** — *Information+, Trelawney neutral.* Rose takes what he has given and asks for nothing more — a client's courtesy, a banker's discretion. He remains a door she can knock on, nothing more; the trail stays hers alone.
- **Protect him from the trail** — *Trelawney shielded, Rose alone.* Rose warns him off — tells him to forget her visit, to keep his ledgers beautiful and his head down. He is grateful, and useless to her; the counting-house door closes behind her, perhaps for good.

scenes.synopsis: At the tea — the banker's wife talks; what she knows that the ledgers don't say. The harmlessness works. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> Mrs. Trelawney's drawing room was the dullest Rose had ever sat in, and within twenty minutes she understood that it was also the best-informed: the dullness was camouflage, and the tea was the town's clearing-house.
> *(System: the Thursday tea — bankers' wives, dowagers, the harmless direction worn perfectly; Rose is approved, and therefore told things.)*
> Mrs. Trelawney herself — plump, plain, watchful as a cat at a mouse-hole — took Rose's hand in both of hers and said, "My husband speaks highly of your discretion, Miss Hartwell," which told Rose, in one sentence, that the counting-house had reported the interview, that the wife knew its contents, and that the marriage was a partnership in the fullest sense.
> (T1 · tone) *Rose answers with the tea's own currency — "How interesting," meaning nothing, believing everything.* — remembered: *the password, used.*
> (T2 · look closer) *She studies Mrs. Trelawney the way she studied the ledger — for the margins: what the wife knows that the husband's books don't say.* — remembered: *the second ledger.*
> "Bath is a small town, my dear, for all its crescents." Mrs. Trelawney poured with the precision of a woman who had poured through thirty years of other people's business. "The London houses — you will have heard the names — do love our Bath paper. And our Bath carriers do love their London errands. It is all very —" the pause, the lowered voice — "particular."
> (T3 · social maneuver) *Rose lets the silence do the asking — Letitia's creditor, compounding.* — remembered: *what the silence buys.*
> (T4 · remembered micro-decision) *"Particular" — the clerk's word, the banker's word, now the wife's word; three witnesses, one vocabulary. She files it.* — remembered: *the word, triangulated.*
> What followed, over the second cup, was the wife's ledger — kept not in ink but in memory, and therefore unseizable: which Bath families had sold notes at a discount and why; which carriers were honest and which were merely punctual; and — dropped like a handkerchief, to be picked up or not — that the London collector had been seen twice this month at the White Hart, "asking after the Hartwell girl's movements, my dear — I thought you should know."
> (T5 · stance) *Rose does not flinch. The harmless dress holds; the pleasant smile holds; only her hand, on the teacup, stills for half a second.* — remembered: *her discipline, witnessed.*
> (T6 · tone) *"How interesting," she says — and means, for the first time that afternoon, exactly that.* — remembered: *the mask, and its one crack.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She asks, lightly, for the collector's description — or lets it come, unasked, in the tea's own time.* — remembered: *how she got the face.*
> Young, the wife said. London-cut coat. A watch-chain — no, not a watch-chain; that was the other one, the master. This one was the servant of the traffic: neat, quiet, forgettable. Like, Mrs. Trelawney said, looking Rose up and down with sudden shrewdness, a girl in a grey dress trying to be wallpaper.
> (T8 · look closer) *Rose meets the shrewdness with candor — one honest look, hostess to guest, woman to woman.* — remembered: *the recognition, mutual.*
> "Wallpaper," Mrs. Trelawney said softly, "sees everything, my dear. Mind you hang straight."

scenes.synopsis: The wife's warning — "particular London houses," named at last; what the London collector wants with the Hartwell girl. (Turns: 9)
scenes.prose:
> They were alone, briefly — the other guests drawn to the window by a commotion in the street (a runaway chair, a shouting chairman; Bath's dullness, punctured) — and Mrs. Trelawney used the minute the way a banker uses a margin: for the entry that must not appear in the main account.
> "Voss and Hallett," she said, without preamble, refilling Rose's cup though it was full. "You have the name from my husband, I don't doubt. What you don't have — what he won't say, because bankers don't — is what the house *is*. It is not a banking house, my dear. Not really. It is a —" she searched for the word — "a funnel. Money goes in from a dozen directions, and comes out in one: English land. Mortgages. Your Mr. Quill would call it a front. I call it what it is, because I am a banker's wife and I am allowed."
> (T1 · look closer) *Rose listens with her whole attention — this is the wife's ledger, open at last, and it will not stay open long.* — remembered: *what she hears.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *"A funnel" — she writes it in her head in capital letters, next to Trelawney's "broader correspondences."* — remembered: *the translation.*
> "And the collector — the London man — he is Voss's creature. Not Voss himself; Voss is the master, the watch-chain, the one who dines with directors. This one is the errand boy with expensive errands, and his errand, these two months, has been —" she looked at Rose directly — "you. Your movements. Your questions. Your callers."
> (T3 · stance) *Rose sits very still — the watched, learning she is watched; the hunter, learning she is hunted.* — remembered: *the reversal, absorbed.*
> (T4 · tone) *"Me," she says evenly. "How flattering. One does like to be someone's errand."* — remembered: *her nerve, displayed.*
> "My husband says you are tracing your father's papers." Mrs. Trelawney's voice dropped to the tea's lowest register. "My dear — papers are the least of it. They are watching *you* because you are the paper that matters now. The Hartwell name, on a mortgage, on a draft, on a girl who asks questions in counting-houses — you are the account they are trying to settle."
> (T5 · social maneuver) *Rose can ask what the wife advises (counsel, owed) or tell the wife what she intends (trust, offered).* — remembered: *the exchange's terms.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *She files the collector's description whole — young, London-cut, neat, quiet, forgettable — a face to find in a crowd.* — remembered: *the quarry, described.*
> (T7 · look closer) *She studies Mrs. Trelawney's face for the price of this warning — there is always a price; the wife's is that Rose remember who told her.* — remembered: *the debt, acknowledged.*
> (T8 · tone) *Her thanks are real — the first unperformed thing she has said all afternoon — and the wife hears it.* — remembered: *the alliance, sealed.*
> (T9 · stance) *She rejoins the tea as if nothing has happened — the wallpaper, rehung straight.* — remembered: *the performance, resumed.*
> "Mind you hang straight," Mrs. Trelawney had said. Rose hung straight — and underneath the harmless muslin, every nerve was a plumb-line, true and trembling.

scenes.synopsis: Texture — the tea reckoned on the walk home; what harmlessness bought: a funnel, a collector, and the knowledge that she is the account. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> She walked home through the damp Bath dusk, the harmless dress still on, the harmless smile still available — and underneath them, the reckoning.
> *(System: the walk — the Circus lamps lit, the Crescent's curve, Rose turning the wife's ledger over like a coin.)*
> What harmlessness had bought: the truth about Voss & Hallett — *a funnel, not a banking house.* The collector's errand — *her.* And the sentence that rearranged the whole campaign like a pin moved on a board: *you are the paper that matters now. You are the account they are trying to settle.*
> (T1 · remembered micro-decision) *She rehearses the wife's words verbatim — "a funnel," "the account they are trying to settle" — committing them the way she committed the margin's hand.* — remembered: *the testimony.*
> (T2 · look closer) *She checks the street behind her — once, casually, the way she has learned to check streets — for the neat, quiet, forgettable London man.* — remembered: *the habit, formed.*
> (T3 · stance) *She walks on, unhurried — a watched woman must never look watched; it spoils the watcher's confidence, and confidence makes men careless.* — remembered: *the counter-game, begun.*
> She had come to Bath to follow the money up the chain. She was learning, instead, that the chain had been following her — that every question she asked in a counting-house was reported, every carrier's name she copied was noted, every tea she drank was drunk under observation.
> (T4 · social maneuver) *She decides: to go on asking openly (the brazen road) or to go quiet (the wallpaper, perfected).* — remembered: *the campaign's new footing.*
> (T5 · tone) *She laughs — once, short, at herself — for having thought the underestimation was her idea.* — remembered: *her humility, filed.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *She does not write any of it down tonight. Some things are safer in the head than in the book, and "they send collectors" has joined them.* — remembered: *the discipline, deepened.*
> (T7 · look closer) *At the lodgings' door she pauses and looks back at Bath — the town that had seemed all circles and water and cure, and was, underneath, a counting-house with crescents.* — remembered: *Bath, re-seen.*
> The tea had been harmless. The reckoning was not.

scenes.synopsis: Beat B4 — Laurent's letter arrives: the family pressure; the de Varenne bankers near the trail; his polish, strained. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> The letter came with the Friday post — French paper, French seal, Laurent's hand, which was usually so perfectly formed it might have been engraved, and was today, Rose saw at once, hurried.
> *(System: the morning room — Letitia tactfully absorbed in a novel held upside down; Rose alone with the letter, in effect if not in fact.)*
> *My dear Miss Hartwell —* (not *Rose*; the formality was the first crack in the polish) *— I write in some haste, and some disquiet. My family's bankers — you will remember I spoke of them — have been making inquiries. About Bath. About discounting. About — forgive me — about you. They are respectable men, Rose. They are also frightened men, and frightened respectable men are the most dangerous kind, because they mistake their fear for prudence.*
> (T1 · look closer) *She studies the handwriting — the hurried loops, the ink pressed harder on "frightened" — his polish, strained, in every line.* — remembered: *how far the pressure has reached.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *"My family's bankers" — the de Varenne bankers, uncomfortably near the trail; she files it next to the funnel.* — remembered: *the adjacency, marked.*
> *I tell you this because you once told me that a debt is a lever and a lever needs a fulcrum. My family may be someone's fulcrum, and I do not know whose hand is on the lever. Be careful of them — and, I beg you, be careful of me. I am not sure, just now, which of us is the more exposed.*
> (T3 · tone) *She reads the last line twice — "which of us is the more exposed" — and feels the letter's real message underneath the polish: he is asking for help without asking.* — remembered: *what he didn't quite say.*
> (T4 · stance) *She folds the letter slowly — the suitor's distress, held at arm's length or drawn close; the war council of one, deciding.* — remembered: *her posture toward him.*
> (T5 · social maneuver) *She considers what the letter costs him — a de Varenne, admitting fear, in writing — and prices his trust accordingly.* — remembered: *the admission's weight.*
> (T6 · look closer) *She holds the seal to the light — French paper, French wax; the world he comes from, pressing on the world she is in.* — remembered: *the two worlds, touching.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She does not show Letitia the letter — not yet; some intelligence is hers alone until she decides its use.* — remembered: *the secret, kept.*
> (T8 · tone) *Her first thought, unguarded and unworthy: *the de Varenne bankers are near the trail because the trail runs past everyone.* Her second thought, better: *he told me anyway.** — remembered: *both thoughts, filed.*
> She slipped the letter into her workbox — beside Drummond's card, beside the carrier names — and understood that the war had just acquired a second front: not only the money's roads, but the people standing on them.

scenes.synopsis: The letter's contents, turned over — what loyalty might require; Rose drafts and discards three replies in her head. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> She did not answer at once. She walked — the Crescent, the Circus, the long way round by the Assembly Rooms — with the letter's phrases keeping step beside her like an unwelcome companion.
> *(System: the walk — Bath going about its cure, Rose going about her war; the reply, composed and discarded, three times over.)*
> First draft, honest: *My dear Laurent — tell me everything about your family's bankers, and I will tell you everything about Voss & Hallett, and we shall be allies in the open, whatever it costs.* Too honest — honesty, between a Hartwell and a de Varenne, with bankers listening, was a luxury neither house could afford.
> (T1 · tone) *She tries the honest draft on the empty air — and hears how it sounds: a treaty, proposed in wartime.* — remembered: *the instinct, noted.*
> Second draft, light: *Dear Laurent — Bath is dull, the waters are undrinkable, and your bankers sound perfectly respectable; do stop worrying.* Too light — he would hear the dismissal in it, and the polish would seal over the crack, and she would lose the one honest letter he had ever written her.
> (T2 · social maneuver) *She weighs the light draft — dismissal as protection; would it shield him, or only shield her?* — remembered: *the calculation.*
> Third draft, silence: no answer at all — let the letter lie, let him wonder, let the pressure show her what it is before she commits a word to paper that a collector might read.
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *She considers the collector — the neat, quiet London man, asking after her movements — and what an answered letter looks like in his report.* — remembered: *the surveillance, priced.*
> (T4 · look closer) *She stops at the top of the Crescent and looks back at the town — every crescent a ledger entry, every ledger entry somebody's fear.* — remembered: *Bath, as Laurent sees it.*
> (T5 · stance) *She stands very still, the three drafts balanced like scales — honesty, lightness, silence — and feels the weight of each.* — remembered: *the choice, loading.*
> (T6 · tone) *She says his name aloud — "Laurent" — testing whether it sounds like an ally or a liability. It sounds, annoyingly, like both.* — remembered: *the verdict, inconclusive.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She remembers his flicker in London — the émigré notes touching his world, the polish mastering it — and understands the crack has been widening for weeks.* — remembered: *the pattern, long.*
> (T8 · social maneuver) *She decides: the answer will be written tonight — but which of the three drafts survives is a decision for the desk, not the street.* — remembered: *the deferral, deliberate.*
> The walk ended where it began, at the lodgings' door. Three drafts, no decision — which was, she reflected, itself a kind of answer: the careful kind.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — LAURENT'S LETTER. At the writing desk: answer honestly, answer lightly, or don't answer yet. (Turns: 3 — the decision itself)
scenes.prose:
> The desk was laid — paper, pen, the French seal's red wax waiting — and the three drafts stood in her head like suitors, each with his merits, each with his dangers: the honest letter, the light letter, the silence.
> *(The writing desk, night — the letter from Laurent open beside the blank page; the collector, somewhere out in Bath, writing his own report.)*
> She had walked the Crescent composing and discarding all three — honesty that would warn and implicate, lightness that would protect and dismiss, silence that would let the pressure declare itself before she committed a word a collector might read. Now the pen was in her hand, and the choice was paper:
*★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — Laurent's letter:*
- **Answer honestly** — *Laurent+, risk shared.* Rose tells him what she knows — Voss & Hallett the funnel, the collector watching her, the de Valcourt margin — and asks what his family's bankers fear. He is warned and implicated in equal measure; the polish cracks further, and something truer shows beneath.
- **Answer lightly** — *Laurent neutral, protected.* Rose writes the bright, dismissive letter — Bath is dull, the waters undrinkable, do stop worrying — giving him deniability and herself distance. He hears the dismissal and seals the crack; the honest letter becomes a thing that happened once, and never again.
- **Don't answer yet** — *Information+, Laurent waiting.* Rose writes nothing — lets the silence do the work, lets the pressure declare itself before she commits a word. He waits, and worries, and the next letter — his — will tell her more than any reply of hers could.
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the decisiveness of the writing, or the deliberate folding-away of the blank page. The pen was laid down. The wax was cool. Whatever she had chosen, the choice was now paper — and paper, as Quill said, always tells the truth, because it does not know it is lying.)*
