He is warned and implicated in equal measure; the polish cracks further, and something truer shows beneath.

options.label: Answer lightly
options.detail: *Laurent neutral, protected.* Rose writes the bright, dismissive letter — Bath is dull, the waters undrinkable, do stop worrying — giving him deniability and herself distance. He hears the dismissal and seals the crack; the honest letter becomes a thing that happened once, and never again.

options.label: Don't answer yet
options.detail: *Information+, Laurent waiting.* Rose writes nothing — lets the silence do the work, lets the pressure declare itself before she commits a word. He waits, and worries, and the next letter — his — will tell her more than any reply of hers could.

scenes.synopsis: Texture — the letter posted (or held); the morning after the decision; Rose examines what she chose and finds no regret — yet. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> Morning. The post had gone — with her letter in it, or without it; the house would never know which, and that was the point.
> *(System: the breakfast room — Letitia, the Gazette, the toast; Rose, composed, the decision filed.)*
> (T1 · stance) *She takes her breakfast with the particular calm of a woman who has made a hard choice and means to live inside it.* — remembered: *the composure, performed or real.*
> (T2 · look closer) *She watches Letitia read the Gazette — the aunt's face giving nothing away, as usual, about whatever Bath is saying today.* — remembered: *the town's verdict, awaited.*
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *She replays the decision once — honestly, lightly, or not at all — and examines it for regret. None, yet. Regret, she is learning, arrives by the slow post.* — remembered: *the audit, clean.*
> (T4 · tone) *Letitia asks, with elaborate casualness, whether there was "any interesting post" — and Rose answers with exactly the right amount of nothing.* — remembered: *the aunt's curiosity, managed.*
> (T5 · social maneuver) *She turns the talk to the week's true business — the carriers, the collector, the London man who is watching her watch.* — remembered: *the campaign, resumed.*
> (T6 · look closer) *Out the window, Milsom Street goes about its banking business — and she thinks of Laurent's bankers, frightened and respectable, making inquiries about Bath.* — remembered: *the second front, open.*
> (T7 · stance) *She rises from the table — the letter dispatched or withheld, the choice made, the war continuing on two fronts now.* — remembered: *the general, at work.*
> Whatever the post carried, it carried her decision with it — or her deliberate silence, which was also a decision, and would also be read, by Laurent and by any collector who cared to read it.
> The morning room was quiet; the war, for once, was paper.

scenes.synopsis: Beat B6 — a London agent: a London house's man in Bath, watching Rose watch. The Pump Room sighting. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> She found him on the third day — or rather, she found the space where he had been, which is how one finds a man trained to be forgettable.
> *(System: the Pump Room, morning — the waters, the company, and, at the edge of it, a young man in a London-cut coat, neat, quiet, forgettable — exactly as Mrs. Trelawney had described him.)*
> He was not looking at her. That was the first thing she noticed — the discipline of it. Everyone in the Pump Room looked at everyone; it was the room's whole purpose. This man looked at the windows, at the water, at the musicians — everywhere, with equal and practiced indifference, except at the Hartwell girl in the grey dress.
> (T1 · look closer) *She studies him the way she studied the margin — peripherally, without seeming to; the London cut, the neatness, the forgettability, all present and correct.* — remembered: *the face, fixed.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *"Young. London-cut coat. Neat, quiet, forgettable." Mrs. Trelawney's description, confirmed in the flesh.* — remembered: *the quarry, found.*
> (T3 · stance) *She does not alter her behavior by a fraction — the waters are drunk, the gossip is heard, the grey dress is grey.* — remembered: *the performance, under observation.*
> She moved — slowly, by the aimless drift of Pump Room circulation — to the window beside him, and stood there a moment, looking out at the street, close enough to hear him order his water, close enough for him to know she was there.
> He did not turn his head. But his hand, lifting the glass, paused — a half-second's arrest, the stillness of a man who has been noticed noticing.
> (T4 · social maneuver) *She lets the pause hang — saying nothing, letting him understand that she knows.* — remembered: *the message, delivered.*
> (T5 · tone) *She remarks, to the room at large, "The waters are particularly — particular — this morning," and does not look at him.* — remembered: *the word, used as a signal.*
> (T6 · look closer) *She watches, in the window's reflection, his reaction to the word — the flicker, there and gone, like Augusta's at the de Valcourt name.* — remembered: *the tell, caught.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She files him whole — the face, the coat, the pause, the flicker — as the London end's man in Bath.* — remembered: *the agent, known.*
> (T8 · stance) *She drifts away, back into circulation — the grey dress, the grey girl, leaving him with the knowledge that the watched is watching.* — remembered: *the reversal, complete.*
> Behind her, she felt rather than saw him finish his water quickly and leave. The collector had been collected — noticed, named, and notified. The game, she thought, was now played in the open, or as open as such games ever got.

scenes.synopsis: The agent, considered — Rose turns him over: whose man, what errand, what use; the decision to test him forming. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> She did not follow him out. She finished her water, listened to a dowager's full account of a grandson's prospects, and thought — with the part of her mind that had once done affidavits — about the London man.
> *(System: the Pump Room, after — Rose thinking aloud to herself, the way generals do when the war council is one.)*
> Whose man? Voss's creature — Mrs. Trelawney had said so, and the wife's ledger had not lied yet. What errand? Her movements, her questions, her callers — two months of it. What use? That was the question. A watcher is only useful if the watched does something worth watching — or if the watcher can be made to report what the watched wants reported.
> (T1 · look closer) *She replays the window's reflection — the pause, the flicker at "particular" — and reads him again, more slowly.* — remembered: *the re-reading.*
> (T2 · social maneuver) *She considers the classic play: feed him a false trail — let him report movement that isn't movement, questions that aren't questions.* — remembered: *the option, priced.*
> (T3 · choice) *Or the direct play: confront him — a quiet word, a public place, "whose errand are you on?" — and watch him run to his master.* — remembered: *the option, priced.*
> (T4 · stance) *Or the patient play: ignore him entirely — let him watch an empty room, report nothing, and grow careless.* — remembered: *the option, priced.*
> Three plays. Each with its price, each with its yield. The false trail would cost her credibility if discovered; the confrontation would cost her the watcher; the patience would cost her time, and time was the one currency the season spent fastest.
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *She remembers Alder — the copying clerk, the false document, the trap that worked — and considers laying another.* — remembered: *the precedent.*
> (T6 · tone) *She says it aloud, softly, to the empty air of the retiring room: "Watching Rose watch." The phrase pleases her. It is the chapter's whole thesis in three words.* — remembered: *the thesis, named.*
> (T7 · look closer) *She checks the glass — the grey dress, the composed face; the woman in the mirror is ready to play whichever play she chooses.* — remembered: *the player, ready.*
> (T8 · social maneuver) *She decides: the test comes first — a dropped name, a watched reaction — and the play follows the test's result.* — remembered: *the sequence, set.*
> She rejoined the Pump Room's circulation with a fresh glass of water and the particular serenity of a woman who has just promoted herself from watched to watcher.

scenes.synopsis: Texture — the test: a dropped name at the Pump Room, watching who reacts; the agent's report, anticipated. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> The test was simple — the simplest tests always were. At the Pump Room the next morning, in the hearing of the right ears, Rose let fall a name.
> *(System: the Pump Room — the waters, the circulation, the London man at his usual remove, apparently absorbed in the musicians.)*
> "Mr. Quill writes," she said to Letitia — clearly, cheerfully, at exactly the volume that carried to the window — "that the de Valcourt papers are to be sent down to Bath for my inspection. Such a bother — a whole deed box, by the London coach, on Thursday."
> (T1 · social maneuver) *The name, dropped like a handkerchief — "de Valcourt papers," "deed box," "Thursday" — three lures in one sentence.* — remembered: *the bait, laid.*
> (T2 · tone) *Her cheer is perfect — the empty-headed heiress, chattering about solicitors' boxes.* — remembered: *the performance, pitched.*
> (T3 · look closer) *She watches, peripherally: the London man's hand on his glass — does it pause? In the window's reflection — does the flicker come?* — remembered: *the reaction, read.*
> It came. Not the hand — the hand was disciplined — but the stillness around the hand: the particular, total stillness of a man who has just heard the one thing he was sent to hear, and is deciding, very quickly, what to do about Thursday.
> (T4 · remembered micro-decision) *"Thursday." The London coach. A deed box that does not exist — she files his stillness as confirmation: the bait was taken.* — remembered: *the bite.*
> (T5 · social maneuver) *She lets Letitia chatter on — about boxes, about coaches, about the bother of it all — feeding the fiction its details.* — remembered: *the fiction, fed.*
> (T6 · look closer) *She notes who else heard — a dowager, a banker's wife, two young men; the fiction now has witnesses, which makes it real.* — remembered: *the audience, counted.*
> (T7 · stance) *She finishes her water and leaves, the grey dress unremarked — behind her, the London man is already, she would wager, composing his report.* — remembered: *the report, anticipated.*
> There was no deed box. There was no Thursday coach. There was only a name, dropped in the hearing of a watcher — and by Thursday, she would know, by what moved in Bath, exactly whose watcher he was.

scenes.synopsis: The agent moves — he posts a letter, London-bound; Rose has him followed (or follows the letter); the direction read. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> He moved that afternoon — quickly, for a forgettable man; the bait had done its work.
> *(System: Bath, afternoon — the post office in the High Street; the London man, no longer quite so forgettable in his haste, posting a sealed letter.)*
> Rose did not follow him herself — a grey dress is memorable when it hurries — but the chair-man she had paid that morning (a Bath man, discreet, with a memory for faces and a price for silence) followed the letter's posting and reported back: sealed, directed to London, and the direction — the chair-man had excellent eyes, and no scruples — read *Voss & Hallett, London.*
> (T1 · remembered micro-decision) *"Voss & Hallett, London." The direction, read and reported — the London end's name on the agent's letter.* — remembered: *the proof.*
> (T2 · look closer) *She pictures the letter traveling — Bath to London, the mail coach, the sealed parcels reversed: now she is the parcel, and London is reading her.* — remembered: *the reversal, complete.*
> (T3 · social maneuver) *She considers the letter's contents — her movements, her questions, the de Valcourt deed box that doesn't exist — and smiles.* — remembered: *what London will read.*
> (T4 · choice) *She paid the chair-man in coin and a warning — "You saw nothing, you followed no one" — buying silence the honest way.* — remembered: *the asset, secured.*
> The letter would reach London in two days. In two days, Voss & Hallett would read about a deed box coming down on Thursday — and would move, or not move, accordingly. And Rose, watching what moved, would learn the shape of the London end's anxiety.
> (T5 · stance) *She stands at the window, watching the High Street's traffic — the mail coach loading, the parcels, the sealed things going south.* — remembered: *the watcher, watching the watched's mail.*
> (T6 · tone) *She tells Letitia the whole of it, lightly — "Our London friend has written home" — and enjoys, briefly, the aunt's expression.* — remembered: *the war council, informed.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She files the chair-man's price and reliability — a Bath asset, for the weeks to come.* — remembered: *the network, building.*
> (T8 · social maneuver) *She decides the next play is now ripe — confront, feed, or ignore; the test has given her the grounds.* — remembered: *the decision, loading.*
> The trap — for that was what the dropped name had been, a smaller cousin of the false document that had caught Alder — had worked. The London man had bitten. Now came the question of what to do with a hooked fish.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE LONDON AGENT. The hooked fish: confront him, feed him a false trail, or ignore him. (Turns: 3 — the decision itself)
scenes.prose:
> Thursday came — and with it, no deed box, no London coach, nothing but an ordinary Bath morning and a London agent waiting, somewhere, for a box that would never arrive.
> *(The Pump Room, Thursday morning — the London man present, expectant under the forgettability; Rose, composed, the fiction's author.)*
> She watched him watch the door for the better part of an hour, and saw the moment he understood: there was no box. There had never been a box. The Hartwell girl had laid a name like bait, and he had risen to it, and reported it to London. He knew that she knew — and that was the hook, set deep. What she did with the hooked fish now — landed, released, or kept on the line:
*★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — The London agent:*
- **Confront him** — *Agent burned, message sent.* Rose speaks to him directly — quietly, publicly, finally: "Tell Voss that Miss Hartwell knows she is watched." He runs; London learns she is not prey. The watcher is lost, but the warning is delivered.
- **Feed him a false trail** — *Agent turned, unwitting.* Rose lets him keep watching — and carefully, over weeks, feeds him the movements and questions she wants London to read. He becomes her unwitting courier; every report he posts carries her fiction south.
- **Ignore him** — *Agent unworked, Rose patient.* Rose does nothing — lets him watch an empty room, report nothing, and grow careless. The watcher stays in place, unalerted; patience, priced against time.
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the word, the silence, or the long game begun. She made it the way she made all such decisions: in daylight, and without flinching.)*

options.label: Confront him
options.detail: *Agent burned, message sent.* Rose speaks to him directly — quietly, publicly, finally: "Tell Voss that Miss Hartwell knows she is watched." He runs; London learns she is not prey. The watcher is lost, but the warning is delivered.

options.label: Feed him a false trail
options.detail: *Agent turned, unwitting.* Rose lets him keep watching — and carefully, over weeks, feeds him the movements and questions she wants London to read. He becomes her unwitting courier; every report he posts carries her fiction south.

options.label: Ignore him
options.detail: *Agent unworked, Rose patient.* Rose does nothing — lets him watch an empty room, report nothing, and grow careless. The watcher stays in place, unalerted; patience, priced against time.

scenes.synopsis: Texture — the choice executed; the Pump Room after; Rose examines the play and the player. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> After — the Pump Room emptied of its particular tension, the waters drunk, the morning ordinary again — Rose sat a moment alone and examined what she had done.
> *(System: the retiring room — the glass, the grey dress, the woman who had just played a London agent like an instrument.)*
> (T1 · remembered micro-decision) *She replays the play — the dropped name, the stillness, the letter to Voss & Hallett, the empty Thursday — and audits it for cost.* — remembered: *the accounting.*
> (T2 · look closer) *She studies herself in the glass — not for vanity; for evidence. Does she look like a woman who lays traps in pump rooms? She does not. That is the point.* — remembered: *the disguise, holding.*
> (T3 · tone) *She says it aloud, to the empty room: "Watching Rose watch." It still pleases her — the chapter's thesis, in three words, now with a second verse.* — remembered: *the thesis, extended.*
> Whatever she had chosen — confrontation, false trail, or patience — the deeper truth held: she was no longer the watched. She was the watcher who had been watched watching, and had turned the watching inside out like a glove.
> (T4 · stance) *She straightens the grey dress — the armor of the forgettable, worn in a battle no one saw.* — remembered: *the uniform, honored.*
> (T5 · social maneuver) *She decides what Thursday's lesson buys her next: the carriers (Foale, Grimes — still to be found), the panorama (still to be seen), the masquerade (still, unheard, to come).* — remembered: *the campaign's next ground.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *She writes nothing down — some victories are safest in the head, where no collector can read them.* — remembered: *the discipline, again.*
> (T7 · look closer) *Out the window, Bath goes about its cure — and somewhere in it, a young London man is writing a very different report than the one he wrote on Tuesday.* — remembered: *the fiction, traveling south.*
> The Pump Room had been a battlefield. No one had bled. The only casualty was a fiction about a deed box — and fictions, Rose reflected, were the cheapest ammunition in London, and the most expensive to be hit by.

scenes.synopsis: Quill's letter arrives — the solicitor confirms the pattern: the London end's interest in the Hartwell estate is documented, deliberate, and personal. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> Quill's letter arrived with the Saturday post — London paper, the solicitor's clerkly hand, and the particular dryness of a man who has discovered something and intends to be thanked for it properly.
> *(System: the morning room — the letter, opened; Letitia, tactful again, with the novel right-side up this time, which meant she was actually reading.)*
> *My dear Miss Hartwell — I have made the inquiries you requested, and some you did not. The pattern is confirmed: Voss & Hallett's interest in the Hartwell mortgages is documented, deliberate, and — I must be frank — personal. They have acquired the Hartwell paper at terms that make no commercial sense, unless the commercial sense is not the point. Someone is buying your debts the way a collector buys paintings: not for the yield, but for the ownership.*
> (T1 · look closer) *She reads the phrase twice — "not for the yield, but for the ownership" — and feels the chapter's thesis turn its final key.* — remembered: *Quill's verdict.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *She sets Quill's letter beside Trelawney's confirmation, Mrs. Trelawney's warning, the margin's name — the pattern, from four independent witnesses.* — remembered: *the pattern, corroborated.*
> (T3 · stance) *She sits very straight — the solicitor's dry prose doing what all the Pump Room theater could not: making it official.* — remembered: *the formality, felt.*
> *There is more. The de Valcourt interest — you will forgive the phrase; it is theirs, not mine — has been consolidating English mortgages for eighteen months. Yours is the largest single holding. I do not know what they intend. I know what they have.*
> (T4 · tone) *"The de Valcourt interest" — the phrase, in a solicitor's hand, in London ink; the name is no longer a margin's whisper.* — remembered: *the name, now official.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *"Eighteen months." "The largest single holding." She does the arithmetic of exposure and does not like the sum.* — remembered: *the scale.*
> (T6 · look closer) *She studies Quill's signature — the clerkly flourish, the professional caution; he has told her everything he dares, in writing, which means he dares a great deal.* — remembered: *the solicitor's courage.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She considers what Quill wants — the thanks, properly expressed; the continued retainer; perhaps, like Trelawney, the feeling of being on the right side.* — remembered: *his price.*
> (T8 · stance) *She folds the letter into the workbox — beside Drummond's card, beside Laurent's letter, beside the whole growing archive of the war.* — remembered: *the archive, complete for now.*
> Four witnesses — the banker, the wife, the watcher, the solicitor — and one name, written in a margin, spoken in a Pump Room, printed in a solicitor's hand. The pattern was no longer a pattern. It was a portrait, and the face was nearly visible.

scenes.synopsis: The pattern, assembled — Rose lays out everything she knows, the full map of the money's roads; the general's briefing, to herself. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> That night she did what generals do before a campaign: she laid out the whole of it, in order, and looked at it entire.
> *(System: the writing desk, night — the workbox open, the papers spread: Drummond's card, the carrier names, Quill's letter, the memory of the margin.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *She arranges the papers in a line — Bath at one end, London at the other; the money's roads, drawn in documents.* — remembered: *the map, laid.*
> Paris: the émigré paper, born in exile and fear. Bath: Trelawney's discounting, the respectable front. The roads: Foale and Grimes, the carriers, the post-chaise parcel that never arrived. London: Voss & Hallett, the funnel, the watch-chain man's window, the young agent's reports.
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *She walks the line with her finger — Paris, Bath, the roads, London; every station confirmed, every handoff witnessed.* — remembered: *the chain, whole.*
> And behind London — behind Voss, behind the watch-chain, behind the margin — the name. De Valcourt. Written in ink. Spoken in a solicitor's letter. Eighteen months of buying, and hers the largest holding.
> (T3 · tone) *She says the name aloud, once, in the empty room — "de Valcourt" — and it sounds like a door closing.* — remembered: *the name, spoken.*
> (T4 · stance) *She sits back — the general, surveying the campaign map; the war has a shape now, and the shape has a name.* — remembered: *the commander's view.*
> What remains unknown: the face. The London end has a name, a funnel, an agent, a watch-chain — but not a face. A name without a face is a ghost; a face without a name is a stranger. She has the name. The face is the next campaign.
> (T5 · social maneuver) *She lists the unknowns — the face, the intention, the eighteen months' purpose — in order of urgency.* — remembered: *the gaps, ranked.*
> (T6 · look closer) *She looks at Drummond's card, last — the clerk's gift, the cheapest intelligence and the dearest; the whole war, in a way, began with a frightened clerk.* — remembered: *the origin.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She remembers S1's question — "Miss, do the Hartwell accounts balance?" — and answers it now, silently: *no. They never did. That was the point.** — remembered: *the first question, answered.*
> (T8 · tone) *She gathers the papers — not with triumph; with the quiet of a woman who has finished the reconnaissance and must now decide what the battle is.* — remembered: *the briefing, complete.*
> The map was whole. The roads were drawn. The name was written. All that remained was the face — and faces, she was learning, have a way of appearing exactly when you stop looking for them and start deserving them.

scenes.synopsis: Texture — Sunday: the Pump Room, the Crescent, Bath at worship and at play; the ordinary world continuing around the war. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> Sunday in Bath — the bells, the promenades, the waters drunk with particular piety — and Rose, who had spent the week at war, permitted herself a morning of ordinary life.
> *(System: the Pump Room, Sunday — the company at its most respectable; the London agent notably absent; the grey dress, present as always.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *She takes in the room — the dowagers, the beaux, the bankers' wives; the whole of Bath's respectable machinery, turning.* — remembered: *the town, at rest.*
> (T2 · stance) *She is, this morning, merely Miss Hartwell — an heiress, a beauty, a girl with a fortune and a future; the war packed away like a workbox.* — remembered: *the mask of ordinariness.*
> (T3 · tone) *She exchanges the Sunday civilities — the weather, the sermon, the waters — with the fluency of a native.* — remembered: *the performance, effortless now.*
> (T4 · remembered micro-decision) *She notes the agent's absence — the window where he stood, empty; whatever her choice did to him, it did it thoroughly.* — remembered: *the empty post.*
> (T5 · social maneuver) *She lets herself be seen — the grey dress in the Sunday light, the composed face; visibility, sometimes, is its own kind of armor.* — remembered: *the strategy of being seen.*
> (T6 · look closer) *Letitia, beside her, is genuinely happy — the teas, the company, the niece behaving beautifully; Rose loves her for it, fiercely, suddenly.* — remembered: *the aunt's joy.*
> (T7 · stance) *She takes Letitia's arm for the promenade — the war can wait an hour; the aunt cannot.* — remembered: *what matters, ranked.*
> The Crescent in Sunday sun, the town spread below like a ledger no one was auditing — and Rose, walking it with her aunt, allowed the general to rest and the girl to breathe. The war would keep. It always kept, and so would she.

scenes.synopsis: [F] occasion — the panorama dress: "a lady at leisure" walking dress for the great 360° painting; Rose and Élise choose fabrics with the London-that-is-coming in mind. Full choice depth — motif × colorway × thread × complete accessory set, via convergent choices. (Turns: 8 — the choosing + its wearing)
scenes.prose:
> Monday's plan was made over breakfast: the panorama — the great 360° painting of London, all lamplight and spires, newly arrived in Bath — and Élise, summoned to the lodgings, with her arms full of walking-dress possibilities.
> *(System: [F] occasion — the panorama outing: walking dress, "a lady at leisure"; the atelier's case open, the muslins and pelisses spread.)*
> (T1 · choice — the muslins) *Élise lays out three muslins — "For looking at London, mademoiselle. One must dress for the city one is about to — understand." A sprigged white, the sprigs in ivory whitework; a pale blue, pinstriped in silver thread; a grey-lavender, hemmed with a climbing fern in steel-grey embroidery. Three pastels, three motifs, three threads.* — remembered: *the occasion, framed.*
> (T2 · choice — the motif) *Rose touches each — the white too bridal, the blue too certain; the grey-lavender, like a London sky before rain, exactly right. The fern's depth: the full climbing spray in steel-grey, or the plainer hem edged in ivory whitework. She takes the fern, in steel.* — remembered: *the choice; the motif, decided.*
> (T3 · choice — the spencer) *"The lavender-grey," she says — "with the darker spencer. A lady at leisure — but a lady who is looking at something." The spencer's frogging: black silk, silver, or steel thread. "Steel," Rose says. "To match the fern."* — remembered: *the brief, set; the thread, chosen.*
> (T4 · choice — the bonnet) *"And the bonnet — the grey silk." The ribbon: lavender, pearl, or silver-grey. "Lavender," Rose says. "To match the sky I am wearing."* — remembered: *the ribbon's colorway.*
> (T5 · choice — the set) *The set, complete: grey kid gloves, plain; the reticule — lavender silk, large enough for a notebook ("For sketching the supply lines," Rose says, and Élise laughs, not understanding, which is perfect); small silver earrings, daytime-modest; the hair dressed soft, the bonnet's bow its only ornament.* — remembered: *the tools, packed.*
> (T6 · choice — the boots and shawl) *The boots — half-boots, grey, for the panorama's stairs; the shawl — a light wool, against the great painted city's imagined chill.* — remembered: *the practicalities.*
> (T7 · look closer) *The fitting — the dress pinned, the spencer settled, the fern climbing the hem in steel-grey; Rose in the glass, a lady at leisure, dressed to look at London.* — remembered: *the transformation.*
> (T8 · tone) *"Thursday," Élise says, gathering the muslins — "the panorama, the London-in-lamplight. You will see your city, mademoiselle." *My city,* Rose thinks. *The funnel's city. The margin's city.* "I can't wait," she says.* — remembered: *the appointment, kept.*
> The dress was ordered — lavender-grey, like a London sky, the fern climbing its hem in steel-grey thread. She would wear it to look at a painted London and think about the real one. Élise suspected nothing. That was the atelier's blessing: beauty, made innocently, worn to war.

scenes.synopsis: Texture — the week closes: calls, cards, the order queue; Rose's Bath life, running smoothly on the surface, the war underneath. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> The week closed as Bath weeks do — with calls paid, cards left, the order queue turning its honest ten slots, and the surface of Rose Hartwell's life running as smoothly as the Avon.
> *(System: the lodgings, week's end — the card tray, the order book, the quiet; the war, underneath, humming.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *She reviews the week's social accounts — the calls, the teas, the Pump Room mornings; every appearance made, every duty done.* — remembered: *the surface, maintained.*
> (T2 · social maneuver) *She checks the order queue — ten slots, turning; the free-income engine, honest and open, while the other ledger runs beneath it.* — remembered: *the two economies.*
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *She counts the week's intelligence yield — Trelawney, his wife, the agent, Quill, Laurent; five sources, one pattern.* — remembered: *the harvest.*
> (T4 · tone) *Letitia, settling the accounts, remarks that it has been "quite a satisfactory week" — and Rose agrees, with the serenity of a woman whose satisfactions are classified.* — remembered: *the aunt's verdict.*
> (T5 · stance) *She writes the week's private account — not in any book; in the head, where no collector reads.* — remembered: *the true ledger.*
> (T6 · look closer) *Out the window, the evening mail coach loads for London — carrying, among its parcels, whatever the agent reported, whatever Thursday taught.* — remembered: *the fiction, traveling.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *She decides the week's final act: tomorrow, the panorama — London in lamplight, the money's roads as supply lines; the next campaign's ground, surveyed.* — remembered: *the plan.*
> The surface: calls, cards, queues, teas. The underneath: ledgers, margins, agents, names. Rose Hartwell lived in both now, and moved between them the way other girls moved between rooms — without knocking, and without being seen to pass.
> The week was done; the next would begin with a painted London and the money's roads drawn like supply lines across it.

scenes.synopsis: The margin, revisited — Rose returns to Trelawney's ledger in memory and examines the name once more; the ink, the hand, the meaning. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> That night, unable to sleep, she returned — in memory, which was the only place she could return — to the counting-house, the ledger, the margin.
> *(System: the bedroom, night — the lamp low; Rose, wakeful, re-walking the counting-house in her mind.)*
> (T1 · remembered micro-decision) *She re-opens the ledger in her mind — the page, the entry, the margin; the name, written in ink, in a clerk's careful hand.* — remembered: *the page, revisited.*
> De Valcourt. Not a rumor — ink. Not gossip — a ledger entry's margin, where clerks write the things the columns cannot hold. Someone's name, kept beside the money, the way one keeps a knife beside the plate.
> (T2 · look closer) *She studies the remembered handwriting — careful, clerkly; not Trelawney's hand (too hurried), not a London hand (too neat); a clerk's hand, recording what he was told.* — remembered: *the hand, analyzed.*
> (T3 · tone) *She says it again, in the dark — "de Valcourt" — and this time it sounds less like a door closing and more like a door waiting to be opened.* — remembered: *the name, changing.*
> (T4 · remembered micro-decision) *She sets it beside Quill's letter — "the de Valcourt interest," in a solicitor's hand; beside the Pump Room — the name, dropped, the stillness; beside Voss & Hallett — the funnel, the watch-chain.* — remembered: *the name's four witnesses.*
> Ink. A solicitor's phrase. A watcher's stillness. A funnel's window. Four witnesses, and still no face — the name was everywhere now, and the man nowhere.
> (T5 · stance) *She sits up in the dark — the wakeful general, done with sleep; some questions are better asked of the ceiling.* — remembered: *the insomnia, useful.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *She asks the ceiling the real question: what does the de Valcourt interest want with Hartwell Park? Not the yield — Quill said so. The ownership. But ownership *for what*?* — remembered: *the unanswered question.*
> (T7 · look closer) *The lamp gutters — the margin's ink, the ceiling's plaster; for a moment they are the same color, the color of things written down.* — remembered: *the image.*
> (T8 · tone) *She lies back down — the name in the margin, in ink, in her head; tomorrow the panorama, the painted London, the supply lines. "One step nearer," she whispers, to no one.* — remembered: *the promise.*
> Sleep came eventually, the way it comes to generals before battles — late, light, and with the maps still spread behind the eyes. The margin's ink. The name. One step nearer.

scenes.synopsis: The Gazette sting — Bell's verdict on the week: "Miss Hartwell calls on bankers. The ton in Bath approves of heiresses who count." (Turns: 1 — the reading)
scenes.prose:
> The Gazette came with the Tuesday post — and Bath, reading it over breakfast, found Miss Hartwell in it again, in Bell's unmistakable voice.
> *(The breakfast room — the Gazette, open; Letitia reading aloud, with enjoyment; Rose, composed, reading between the lines.)*
> *"Miss Hartwell calls on bankers. The ton in Bath approves of heiresses who count."*
> (T1 · tone) *She hears Bell's voice in the sentence — the proprietor's dry amusement, the sting dressed as approval.* — remembered: *the verdict's flavor.*
> She studies the paragraph — two sentences, no more; Bell's economy, saying everything by saying little.
> *"Whether she counts coins or counts consequences, this paper declines to speculate. But the counting-houses of Milsom Street have had, of late, a most attentive visitor — and the visitors' book, we are told, does not lie."*
> "The visitors' book does not lie" — the warning inside the wit: Bell knows she was there, and wants her to know he knows. She wonders what Bell's sources are — the counting-house clerk? The Pump Room? The neat, quiet London man, before Thursday? Letitia declares it "perfectly delightful" — "the ton approves of heiresses who count!" — and Rose lets her enjoy it, because the aunt's delight is the verdict's intended surface. She folds the paper — the sting, taken; the approval, banked; the warning, filed. Bell's Gazette: judge and narrator, never hunter. Out the window, Milsom Street's counting-houses go about their business — attentive visitors and all.
> *"Miss Hartwell calls on bankers. The ton in Bath approves of heiresses who count."* She had called on bankers. She had counted — coins, consequences, and everything between. The ton approved. Bell, somewhere, was smiling. And the London end, reading the Gazette as it read everything, would note — as she had intended — exactly nothing it did not already know.
scenes.sting: Miss Hartwell calls on bankers. The ton in Bath approves of heiresses who count.

scenes.synopsis: Texture — the sting's aftermath: Bath's reaction; the bankers' wives, the dowagers, the beaux; Rose navigates the town's approval. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> The sting landed the way Bell's stings always landed — as approval that was also a warning, and Bath received it in both senses at once.
> *(System: the Pump Room, after the Gazette — the town, reading Rose through Bell's sentences; Rose, navigating.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *She feels the room's attention shift — the bankers' wives, nodding; the dowagers, approving; the beaux, recalculating.* — remembered: *the town's verdict, worn.*
> (T2 · tone) *"How delightful — an heiress who counts!" — the phrase, repeated back to her a dozen times, each repetition a small coronation.* — remembered: *the catchphrase.*
> (T3 · social maneuver) *She accepts the coronation gracefully — the counting heiress, the sensible girl; the mask of the ordinary, burnished by the Gazette itself.* — remembered: *the cover, deepened.*
> (T4 · remembered micro-decision) *She notes who repeats it most warmly — Mrs. Trelawney, beaming; the banker's wife, proud of her tea's guest.* — remembered: *the allies, visible.*
> (T5 · stance) *She deflects the deeper questions — "And what did the bankers tell you, Miss Hartwell?" — with the practiced ease of the grey dress.* — remembered: *the deflection.*
> (T6 · look closer) *Across the room — a new face. Or rather, a face she has seen before, in a window's reflection, on a London street: the watch-chain man. Older, heavier, the chain across the waistcoat unmistakable. In Bath.* — remembered: *the face, placed.*
> (T7 · tone) *Her heart does exactly one irregular beat — and then the training holds: she does not stare, does not start, does not alter the grey dress by a fraction.* — remembered: *the discipline, holding.*
> The watch-chain man. In the Pump Room. In Bath. The London end's window, walking — the face, one step nearer, exactly as the chapter promised. She finished her water, smiled at a dowager, and filed the sighting where it belonged: at the top of the war's new page.

scenes.synopsis: The London face, one step nearer — the watch-chain man in Bath; Rose watches him watch; the shape of the London end nearly visible. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> He did not stay long — a quarter-hour, perhaps; long enough to be seen, which, she understood at once, was the point.
> *(System: the Pump Room — the watch-chain man, circulating; Rose, circulating; the two of them, never once exchanging a glance.)*
> He moved through the room the way money moves through a funnel — quietly, inevitably, toward the center. The bankers knew him; she saw it in the nods, the half-bows, the particular deference Bath's money showed to London's. Trelawney himself — poor, careful Trelawney — went a shade paler and bowed a shade deeper than the occasion required.
> (T1 · look closer) *She studies him openly now — older, heavier, the watch-chain; the face that belongs to the window, the letter's direction, the funnel.* — remembered: *the face, at last.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *She sets him against everything she knows — Voss? Hallett? Neither name fits comfortably; he is the London end's man, but the London end's *face* is still behind him.* — remembered: *the face, not quite the face.*
> (T3 · stance) *She does not approach — the grey dress, the grey girl; some faces are best seen from a distance, before they know they are seen.* — remembered: *the discipline, again.*
> He paused, once, near the window — the same window where the young agent had stood — and looked out at the street with the air of a man checking that the world is where he left it. Then he turned, and for one unguarded second, his eyes found hers across the room.
> (T4 · tone) *The look — one second, unguarded; not surprise, not recognition; assessment. He was pricing her, the way she had priced the margin.* — remembered: *being priced.*
> (T5 · social maneuver) *She held the look — level, grey, unhurried; the author of Thursday, meeting the reader of the report.* — remembered: *the exchange.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *She understood, in that second: he knows about the deed box. He knows it was bait. He is here because the bait worked — because London, having been fished, has sent a bigger fish to look at the angler.* — remembered: *the escalation.*
> (T7 · look closer) *He looked away first — a quarter-bow, courteous, final — and left the Pump Room with the unhurried pace of a man who has seen what he came to see.* — remembered: *the departure.*
> (T8 · stance) *She finished her water — the grey dress, the composed face; inside, the general was already redrawing the map with a new piece on it.* — remembered: *the map, updated.*
> The London face — one step nearer. Not the face behind the face; not yet. But the funnel had sent its man to look at her, and he had looked, and she had looked back, and neither of them would forget it.

scenes.synopsis: THE CLIFFHANGER — the de Valcourt name in the margin, in ink; the London face one step nearer; the chapter's final image. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> That evening, alone, she took out a sheet of paper — and did what she had not permitted herself to do all week: she wrote the name down.
> *(System: the writing desk, night — the lamp, the pen, the blank page; the chapter's final image.)*
> *De Valcourt.* In ink. In her own hand. The name from the margin, copied from memory onto her own paper — the clerk's careful hand, reproduced in hers; the margin's secret, made her own.
> (T1 · look closer) *She studies what she has written — the name, in ink, in her hand; the margin's ghost, summoned onto her own page.* — remembered: *the transcription.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *She sets the paper beside Quill's letter — "the de Valcourt interest," in the solicitor's hand; beside the week's whole archive — the funnel, the agent, the watch-chain man, the bait, the report.* — remembered: *the archive, complete.*
> Outside, somewhere in Bath's lamplit streets, the watch-chain man was dining — or posting a letter — or simply being in Bath, which was itself a message. The London face, one step nearer. The name, in the margin, in ink. The two facts, side by side, like columns in a ledger that would not balance.
> (T3 · tone) *She looks at the name she has written — and understands, finally, what the chapter has been teaching her: the money has roads, and the roads have a destination, and the destination has a name.* — remembered: *the lesson, learned.*
> (T4 · stance) *She folds the paper and seals it — not with wax; with the decision that some things are safest carried, not filed.* — remembered: *the secret, kept close.*
> (T5 · look closer) *The lamp gutters out — the name, in ink, in the dark; the chapter's last image, held a moment before sleep.* — remembered: *the final image.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *Tomorrow: the panorama — London in lamplight, the money's roads drawn like supply lines; the painted city, and the real one behind it.* — remembered: *the next ground.*
> (T7 · stance) *She extinguishes the lamp herself — the general, dismissing the war council of one; the name kept, the face awaited, the campaign continuing.* — remembered: *the chapter, closed.*
> *De Valcourt.* In the margin, in ink. The London face, one step nearer. And Rose Hartwell — the girl who had called on bankers, and counted, and been approved by the ton for it — asleep at last, with the name under her pillow and the war in her dreams.

scenes.synopsis: Continuity — the name under her pillow; morning after Chapter 13; Rose wakes with the margin's ink still behind her eyes. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> She woke with the name still there — behind her eyes, where the lamp had left it: *de Valcourt*, in ink, in her own hand, folded and sealed and slipped under her pillow like a girl's keepsake that was nothing of the kind.
> *(System: the bedroom, morning — the sealed paper under the pillow; Bath's bells; the panorama day ahead.)*
> (T1 · remembered micro-decision) *She touches the paper under the pillow — still there, still sealed; the margin's ghost, kept close.* — remembered: *the secret, carried.*
> (T2 · look closer) *The morning light does what lamplight could not — makes the name ordinary, ink on paper, a fact among facts.* — remembered: *the daylight test.*
> (T3 · stance) *She rises — the general, rested; the panorama today, the painted London, the supply lines to be drawn.* — remembered: *the campaign's next ground.*
> (T4 · tone) *She says it once more, aloud, to the empty room — "de Valcourt" — and it sounds, in daylight, like a question she intends to answer.* — remembered: *the name, as a question.*
> (T5 · social maneuver) *She decides the paper stays under the pillow — some intelligence is safest where no collector thinks to look: in a girl's bedroom, under a girl's pillow.* — remembered: *the hiding place.*
> (T6 · look closer) *In the glass — the lavender-grey walking dress waiting, Élise's work; a lady at leisure, dressed to look at London.* — remembered: *the uniform for today.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She remembers the watch-chain man's quarter-bow — the assessment, the pricing; today she will price him back, in paint and lamplight.* — remembered: *the return match.*
> She dressed slowly, the way she did everything now — with attention as a form of armor. The maid's hands, the tapes, the pins; the ordinary sacraments of a Bath morning, performed over an extraordinary secret. Outside, the street was already busy with chair-men and water-drinkers, the town beginning its daily performance of health.
> The name went back under the pillow. The dress went on. And Rose Hartwell went down to breakfast with the particular serenity of a woman carrying a secret so close it had become part of her posture.

scenes.synopsis: Texture — breakfast; Letitia's excitement about the panorama; the aunt sees pretty lights, and Rose loves her for it. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> "The panorama!" Letitia was at her most radiant — the novel abandoned, the Gazette unread, the whole of her attention fixed on the day's pleasure. "A whole London, Rose — painted round a room, in lamplight! They say you can see the spires!"
> (T1 · tone) *Rose lets the aunt's delight wash over her — uncomplicated, unfeigned; the purest thing in the lodgings.* — remembered: *the joy, witnessed.*
> (T2 · look closer) *She studies Letitia — the bright eyes, the plans for the afternoon; the woman sees pretty lights, and nothing else, and Rose loves her for it.* — remembered: *the love, fierce and sudden.*
> (T3 · stance) *She does not correct, does not complicate — the aunt's panorama will be lamplight and spires, and that is  exactly as it should be — the pretty lights, protected. That was the whole of the war, really, in miniature — the pretty lights, kept pretty, whatever it cost. Letitia hummed on, oblivious and radiant.* — remembered: *the protection.*
> (T4 · social maneuver) *She steers the talk — the bonnet, the shawl, the stairs; practicalities, keeping the day light.* — remembered: *the care.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *She remembers every time Letitia has asked no questions — the upside-down novel, the tactful teas — and understands the aunt knows more than she lets on, and loves her more for the letting.* — remembered: *the aunt's own discretion.*
> (T6 · tone) *"We shall see the spires," Rose promises — and means it; whatever else she sees in the painted London, Letitia will see spires.* — remembered: *the promise.*
> (T7 · look closer) *Out the window, Bath in morning sun — the real city, waiting; the painted one, an hour away.* — remembered: *the two cities.*
> The toast was buttered, the tea poured, the morning proceeding with the well-oiled smoothness of a household that has performed it a thousand times. Letitia had already decided which bonnet, which shawl, which gloves — the small liturgies of an outing, observed with complete seriousness. Rose watched her, and felt the war recede to its proper distance: not gone, but waiting, the way a sword waits in its scabbard.
> Letitia swept off to dress, humming. Rose finished her tea alone, and thought: *she sees only pretty lights. Thank God. Someone in this house should get to see only pretty lights.* The fierceness of the love surprised her — and then it didn't. It was the whole reason for the war.

scenes.synopsis: [F] occasion — dressing for the panorama: the lavender-grey walking dress goes on; Élise's final touches; "a lady at leisure." Full choice depth — the motif and thread decided at the choosing, worn; the accessory set completed with Élise's final options. (Turns: 8 — the choosing + its wearing)
scenes.prose:
> Élise arrived with the dress itself — the lavender-grey muslin, the darker spencer, the grey silk bonnet with its lavender ribbon — and the air of a general delivering ordnance.
> *(System: [F] occasion — the panorama: walking dress, "a lady at leisure"; the final fitting, the accessories chosen.)*
> (T1 · choice — the fabric) *The muslin goes on — lavender-grey, like a London sky before rain; and climbing the hem, the fern in steel-grey embroidery — Monday's motif, now alive on the fabric. The drape, the fall, exactly as Élise promised.* — remembered: *the fabric, the motif, worn.*
> (T2 · choice — the colorway) *The spencer — darker grey-lavender, fitted, the frogging in steel thread to match the fern; the silhouette, a lady at leisure, a lady who is looking at something.* — remembered: *the line, the thread, worn.*
> (T3 · choice — the bonnet) *The bonnet — grey silk, lavender ribbon; Élise ties it herself, the bow precise as a signature.* — remembered: *the crown.*
> (T4 · choice — the final options) *The final options — Élise's instinct for the last detail: the earrings, small silver drops or tiny pearls ("Drops," Rose decides — silver, to answer the thread); the hair, a braided coronet or soft curls under the bonnet ("Curls" — the coronet is for evenings). The gloves — grey kid, plain; the reticule — lavender silk, the notebook inside. "For the supply lines," Rose says, and Élise, pinning, does not ask.* — remembered: *the final choices, made.*
> (T5 · look closer) *The glass — Rose, complete; the walking dress, the bonnet, the silver drops, the composed face; a lady at leisure, armed for observation.* — remembered: *the transformation.*
> (T6 · tone) *Élise steps back, critical — then nods. "You will see your city, mademoiselle." The funnel's city, Rose thinks. "I intend to," she says.* — remembered: *the exchange.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She remembers the wallpaper ritual — "be the wallpaper" — and understands today's dress is the opposite: not wallpaper, but a window.* — remembered: *the reversal.*
> (T8 · stance) *She takes up the reticule — the notebook, the pencil; the general's instruments, in lavender silk.* — remembered: *the readiness.*
> Élise fussed once more with the bonnet's ribbon, tweaked the spencer's collar, and stood back with the critical eye of an artist releasing a work into the world. "A lady at leisure," she pronounced, "who is looking at *something*." The emphasis was slight, and conspiratorial, and Rose laughed — the atelier suspected nothing and understood everything, which was exactly the arrangement she required.
> The dress was on. The bonnet was tied. And Rose Hartwell — a lady at leisure, in lavender-grey, the fern climbing her hem in steel — went down to join her aunt, carrying a notebook in her reticule and a war in her head, and no one, looking at her, would have guessed which was heavier.

scenes.synopsis: Arrival — the panorama building; the ascent; the first sight of the 360° London in lamplight and spires. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> The panorama building rose on its street like a temple to looking — round, windowless, promising everything; and inside, up the dark stair, the promise was kept all at once.
> *(System: the panorama — the ascent, the dark stair; then the viewing platform, and London, all around.)*
> She came out onto the platform — and London was there. All of it. Three hundred and sixty degrees of it: the lamplight, the spires, the river's black ribbon, the rooftops running to the horizon like a ledger's ruled lines. Painted, but the scale defeated disbelief — you did not look *at* it; you stood *in* it.
> (T1 · look closer) *She turns slowly — the full circle, the lamplight, the spires; London, surrounding her, painted but present.* — remembered: *the immersion.*
> (T2 · tone) *Letitia gasps — "Oh! Oh, the lights!" — and clutches Rose's arm; the pretty lights, exactly as promised.* — remembered: *the aunt's delight, delivered.*
> (T3 · stance) *Rose stands very still — the general, arrived on the high ground; the whole of the enemy's country, spread below.* — remembered: *the vantage.*
> (T4 · remembered micro-decision) *She finds the river — the black ribbon; somewhere along it, the City, the counting-houses, Voss & Hallett's window.* — remembered: *the funnel, placed.*
> (T5 · look closer) *She traces the rooftops — the ruled lines, running out; the money's roads, she thinks, run under these roofs like veins.* — remembered: *the roads, imagined.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *She steadies her breathing — the lady at leisure does not stare like a surveyor; she will look the way the ritual taught her.* — remembered: *the discipline, ready.*
> (T7 · tone) *A gentleman nearby remarks on the painting's accuracy — she answers with the empty pleasantries of a lady at leisure, and means them, for once.* — remembered: *the ease.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She thinks of the margin — the name, in ink, under her pillow; the painted city before her, the real one behind the name.* — remembered: *the two cities, overlaid.*
> London in lamplight and spires — all around her, above her, below. She had come to see a painting. She was seeing, instead, the shape of everything: the money's roads, drawn in lamplight, like a general's supply lines on a campaign map.

scenes.synopsis: ★ DRESSING RITUAL — "A Lady at Leisure": the panorama promenade. 20 micro-decisions on how Rose conducts the outing — gaze, pace, conversation, sketching — 5 coins each, 100 coins. (Turns: 20 — the ritual's pins)
scenes.prose:
> *(System: [C] ritual — the panorama outing. The player commits to a direction for the promenade — remembered through the chapter. Then the pins begin. Each pin costs 5 coins from play earnings; no Crown SKUs touch the ritual. Jewels come from owned pieces only — the jewel shelf is always open but never a ritual step; owned pieces enter as ordinary options with no scoring edge.)*
> Élise's parting instruction, pinned to the reticule: *"Chérie — today you are not the wallpaper. Today you are the window: everyone looks through you at the view, and no one sees the looking."*
> The promenade round the platform — the full 360 degrees, taken slowly — is the ritual: twenty small decisions about how a lady at leisure looks at London, each one a choice of gaze, pace, and company.
> **Pin 1 (T1 · micro-decision) — The first gaze:** the long, slow turn — taking the whole circle before fixing on any part. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 2 (T2 · micro-decision) — The pace:** unhurried — the platform circled at a stroll, never a march. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 3 (T3 · micro-decision) — The spires:** the dutiful admiration — "Oh, the spires!" — for Letitia's benefit and the company's. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 4 (T4 · micro-decision) — The lamplight:** the pause where the painted lamps cluster thickest — letting the light do the looking. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 5 (T5 · micro-decision) — The river:** the lingering at the black ribbon — the Thames, the trade, the thought of what floats on it. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 6 (T6 · micro-decision) — The sketch:** the notebook opened — a skyline study, innocent; the map hidden inside the drawing. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 7 (T7 · micro-decision) — The pencil:** the choice of what to draw first — the spires (for the company), the rooftops (for the war). *5 coins.*
> **Pin 8 (T8 · micro-decision) — The conversation:** the gentleman's remark on accuracy — answered with pleasant emptiness, the lady at leisure. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 9 (T9 · micro-decision) — The dowager:** the older lady's reminiscences of London — heard with flattering attention, mined for nothing, enjoyed for itself. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 10 (T10 · micro-decision) — The second circuit:** the round begun again — slower this time; the ritual's heart, the repeated looking. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 11 (T11 · micro-decision) — The City quarter:** the gaze settling where the painted counting-houses stand — the funnel's neighborhood, noted. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 (T12 · micro-decision) — The annotation:** the tiny mark in the notebook's margin — *V&H*, in pencil, beside the painted rooftops. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 13 (T13 · micro-decision) — The bridges:** the counting of crossings — the money's roads need bridges; she counts them like rosary beads. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 (T14 · micro-decision) — The rest:** the pause at the platform's rail — the lady at leisure, resting; the general, thinking. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 (T15 · micro-decision) — The aunt:** the turning back to Letitia — "Which spire is tallest, do you think?" — the pretty lights, shared. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 16 (T16 · micro-decision) — The laugh:** the genuine laugh at Letitia's answer — unguarded, unperformed; the ritual allows one true thing. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 17 (T17 · micro-decision) — The last look:** the final slow turn — the whole circle, committed to memory; the campaign map, photographed by the eyes. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 (T18 · micro-decision) — The closing of the book:** the notebook shut — the map complete, the skyline innocent; the lady at leisure, her leisure concluded. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 19 (T19 · micro-decision) — The descent:** the dark stair, taken carefully — the bonnet, the reticule, the composure, all intact. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 20 (T20 · micro-decision) — The daylight:** the emergence — blinking in the sun, the painted London behind her, the real one ahead; the window, become a girl again. *5 coins.*
> *(System: 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins drawn from play earnings. The completed direction is remembered — the chapter's outings will react to it. Owned jewels may be added freely from the open shelf at any point, never as a step. Reveal coda: the mirror moment — Rose, a lady at leisure, and the look saved to the season lookbook.)*

scenes.synopsis: The mapping — under the ritual's cover, Rose draws the money's roads onto the painted London: Paris, Bath, the carriers, Voss & Hallett; supply lines on a campaign map. (Turns: 9)
scenes.prose:
> The notebook filled — page after page, the pencil moving while the lady at leisure smiled at the spires, exactly as the ritual had rehearsed.
> First: Paris — she marked it in the margin of the page, the way the clerk had marked the margin of the ledger; the émigré paper, born in exile. An arrow, east to west, across the painted Channel.
> (T1 · social maneuver) *The Paris mark — the origin, placed; the arrow, drawn; the first supply line.* — remembered: *the source.*
> Then Bath — the crescents, the Pump Room, Trelawney's counting-house; the discounting front, respectable and grey. Another arrow, Bath to London, along the mail-coach road.
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *The Bath mark — Trelawney, the carriers Foale and Grimes, the post-chaise parcel; the road, drawn.* — remembered: *the front.*
> Then the carriers' road itself — she drew it dotted, uncertain; Foale and Grimes, still to be found, still to be questioned. The dotted line of the not-yet-known.
> (T3 · look closer) *The dotted line — the gap in the map, honestly marked; a general marks what she does not know.* — remembered: *the gap.*
> Then London — the City, the funnel; Voss & Hallett's window, the watch-chain, the young agent's reports. She drew the funnel as a funnel — wide at Bath, narrow at the window.
> (T4 · social maneuver) *The funnel, drawn — the money narrowing toward the window, toward the face behind the face.* — remembered: *the destination.*
> And behind it all — behind the funnel, behind the window — the name. She wrote it small, in the corner of the page: *de Valcourt.* The destination's name, on the campaign map.
> (T5 · tone) *The name, written small — not shouted; mapped. A general does not shout at the map.* — remembered: *the discipline.*
> (T6 · look closer) *She surveys the page — Paris, Bath, the dotted road, the funnel, the name; the money's roads, like supply lines.* — remembered: *the whole.*

scenes.synopsis: Octavia's gossip, placed — the émigré-sitter intelligence finds its spot on the map; a name, a house, a road confirmed. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:

> *(System: the viewing platform — Rose walking the circle again; Octavia's words, remembered, placed.)*
> Octavia — at whose tea, weeks ago, the émigré-sitter had talked: the Frenchwoman who sat for the miniature-painter, who had spoken of Paris paper, of men who carried things between cities, of a house in London where such men were paid. Gossip, at the time — the sitter's chatter, the tea-table's currency. But now, on the map, it had coordinates.
> (T1 · remembered micro-decision) *She replays the sitter's chatter — Paris paper, the carriers, the London house where men were paid.* — remembered: *the gossip, recalled.*
> (T2 · social maneuver) *She places it — the London house, on the painted City; the carriers' dotted road, ending there. The gossip has coordinates now.* — remembered: *the placement.*

scenes.synopsis: Texture — the descent; the panorama's shop; Letitia buys a print of the spires; Rose buys a map of London. (Turns: 7)

> *(System: the shop — prints, maps, souvenirs; Letitia, delighted; Rose, purposeful.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *Letitia chooses — a print of the spires, seventeen of them, for the lodgings' wall; the pretty lights, to keep.* — remembered: *the aunt's souvenir.*
> (T2 · social maneuver) *Rose chooses — a map of London. A real one. Streets, bridges, the City marked. "For my correspondence," she says. The shopkeeper does not blink.* — remembered: *the general's purchase.*
> (T3 · tone) *Letitia teases — "Corresponding with London now?" — and Rose laughs, and lets the tease stand, because the truth is stranger.* — remembered: *the cover, easy.*
> (T4 · remembered micro-decision) *She remembers the notebook — the pencil map, the funnel, the name; the real map will anchor it.* — remembered: *the pairing.*

Twice they were stopped by acquaintances, twice the panorama was praised, twice Rose performed the lady at leisure with increasing fluency. The performance was becoming a second skin — which was, she reflected, either a triumph of discipline or a warning.
> Two purchases: a print of spires, for the wall; a map of London, for the war. Letitia carried the pretty lights home. Rose carried the supply lines. Each, in her way, had gotten exactly what she came for — and neither suspected, as they walked, how precisely the day had served them both.

scenes.synopsis: The masquerade, rumored — talk of a subscription masquerade at the Assembly Rooms; "everyone" will be there; Rose considers what a mask could do. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> It began, as Bath things do, as talk — at the Pump Room the next morning, in the mouths of three separate dowagers, which meant it was true: a subscription masquerade, at the Assembly Rooms, within the fortnight. Masks, dominos, midnight unmasking by custom — and, the dowagers agreed, *everyone* would be there.
> *(System: the Pump Room — the rumor, circulating; Rose, listening the way the ritual taught her.)*
> (T1 · remembered micro-decision) *She catches it from the first dowager — "a masquerade, my dear, subscription" — and files it before the sentence ends.* — remembered: *the rumor, caught.*
> (T2 · tone) *The second dowager adds the detail that matters — "everyone in the money will be there" — said lightly, meaning heavily.* — remembered: *the guest list, implied.*
> Everyone in the money. The phrase sat in her head like a coin dropped in a fountain. Everyone in the money — the bankers, the London men, the watch-chain's whole circulating library of faces — all in masks, all unguarded, all talking.
> (T3 · social maneuver) *She does the arithmetic — masked men, talking freely; the funnel's people, unguarded; what the ton says when it thinks Rose is not there.* — remembered: *the opportunity, priced.*
> (T4 · look closer) *She watches the room discuss it — the excitement, the plans; Bath, preparing to be someone else for a night.* — remembered: *the town, anticipating.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *She remembers the thesis — "hear what the ton says when they think Rose is not there" — the masquerade is the instrument, custom-built.* — remembered: *the purpose, named.*
> (T6 · stance) *She considers her approaches — masked and listening; open and watching; or Letitia, sent as ears, while Rose stays home and innocent.* — remembered: *the options, loading.*
> (T7 · tone) *Letitia is ecstatic — "A masquerade! Oh, Rose!" — the pretty lights, about to get prettier.* — remembered: *the aunt's joy.*
> (T8 · social maneuver) *She decides nothing yet — the decision wants the desk, the night, the general's full briefing; but the shape of it is already forming.* — remembered: *the deferral, deliberate.*
> A subscription masquerade. Masks. Midnight. Everyone in the money. She finished her water, smiled at the dowagers, and felt the familiar click of a campaign's next ground locking into place — the way the panorama's platform had clicked under her boots.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE MASQUERADE. At the writing desk: go masked and listen, go openly, or send Letitia as ears. (Turns: 3 — the decision itself)
scenes.prose:
> Night — the desk, the lamp, the rumor laid out like a map beside the money's roads; the masquerade, considered as a military problem.
> *(The writing desk — the decision; three approaches, each with its price.)*
> The rumor was memorized: subscription, Assembly Rooms, masks, midnight, everyone in the money. Three approaches, each weighed — the masked listener, unrecognizable, hearing what men say when Rose is not there; the open watcher, herself, hiding in plain sight; the aunt as ears, innocent and beloved, and unguarded among the money. Out the window, the Assembly Rooms stood dark — in a fortnight, lamplit, masked, full of the money:
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The masquerade:*
- **Go masked and listen** — *Intelligence+, risk personal.* Rose attends in domino and mask, unrecognizable — hearing what the ton says when it thinks she is not there. The boldest play; the mask is the instrument.
- **Go openly** — *Safety+, intelligence thin.* Rose attends as herself — watching openly, dancing, being seen. Nothing will be said in her hearing, but everything will be seen; the honest spy.
- **Send Letitia as ears** — *Letitia risked, Rose clean.* Letitia goes masked, briefed and beloved, while Rose stays home — innocent, deniable. The aunt hears what no one guards against; but the aunt is unguarded too.
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the decisiveness of a woman who has made masked decisions before, in pump rooms and counting-houses. Whatever she had chosen, the masquerade was now a campaign with a plan.)*

> The rest of the morning went to practicalities — the subscription list to be found, the Assembly Rooms' arrangements to be learned, the question of who was supplying masks (London, said the dowagers; Paris, said the fitter's gossip). Rose made her notes in the lavender reticule's notebook, on the page facing the money's map — the masquerade's plan, confronting the money's roads. Two campaigns, one notebook. It felt right.
> The practical shape: a letter to Élise, a subscription to take, a fortnight of preparation. Whatever she had chosen, the machinery was moving — and Rose, who had once been the watched, was becoming the woman who chose her own disguises.  It was, she thought, the difference between hiding and hunting — and she had chosen hunting. The difference mattered, and the choosing mattered more.

scenes.synopsis: Julian's letter arrives — debts paid, name cleared, no thanks asked; the honorable suitor's settlement. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> The letter was waiting with the afternoon post — London postmark, Julian's hand, and a weight to the paper that suggested enclosures.
> *(System: the lodgings, afternoon — the letter, opened; Letitia tactfully with the spire print; Rose, alone with it.)*
> *My dear Miss Hartwell — The debts are paid. The name is cleared. What was owed — to you, to the estate, to the whole unhappy business — is settled, and I write not to claim thanks but to decline it in advance: no thanks asked, none wanted. You did what honor required when honor was expensive. I have done what honor required now that it is merely costly.*
> (T1 · tone) *She reads it twice — the honor, the expense; Julian's particular music, pride tuned to generosity.* — remembered: *the letter's note.*
> (T2 · look closer) *She studies the enclosures — the settled accounts, the cleared name, in clerks' hands; the proof, not the promise.* — remembered: *the evidence.*
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *She remembers what the debts cost him — the London season, the whispers, the price of honor when it was expensive.* — remembered: *the cost.*
> *"Do not mistake this for a farewell. It is a settlement. What comes next — if anything comes next — will be built on cleared ground, or not built at all. Yours, in honor, Julian."*
> (T4 · stance) *"Not a farewell. A settlement." She sits very still — the honorable suitor, refusing both debt and gratitude in a single stroke.* — remembered: *the maneuver.*
> (T5 · tone) *"No thanks asked" — and yet the whole letter is a kind of asking: *see me clearly.* She sees him. Clearly.* — remembered: *the ask, understood.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *She considers what the cleared name means for the war — Julian's debts, settled; one less lever for the London end to pull.* — remembered: *the strategic yield.*
> (T7 · look closer) *She holds the letter to the light — London paper, honest ink; no polish, no crack; the opposite of Laurent's letter in every way.* — remembered: *the contrast.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She files it with the archive — beside Laurent's strained polish, beside Quill's dry confirmation; the suitors' letters, each a different kind of truth.* — remembered: *the collection.*
> Debts paid. Name cleared. No thanks asked. Julian — honorable to the last, and past the last — had settled his accounts and laid the cleared ground before her like a duelist laying down his pistol: *what comes next is your choice.* The settlement was complete. The choice was loading.

scenes.synopsis: The letter, considered — Rose turns Julian's settlement over; what answering would mean, and what silence would mean. (Turns: 8)

> She did not answer at once — the masquerade's plan still fresh, the map still spread in her head; Julian's letter had to find its place among them.
> *(System: the evening — the letter re-read; the map, the archive; Rose, deciding what the letter is.)*
> What was it? A settlement — he said so. A farewell — he denied it. An asking — "see me clearly" — disguised as a refusal to be thanked. Three things at once, like everything Julian did: honor, pride, and underneath, the thing he would never name.
> (T1 · tone) *She names the underneath thing, silently — *he is still in the field.* The settlement settled the debts, not the man.* — remembered: *the reading.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *She remembers his season — the friendship, the honor, the expensive choices; the suitor who behaved honorably because he was honorable.* — remembered: *the record.*
> (T3 · social maneuver) *She weighs the warm answer — gratitude, openness, the cleared ground acknowledged; what it would build, and what it would cost.* — remembered: *the option.*
> (T4 · choice) *She weighs the careful answer — thanks, measured; warmth, rationed; the door neither opened nor closed.* — remembered: *the option.*
> (T5 · stance) *She weighs the distance — no answer, or the briefest; the settlement accepted in silence; the field, left fallow.* — remembered: *the option.*
> (T6 · look closer) *She looks at the enclosures again — the cleared name, in clerks' hands; whatever she writes, the facts are settled. Only the tone is hers to choose.* — remembered: *what is fixed, and what is free.*
> (T7 · tone) *She says his name aloud — "Julian" — and it sounds like cleared ground: solid, quiet, waiting.* — remembered: *the sound.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She sets the letter aside — the answer will come, but tonight is for the map; the suitor can wait one night for the general.* — remembered: *the deferral.*
> Three answers — warm, careful, distant — each honorable, each with its price. The debts were settled. The name was cleared. What remained was the only thing Julian had ever actually asked for, without asking: to be seen clearly. Tomorrow, she would decide how clearly to see him back.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — JULIAN'S LETTER. At the writing desk: answer warmly, answer carefully, or keep distance. (Turns: 3 — the decision itself)
scenes.prose:
> Morning — the desk laid, the pen ready, Julian's letter open beside the blank page; the cleared ground, waiting for her to build on it or leave it fallow.
> *(The writing desk — the decision; the three answers, each honorable.)*
> She had re-read the last line — "built on cleared ground, or not built at all" — and weighed what warmth would give him against what it would cost her, what careful thanks would ration, what silence would settle. Three honorable answers, one pen:
*★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — Julian's letter:*
- **Answer warmly** — *Julian+, door open.* Rose writes with genuine warmth — gratitude, admiration, the cleared ground acknowledged and welcomed. He is seen clearly, as he asked; the friendship deepens toward something more, built on settled accounts.
- **Answer carefully** — *Julian neutral, door ajar.* Rose writes with measured thanks — warm but rationed, the door neither opened nor closed. He is respected, kept at the honorable distance; the field lies fallow, for now.
- **Keep distance** — *Julian-, settlement accepted.* Rose writes briefly or not at all — the settlement accepted in silence. He understands: the debts are settled, the story is closed; honor, satisfied, asks nothing more.
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the tone she chose, the decisiveness of the writing or the folding-away. The pen was laid down. Whatever she had written — warmth, care, or distance — it was honorable, because he had been honorable.)*

scenes.prose:
> Morning — the post gone, with her letter or without it; two decisions made, the third still ahead, the week half-spent.
> *(System: the breakfast room — the calm after choosing; Letitia, the Gazette; Rose, the general between campaigns.)*
> (T1 · stance) *She takes breakfast with the composure of a woman current on all her correspondence — the masquerade planned, Julian answered.* — remembered: *the accounts, settled.*
> (T2 · remembered micro-decision) *She audits neither decision for regret — regret arrives by the slow post; for now, the choices hold.* — remembered: *the discipline.*
> (T3 · look closer) *Letitia reads the Gazette's fashion column aloud — the masquerade, anticipated in print; the town, preparing.* — remembered: *the public countdown.*
> (T4 · tone) *Rose answers the aunt's questions about dominos with the ease of a woman whose plans are made.* — remembered: *the cover, comfortable.*
> (T5 · social maneuver) *She turns her mind to the third decision waiting — Cecilia, the lodgings, the London men; the surveillance, to be decided.* — remembered: *the next ground.*
> (T6 · look closer) *Out the window, Bath goes about its morning — and somewhere in it, Cecilia's lodgings, with their stream of London visitors.* — remembered: *the watch, resuming.*
> (T7 · stance) *She rises — two campaigns decided, the third loading; the week, half-spent, well-spent.* — remembered: *the momentum.*
> She spent the late morning on correspondence — the atelier's letter answered, the order queue's commissions advanced, a note to Octavia (the sitter's intelligence, to be pursued gently). The pen moved, the sand dried, the seals were pressed. Ordinary letters, carrying extraordinary purposes — the season's whole method in miniature. By noon the desk was clear, the decisions were paper (or deliberate silence), and the third front waited.
> The masquerade: planned. Julian: answered. What remained was Cecilia — the rival, the seller of secrets, the lodgings with their London men. Rose finished her tea, and turned her attention — the way a general turns a map — to the third front.  The week was half-spent, and the spending had been worth it. Three fronts, three decisions, one map. The week's work, standing like milestones behind her.

> *(System: the lodgings — the report, delivered; Rose, listening; the rival's trade, quantified.)*
> Cecilia's lodgings — watched, these three days, at Rose's instruction. The visitors: London men, mostly. Young, neat, forgettable — the same cut as the Pump Room agent. They came singly, stayed an hour, left with parcels — papers, by the look; and left coin behind, by the sound.

> (T2 · look closer) *She pictures it — Cecilia's parlor, the London men, the papers changing hands; the rival, selling what Rose is trying to buy back.* — remembered: *the scene, imagined.*
> (T3 · tone) *The chair-man adds the detail that matters — "They're the same lot, miss. Same cut o' coat. London lot." The funnel's errand boys, buying secrets retail.* — remembered: *the identification.*
> (T4 · social maneuver) *She pays him — coin, and the warning renewed; the asset, kept.* — remembered: *the network, maintained.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *She sets it against the map — the London house where men were paid; Cecilia's lodgings, where men pay. Two ends of the same road.* — remembered: *the placement.*
