scenes.synopsis: open from L17's cliffhanger — morning; Augusta's "later" in hand; the Network knows; today, the answer. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> Morning. Augusta's letter on the breakfast table — the "later," the inventory, the warning — and Rose, reading it once more before the day began.
> *(The lodgings; the letter; the decision, already made last night: conduct, not correspondence.)*
> The Network knew she had mapped it. Drummond's asking was the proof. And the answer to a warning, Rose had decided, is not a letter — letters can be intercepted, misread, filed. The answer is conduct: public, pointed, unafraid. A Bath call, made in daylight, before witnesses.
> (T1 · look closer) *She re-reads Augusta's "later" — the sister's unhurried; the family's front, holding.* — remembered: *the holding.*
> (T2 · stance) *She decides the day's doctrine — send no flowers back; the warning gets behavior, not bouquets.* — remembered: *the doctrine.*
> (T3 · choice — the day's shape:)*
> - **The call first** — *Nerve+.* The Bath call, made early; the answer, delivered before noon.
> - **The letters first** — *Order+.* Honoria, Laurent; the correspondents, answered before the conduct.
> - **The town first** — *Society+.* The Pump Room, the crescent; the day, begun among witnesses.
> (T4 · look closer) *She studies the call's requirements — public, pointed, unafraid; three adjectives, one morning.* — remembered: *the requirements.*
> (T5 · social maneuver) *She sends the card round — the call announced, the hour set; Bath will know where Miss Hartwell is going.* — remembered: *the announcing.*
> (T6 · stance) *She decides the call's audience is the Network — Drummond's question, answered where Drummond's friends will hear.* — remembered: *the audience.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She chooses the dress — not yet the ritual; the morning's plain, the call's armor selected later.* — remembered: *the selecting.*
> (T8 · choice — the morning's temper:)*
> - **Calm** — *Composure+.* The answer, delivered like weather; unafraid as a habit.
> - **Bright** — *Spirit+.* The answer, delivered like sunshine; unafraid as a triumph.
> The letter lay where she had left it — Augusta's hand, the seal broken, the "later" underlined once in Rose's own pen. Outside, Bath was doing its bright morning business: the water-drinkers, the chairmen, the shops opening. The Network knew. Drummond was asking. And somewhere in London, a financier was taking inventory of her family's roofs. Rose folded the letter and put it in the campaign book's heart-file, next to Honoria's. Family news first. Then the war.
> *(She chooses calm — the answer like weather. And Rose Hartwell begins the day the Thorn answers: not with flowers, not with letters, but with herself, in daylight, before witnesses.)*

scenes.synopsis: Honoria's letter — the wallflower, blooming; the friend's news. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> The morning post brought Honoria's letter — and it was, Rose saw at once, a different letter from any Honoria had written before.
> *(The letter: the familiar hand, but the sentences standing straighter; the wallflower's news.)*
> "You will laugh," Honoria wrote, "or perhaps you will not — I danced. Twice. At the assembly — the Bath assembly, the one you surveyed so magnificently — a Mr. Ellison asked me, and I did not refuse, and the second dance I did not even consider refusing. The wallflower, it seems, has opinions about dancing. I thought you should know first, because you are the reason."
> (T1 · look closer) *She studies the letter's straighter sentences — the wallflower, blooming; Honoria's transformation, in ink.* — remembered: *the blooming.*
> (T2 · stance) *She decides what the blooming means — her own conduct, reflected; the Thorn's courage, contagious.* — remembered: *the contagious.*
> (T3 · choice — the letter's answer:)*
> - **As a friend** — *Friendship+.* "My dearest Honoria — " the equal's joy; the wallflower, celebrated.
> - **As a patron** — *Patronage+.* The introductions, the sponsorship; Honoria's season, advanced.
> - **Bring her to Bath** — *Summons+.* Come; the blooming, witnessed and watered.
> *(The choice of how to answer Honoria is the chapter's — it will come, in its ★ hour. For now, the letter is savored.)*
> (T4 · look closer) *She examines "you are the reason" — the responsibility of it; her conduct has become someone's example.* — remembered: *the example.*
> (T5 · stance) *She decides the example is a trust — Honoria blooms because Rose stood; the standing must continue.* — remembered: *the trust.*
> (T6 · social maneuver) *She shows Letitia the dancing part — the aunt's delight; the household, celebrating.* — remembered: *the delight.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She files the letter with the precious — not the campaign book; the heart's file.* — remembered: *the filing.*
> (T8 · choice — the morning's warmth:)*
> - **Write at once** — *Eager+.* The joy, immediate; Honoria, answered before the call.
> - **Carry it** — *Savored+.* The letter in the reticule; the blooming, carried into the day.
> *(She carries it — the letter in the reticule, the blooming in her heart. And Rose goes to dress for the call with a wallflower's courage in her pocket.)*

scenes.synopsis: Laurent's letter — what loyalty may require; the polish, dropping. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> Laurent's letter came with the second post — and the polish, Rose saw at once, was dropping.
> *(The letter: the elegant hand, less elegant than usual; the sentences, shorter; the correspondent, unguarded.)*
> "I write what I should not," he wrote. "Loyalty — you asked once what it requires. It requires this: that I tell you the London face has a name in certain rooms, and the name is spoken with respect, and respect, in those rooms, means fear. Be careful, Rose. The men you are mapping do not play the Bath game. They play the London one, and the London one has no umpires."
> (T1 · look closer) *She studies the dropped polish — the shorter sentences; Laurent, unguarded, which means afraid.* — remembered: *the unguarded.*
> (T2 · look closer) *She examines the warning — "the London one has no umpires"; the correspondent, telling her what loyalty requires.* — remembered: *the requiring.*
> (T3 · stance) *She decides what the letter is — not gossip; a confession. Laurent has told her where he stands.* — remembered: *the confession.*
> (T4 · choice — the meeting of it (the chapter's ★ will formalize; here, the temper):*
> - **With honesty** — *Honest+.* The confession, met openly; Laurent, answered in kind.
> - **With strategy** — *Shrewd+.* The intelligence, extracted; the warning, mined for detail.
> - **At arm's length** — *Guarded+.* The correspondent, thanked and held off; the wariness, maintained.
> (T5 · look closer) *She considers "respect means fear" — the London rooms, the de Valcourt name; the financier's weight, confirmed.* — remembered: *the weight.*
> (T6 · stance) *She decides the warning does not change the call — it sharpens it; unafraid is the answer to fear, including Laurent's.* — remembered: *the sharpening.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She files the letter with the campaign book — the intelligence, evidenced; Laurent's confession, kept.* — remembered: *the keeping.*
> (T8 · choice — the letter's immediate use:)*
> - **Heed it** — *Prudent+.* The call, made carefully; the warning, honored.
> - **Defy it** — *Bold+.* The call, made boldly; the warning, answered by conduct.
> *(She defies it — carefully. The call will be bold and careful both; that is what unafraid means. And Laurent's unguarded letter goes into the book, where confessions are kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ DRESSING RITUAL — the Bath call; day dress; the brief is unafraid. Twenty decomposed micro-decisions at 5 coins each (≈100 coins). Jewels from owned pieces only; the jewel shelf is always open but never a ritual step. (Turns: 21 — direction + 20 pins)
scenes.prose:
> *(System: the occasion brief is published.)*
>
> **Occasion brief — The Bath Call**
> *Day. A pointedly public morning call — the Network's warning, answered through conduct. The brief is unafraid: day dress for a woman who has mapped a chain, named a financier, and means the town to see her unmoved. Editorial criterion — every choice is judged on whether it says* I am not afraid, *without saying a word about what there is to fear. No armor that looks like armor; the courage must read as ease.*
>
> Rose reads the brief twice, and lays out three directions on the table:
>
> **A. The Bright Morning** — primrose muslin, white spencer; unafraid as sunshine, the answer as brightness.
> **B. The Composed Call** — pearl-grey silk, black trim; unafraid as composure, the answer as steadiness.
> **C. The Bold Day** — scarlet pelisse over white; unafraid as daring, the answer as triumph.
>
> *(System: the player commits to a direction — remembered for the call. Then the pins begin. Each pin costs 5 coins from play earnings; no Crown SKUs touch the ritual. Jewels come from owned pieces only — the jewel shelf is always open but never a ritual step.)*
>
> (T1 · choice — the direction) *She commits: A, B, or C — the call's thesis, remembered.*
>

> **Pin 4 (T4 · micro-decision) — The bodice's cut:** simple, unadorned; courage needs no ornament. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 5 (T5 · micro-decision) — The neckline:** modest, open; the throat, unguarded. *5 coins.*

> **Pin 8 (T8 · micro-decision) — The spencer or pelisse:** white, black-trimmed, or scarlet — the call's outer word. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 9 (T9 · micro-decision) — The trim:** minimal — the brief forbids armor that looks like armor. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 10 (T10 · micro-decision) — The shoe:** walking shoe, sturdy, certain. *5 coins.*
>
> *(Story morsel: Letitia looks in, sees the primrose — or the pearl-grey, or the scarlet — and says, "Unafraid. Yes. Though I confess, my love, I am a little afraid for you, which I suppose is the aunt's part in all of this." Rose kisses her cheek. "Then play your part beautifully," she says.)*
>

> **Pin 12 (T12 · micro-decision) — The bonnet:** straw, silk, or velvet — the street's first reading. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 13 (T13 · micro-decision) — The bonnet's trim:** ribbon, feather, or none — each a different morning. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 (T14 · micro-decision) — The hair:** dressed simply, under the bonnet; ease, all the way down. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 (T15 · micro-decision) — The earring:** small, gold; the day's only glint. *5 coins.*

> **Pin 17 (T17 · micro-decision) — The parasol:** carried, not needed; the lady's punctuation. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 (T18 · micro-decision) — The reticule:** Honoria's letter inside; the blooming, carried. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 19 (T19 · micro-decision) — The scent:** lavender water — calm, worn like weather. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 20 (T20 · micro-decision) — The bearing rehearsal:** the call — chin, shoulders, the door-handling of a woman answering a warning with her presence. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 21 (T21 · micro-decision) — The final mirror:** the whole unafraid, head to heel, judged against the brief's single question — *does it say I am not afraid?* *5 coins.*
>
> *(Story morsel: at the final pin, Rose looks at the girl in the glass — primrose, pearl-grey, or scarlet — and the girl looks back with the particular expression of someone who has decided that courage is a kind of manners. "Unafraid," Rose says aloud. The glass agrees.)*

scenes.prose:
> *(System: reveal coda — the ritual's payoff. Rose stands before the glass in the full chosen direction, the unafraid call complete.)*
> The mirror showed ease — primrose, or pearl-grey, or scarlet — with the tortoiseshell pin at the throat and Honoria's letter in the reticule and the particular stillness of someone whose courage reads as manners.
> (T1 · look closer) *She studies the woman in the glass — the season's work, written on her; the surveyor, the answerer, the Thorn, all at once.* — remembered: *the woman.*
> (T2 · stance) *She decides the look is right — not armor, exactly, though it protects; but ease, which is the call's whole ambition.* — remembered: *the ease, worn.*
> (T3 · remembered micro-decision) *She takes up the parasol — carried, not needed; the lady's punctuation.* — remembered: *the punctuation.*
> (T4 · social maneuver) *She rehearses the call — the knock, the entry, the first sentence; conduct, choreographed.* — remembered: *the choreography.*
> (T5 · stance) *She sets the fear behind her — Laurent's warning, honored and defied; unafraid is the answer.* — remembered: *the answer.*
> (T6 · choice — the call's vow:)*
> - **"Conduct, not correspondence."** — *Doctrine+.* The chapter's rule, spoken aloud.
> - **"Unafraid."** — *Declaration+.* The brief's word, spoken aloud.
> - **"No flowers back."** — *Resolve+.* The negative, spoken aloud.
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She touches Honoria's letter in the reticule — the blooming, carried; the example, shouldered.* — remembered: *the shouldering.*
> The parasol turned slowly in her hand — the lady's punctuation, as the ritual had it. In the glass, the woman turned too: primrose catching the morning light, the tortoiseshell pin at the throat, Honoria's letter a small weight in the reticule. Ease, all the way down — that had been the brief, and the brief was kept. No armor that looked like armor. Only a woman, dressed for a morning call, carrying a wallflower's courage in her pocket and a warning's answer in her bearing.
> Letitia's nod at the door was the ritual's true seal — the aunt's approval, given silently, the way the best approvals are. The surveyor was ready, the lady was complete, and the evening's ledger was memorized. Bath would see sapphire and ease. Only Rose would know about the chain.
> *(She goes down to the carriage — unafraid, complete, unmissable — and Bath, which revised its estimate upward at the assembly, is about to revise it again.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ FASHION-SELECTION — no coin cost, remembered. The call's finishing statement: the shawl, the street's last word. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(System: fashion-selection — diegetic, no coin cost. The choice is remembered and will surface in the town's reading of her.)*
> "The shawl," Letitia said, laying three across the bed — the dress complete, the call nearly sealed, only the street's last word to choose. "The morning is cool, the call is public, and Mrs. Nance Bell will have an opinion by tomorrow. The shawl is the sentence's end. Choose the ending."
>
> **A. The Ivory Cashmere** — soft, trailing; unafraid made graceful, the answer as lady.
> **B. The Grey Silk** — composed, plain; unafraid made steady, the answer as composure.
> **C. The Scarlet Wrap** — bright, sweeping; unafraid made triumphant, the answer as victory.
>
> The three shawls lay across the bed like three different mornings — the ivory cashmere soft as weather, the grey silk composed as a verdict, the scarlet wrap bright as a challenge. Letitia's fingers hovered, then settled, then lifted again; choosing for someone else's courage is a serious business. "The street will read it before you knock," the aunt said. "Choose the sentence you want read." Rose chose — cashmere, silk, or wrap — and the morning's last word was spoken.
> *(System: no coin cost. The selection is remembered — the town will read it.)*
> (T1 · choice) *She chooses — A, B, or C; the street's last word.*
> (T2 · look closer) *She studies each shawl's reading — the cashmere says grace, the silk says steadiness, the wrap says victory; Bath will translate.* — remembered: *the translation.*

> (T4 · social maneuver) *She times the call — mid-morning, when the town is out; the answer, witnessed.* — remembered: *the timing.*
> (T5 · look closer) *She considers Drummond's friends — the asking's audience; what will the shawl say to them?* — remembered: *the message.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *She takes Letitia's arm at the carriage — the aunt's steadiness, borrowed; the call, shared.* — remembered: *the arm.*
> (T7 · stance) *She sets her face — unafraid, complete; the answer begins at the door.* — remembered: *the face.*
> Rose chose — cashmere, silk, or wrap — and Letitia arranged it with the gravity of a general issuing the last order. "Well," the aunt said, "whatever you are answering today, it will know it has been answered. Whether that is a warning or an invitation is entirely up to you."

> (T6 · stance) *She decides the call is working — the warning, answered; the Network's question, met with a lady at ease.* — remembered: *the working.*

> The drawing room was at its mid-morning fullest — the colonel's wife presiding, the banker in the corner, the ladies arranged like a jury. Rose made her entrance with the particular ease she had rehearsed: the knock, the smile, the first sentence landing lightly. "The estate's arrangements are quite sound, thank you." > *(She goes — the street, the carriage, the witnesses dispersing with the news. And Rose Hartwell, who sent no flowers back, has answered the warning the only way that matters: by being seen, unafraid.)*

> - **Spend it** — *Capital+.* The estimate, converted; social capital, banked for the war.
> - **Distrust it** — *Prudence+.* Towns revise downward too; the estimate, held lightly.

scenes.synopsis: Open from Chapter 18's cliffhanger — Quill's letter arrives with the morning post: the Hartwell obligations are being gathered up; someone is buying Hartwell paper, fast.
scenes.prose:
> The letter came with the morning post, on top of the household accounts, underneath nothing — as though it had declined to wait its turn.
> *(System: Mr. Quill's hand, Lincoln's Inn, the seal pressed crooked — haste in a man who never hurries.)*
> "Quill," Rose said, turning it over. "Before breakfast. That is never a social call."
> "Open it before the eggs," said Letitia, who had watched her niece watch the post all week, the way one watches a kettle. "Bad news improves with butter. I have tested the theory extensively."
> Rose broke the seal. The letter was short, and said, in effect, what the cliffhanger had promised: the Hartwell obligations — the scattered notes, the mortgages' loose ends, the paper Rackham had flung like shot across three counties — were being gathered up. Quietly. Someone was buying Hartwell paper, and buying it fast.
> "Fast," Rose read aloud, and the word sat in the breakfast room like a third guest.
> "Fast is expensive," Letitia said. "Fast means they are afraid of being outbid. Afraid of *whom*, precisely?"
> "Of us. Or of anyone who has read what we have read." Rose set the letter down beside her plate and looked at it the way one looks at a fuse. "Quill says the buying runs through the London front — the same men who discount the émigré notes. Voss & Hallett's people. They are not collecting debts, Letitia. They are assembling a position."
> "Against the Park."
> "Against the Park, the mortgages, the forced sale Rackham started and did not live to finish." Rose folded her hands. "Someone means to own enough of us to bury us politely. And they are doing it *fast*."
>

scenes.synopsis: What "buying Hartwell paper, fast" means — the obligations, the position, the sale Rackham started.
scenes.prose:
> "Explain it to me as though I were a débutante," Letitia said, pouring with the concentration of a woman defusing something. "Which, before you make the face, I was, and a stupider one than Honoria."
> "The obligations are the loose paper — notes of hand, the mortgages' tail ends, debts my father left that Rackham bought and scattered." Rose counted them off on her fingers. "Whoever holds enough of them can call them. Called together, at once, they force a sale. Rackham meant to do it. Someone else means to finish it."
> "And the *fast*?"
> "Fast means the front has a timetable. Julian's brother's notes, the émigré bundles, now ours — someone is buying up a whole countryside of paper, and the buying has a direction." Rose looked out at the Crescent, where Bath was going about its unconcerned morning. "Quill writes that the offers are generous. Generous is what you pay when you cannot afford to be refused."
> Letitia set down the pot. "Then we must be the refusal."
> "We must be the *buyer*." Rose turned from the window. "That is the thought I have been having since the second paragraph, Aunt, and I am nearly ashamed of how much I like it. They mean to buy us from under ourselves. What if we buy first — from under *them*?"
> "With what?"
> "With Augusta's backing. With Trelawney's nerve. With" — Rose smiled, thin as a draft — "the one advantage of being the person they are trying to ruin: we know exactly which paper they want."
>

> **[T4 · Maneuver]** — The word "generous": *repeat it with irony / let it lie / underline it for the bankers.* (Remembered: how Rose frames the enemy — Trelawney borrows the frame.)
> **[T5 · Stance]** — Ashamed of liking the thought, or not: *own the relish / disown it / make it a joke.* (Remembered: her honesty with Letitia — the aunt's counsel sharpens or softens.)

scenes.synopsis: Texture — Rose alone with the obligations list; the shape of what is being bought.
scenes.prose:
> Alone in the sitting room, Rose spread Quill's enclosure — the list of the obligations coming to market — across the writing desk, and studied it the way a general studies a map of ground she has already walked.
> *(System: the list — a dozen lines in a clerk's hand, sums in the margin, dates going back twenty years. Her father's hand on the oldest. Rackham's endorsement on the newest.)*
> Each line was a small, exact humiliation, priced and dated. A note from the year of the bad harvest. A mortgage tail from before her birth. A tradesman's bill her father had signed with a flourish, as though the signature were the payment. Together they were not a fortune — that was the obscenity of it. Together they were a *lever*: enough, called at once, to force the sale of Hartwell Park to whoever held them.
> She ran her finger down the margin sums. The total was less than the cost of a London season. Less than Drummond's diamonds, probably. Her whole house — the Park, the name, the four hundred years of Hartwells in the churchyard — priced at less than a season's frivolity, and on the market *now*, and being bought by men who discounted émigré notes for breakfast.
> "Noted," she said to the list. "Filed. And — " she took up her pen and wrote in the margin, in her own hand, under Quill's clerk's sums: *Buy first.*
> The pen scratched. The ink was still wet when she folded the list into her pocketbook — not hidden, kept; the way one keeps a warrant.
>

scenes.synopsis: Beat B1 — Augusta's backing: the rear guard becomes the war chest.
scenes.prose:
> Augusta's letter arrived by the afternoon post, as though the Dowager had smelled the morning's news from London — which, Rose reflected, she very probably had.
> *(System: Ravencroft House, London — the heavy paper, the upright hand, the seal exact. Augusta never hurries. Augusta had simply known sooner.)*
> *My dear Rose —*
> *Quill has written to me as well as to you. I have read his list — and the name of the buyer behind the buyers, which Quill is too much the solicitor to write: it is the de Valcourt interest. The London front is its glove.*
> *You will be wondering about money. Do not. I am the rear guard, and the rear guard has a war chest. Draw on me for the purchase — the whole of the list, if you can take it. I have kept my own counsel and my own funds for forty years against exactly this week. Spend them.*
> *One condition, and it is not negotiable: do it in the open. If you buy this paper in a solicitor's office, it is business. If you buy it at the assembly, in daylight, before the banking houses of Bath, it is a* statement. *The Network has operated in shadow all season. Drag it into the light and make it blink.*
> *— A.*
> Rose read it twice. Then she read it a third time, and folded it with hands that were not quite steady.
> "Well," said Letitia, who had been pretending not to watch. "Is the rear guard still guarding?"
> "The rear guard," said Rose, "has just declared war."
>
> **[T1 · Tone]** — Reading the third time: *slowly / hungrily / with disbelief.* (Remembered: her hunger for the fight — Letitia notes it.)
> **[T2 · Look]** — "The de Valcourt interest": *linger on the name / skip to the money / read the condition first.* (Remembered: what she fears most — the name, or the price.)
> **[T3 · Choice]** — The condition — in the open: *accept it at once / weigh it / resent it.* (Converges: the assembly is the ground. Remembered: her obedience — Augusta's next letter answers it.)
> **[T4 · Micro]** — The letter's keeping: *with Quill's list / apart, in the workbox / carried on her person.* (Remembered: how she guards Augusta's hand.)
> **[T5 · Maneuver]** — "Has just declared war": *said lightly / said gravely / said only to Letitia.* (Remembered: who hears the war named — the household's week turns on it.)
> **[T6 · Stance]** — Draw on the war chest: *as a gift / as a loan / as a trust.* (Remembered: how she names the money — Augusta will hold her to the word.)

scenes.synopsis: Rose's reply to Augusta — the war chest accepted, the condition weighed, the terms of the trust named.
scenes.prose:
> She wrote the reply at the desk, with Quill's list on one side and Augusta's letter on the other, like a woman signing a treaty between two powers — which, she reflected, was exactly what she was.
> *Dear Grandmama —*
> *The war chest is accepted, and the condition with it. In the open. In daylight. At the assembly — there is, you will be glad to hear, one announced for a week hence, and the front's credit will be on parade there like a horse at a fair.*
> *I will name the terms of the trust, since you will not: it is a loan until the paper is ours, and a gift only if I fail to repay it — which I do not intend. The Hartwells will not be bought out of ruin by their grandmother's pin money and call it victory.*
> *Trelawney is with us. The bankers of Bath are being enlisted. Julian has the front's timetable — you will have heard; nothing in this town is secret from you for more than a day.*
> *One question, and you may refuse to answer it: the de Valcourt interest. You wrote the name as one writes a relative's. Is it?*
> *— R.*
> She sanded the letter, sealed it, and sat back. The question had written itself — she had meant to strike it, and had not. Some questions, she was learning, were like thorns: the stripping of them was the message.
> *(System: the letter goes by the evening post. Augusta will answer — or not — in her own time, which is to say, when the answer is useful.)*
>
> **[T1 · Tone]** — "The war chest is accepted": *as a soldier / as a granddaughter / as a Hartwell.* (Remembered: the letter's voice — Augusta reads it thrice.)
> **[T2 · Choice]** — Loan or gift — the terms named: *loan / gift / trust, unnamed.* (Converges: Augusta's money moves. Remembered: the word — it binds the S23 reckoning.)
> **[T3 · Look]** — The thorn-question: *strike it / keep it / soften it.* (Remembered: whether she presses Augusta on de Valcourt — the Dowager's answer, or silence, is data.)
> **[T4 · Micro]** — The seal: *the Hartwell seal / plain wax / Augusta's own wafer.* (Remembered: small ceremony — the postmaster's boy notices.)
> **[T5 · Stance]** — "Not by pin money": *pride / honesty / defiance.* (Remembered: her pride's edge — Julian hears of it, and understands.)
> **[T6 · Maneuver]** — Mention Julian's timetable, or not: *name him / leave him unnamed / mention "a friend."* (Remembered: how she shields him — he learns of it.)
> **[T7 · Tone]** — The signing — "R.": *the initial, bare / "your Rose" / "your obedient."* (Remembered: the intimacy's measure — Augusta keeps every letter.)

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE PURCHASE. Before she can move, the purchase needs a face: bid openly as Hartwell, through Trelawney's name, or through a London agent.
scenes.prose:
> That evening Rose walked the Crescent alone, doing the bankers' arithmetic a day early — the arithmetic of faces.
> *(System: the purchase needs a face before it needs a price. Three faces are available; each costs differently.)*
> Bid openly, as Hartwell — her name on the purchase before the banking houses of Bath. The nerve of it was the statement Augusta demanded. The cost of it would be the exposure: the Network would know, that night, exactly who had bloodied it, and the principal — the de Valcourt interest, the hand behind the glove — would learn her name the way one learns an enemy's.
> Bid through Trelawney — the banker's name on the paper, hers behind it. Respectable, deniable, and exactly what the front would expect a frightened heiress to do. The cost: Trelawney's nerve, which was real but finite, and the whiff of fear about the whole proceeding — the ton can smell a cutout the way it smells a lie.
> Bid through a London agent — Quill's man, or one of Augusta's, a professional buyer with no Bath connections and no face the front would recognize. The safest. The most deniable. And the most *shadowed* — the very thing Augusta's condition forbade: business done in a solicitor's office, not a statement made in daylight.
> The Crescent lamps came on one by one. Below, Bath glittered — the town that had underestimated her all season, and was about to be revised.
> *(System: the choice is Rose's. The block cannot be laid until the purchase has a face.)*
>
> **[T1 · Look]** — The open face: *weigh its nerve / weigh its exposure / weigh Augusta's demand.* (Remembered: what tempts her — nerve or safety.)
> **[T2 · Look]** — Trelawney's face: *weigh his nerve / weigh the whiff of fear / weigh the bankers' read.* (Remembered: how she prices other people's courage.)
> **[T3 · Look]** — The agent's face: *weigh its safety / weigh its shadow / weigh Augusta's condition.* (Remembered: whether the condition binds her.)
> **[T4 · Stance]** — "The principal would learn her name": *welcome it / dread it / price it.* (Remembered: her appetite for being known.)
> **[T5 · Micro]** — The walk's turn: *at the end of the Crescent / at the elm / mid-parade, decided.* (Remembered: small truth — Letitia will ask where she decided.)
> **[T6 · Tone]** — The decision's manner: *swift / savored / reluctant.* (Remembered: how she chooses.)
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The purchase's face:*
- **Bid openly as Hartwell** — *Nerve+, exposure.* Rose's name on the purchase, in daylight, before the houses; the statement Augusta demanded — and the principal learns her name that night.
- **Bid through Trelawney's name** — *Deniability, bankers' nerve spent.* The banker's name fronts it; respectable, expected — with the faint whiff of fear the ton will detect.
- **Bid through a London agent** — *Safety, shadow.* A professional buyer, no Bath face; the safest course — and the least daylight, against Augusta's condition.

scenes.synopsis: Beat B2 — Trelawney's counting-house: the block. The Hartwell obligations coming to market through the London front.
scenes.prose:
> Trelawney & Sons sat on Milsom Street with the quiet prosperity of a house that had never once been surprised by money — which made Mr. Trelawney's expression, when Rose laid Quill's list on his desk, all the more interesting to watch.
> *(System: the counting-house — ledgers, ink, the smell of money gone quiet; the clerk withdrawing at a look.)*
> He read the list twice. He read Augusta's condition — Rose had copied it fair, without the thorn-question — once. Then he took off his spectacles and polished them, a man buying time with chamois.
> "The obligations come to market through the London front," he said at last. "Voss & Hallett's people have been placing the offers. Quietly, but not quietly enough — three of the holders came to me first, out of old feeling for your father, and I told them to wait." He set the spectacles back on. "Miss Hartwell, if we move before the front's next offers land, we can take the whole list. The block — the entire bundle, bought entire — would cost less than the front expects to pay for half of it, because the holders would rather sell to a Hartwell than to London."
> "Then we buy the block."
> "Before the assembly." Trelawney leaned forward. "And at it — your grandmother's condition. Miss Hartwell, do you understand what you are proposing? To outbid the Network's front *in the room*, before the banking houses, with their credit on parade — "
> "I understand," said Rose, "that it is the only way that counts."
>
> **[T1 · Tone]** — "Then we buy the block": *as a command / as a question / as a fact.* (Remembered: her command's manner — the bankers repeat it.)
> **[T2 · Look]** — The polished spectacles: *watch the delay / interrupt it / let him finish.* (Remembered: her patience with frightened men.)
> **[T3 · Choice]** — Show him Augusta's condition, or paraphrase: *the fair copy / her own words.* (Converges: he knows the condition. Remembered: how she handles Augusta's hand — his trust shifts.)
> **[T4 · Maneuver]** — "Old feeling for your father": *press the advantage / honor it / price it.* (Remembered: whether she spends her father's memory — the holders hear of it.)
> **[T5 · Stance]** — The only way that counts: *nerve / arithmetic / both.* (Remembered: her doctrine — the sting will quote it.)
> **[T6 · Micro]** — The list, left with him or kept: *leave the copy / keep it / leave it and take his.* (Remembered: the paper's custody — it matters at the assembly.)
> **[T7 · Tone]** — Leaving the counting-house: *brisk / grave / exhilarated.* (Remembered: the clerk's report below stairs — Bath reads her walk.)

scenes.synopsis: The plan, drawn — how the block is bought from under the front: the timing, the money, the room.
scenes.prose:
> "The front's offers land on Thursday," Trelawney said, spreading a sheet of his own — dates, sums, the front's known movements in a clerk's neat hand. "Their man in Bath places them personally. If the holders have our word first — your word, Miss Hartwell, and the draft to stand behind it — the front will arrive to find the shelves empty."
> "And at the assembly?"
> "The assembly is the *statement*." Trelawney's finger tapped the sheet. "The purchase itself can be settled before — quietly, properly, solicitor to solicitor. But your grandmother is right: if it is only settled, it is only business. At the assembly, before the houses, the front's credit on parade — that is where the *block* is declared. The room must *see* the money change masters. Otherwise the Network simply tries again, somewhere darker."
> Rose studied the sheet. "The draft — Augusta's war chest. When does it arrive?"
> "Tomorrow, by post chaise. And Miss Hartwell — " Trelawney hesitated, a banker weighing whether to spend a confidence. "The houses will ask what stands behind the draft. I will tell them: the Hartwell name, and the Dowager's. But they will want to *see* you. At dinner, before the assembly. Men with ledgers do not lend nerve to a name they have not looked in the eye."
> "Then they shall look me in the eye." Rose folded the sheet. "Name the evening. I will dress for it."
> "Thursday." Trelawney smiled, a fraction. "You will dress to be taken seriously by men with ledgers, Miss Hartwell. It is a particular art. I have seen it done badly for thirty years."
>
> **[T1 · Tone]** — "Then they shall look me in the eye": *as a promise / as a challenge / as a fact.* (Remembered: her nerve's register — the bankers' wives retail it.)
> **[T2 · Look]** — The front's movements: *study the dates / study the sums / study the man's name.* (Remembered: what she hunts — dates or men.)
> **[T3 · Choice]** — Settle quietly first, declare at the assembly — or all at once in the room: *the two-step / the single stroke.* (Converges: the plan holds. Remembered: her taste for theater — Augusta approves or corrects.)
> **[T4 · Maneuver]** — "I will dress for it": *said lightly / said as strategy / said as a warning.* (Remembered: how she wields the wardrobe — Élise takes notes.)
> **[T5 · Stance]** — The draft's backing: *the Hartwell name / the Dowager's / her own.* (Remembered: whose name she spends first.)
> **[T6 · Micro]** — Trelawney's sheet: *kept / memorized / returned.* (Remembered: paper custody — again.)
> **[T7 · Tone]** — "Done badly for thirty years": *laugh / nod / file the warning.* (Remembered: whether she takes the banker's counsel — he offers more, or less.)

scenes.synopsis: Texture — the counting-house after hours: ledgers, ink, the smell of money gone quiet; the paper's human cost.
scenes.prose:
> Trelawney kept her past the clerk's leaving, and Rose sat a while among the ledgers after the plan was drawn, listening to the counting-house settle.
> *(System: the room at dusk — the day's entries ruled off, the strongbox locked, the inkstands capped; money, gone quiet for the night, like a dog that has been fed.)*
> The ledgers stood in rows, each spine a year, each year a hundred small disasters survived or not. She ran a finger along 1794 — the year of the bad harvest note, her father's flourish — and thought of all the hands that had written in these books: clerks dead forty years, the émigré names in faded continental hands, endorsing paper that had crossed the Channel in fishing boats and ended here, in ink.
> Money had a smell, she decided: ink and dust and the faint, sweet rot of old paper. It smelled nothing like the ballroom's orange water. And yet the ballroom and the counting-house were the same war now — the assembly rooms lit for dancing, the ledgers ruled for lending, and between them a girl in a muslin walking both floors with a war chest in her pocketbook.
> "You are thinking," said Trelawney from the doorway, "that it is a great deal of trouble for ink."
> "I am thinking," said Rose, "that ink is the only thing in this town that tells the truth. Paper does not know it is lying. People do, and charge extra for it."
> He laughed — the first unbanked sound she had heard from him. "Quill's line. He uses it on everyone."
> "It is a good line. I intend to steal it." She rose. "Thursday, then. The dinner. And the week after — the assembly."
> "The assembly," he agreed, and locked the strongbox with a sound like a period at the end of a sentence.
>
> **[T1 · Look]** — The 1794 spine: *touch it / read the year / leave it.* (Remembered: whether the past steadies her — the sting may notice.)
> **[T2 · Micro]** — Quill's line, stolen: *use it at dinner / keep it for the assembly / keep it private.* (Remembered: the line's first audience — it becomes hers.)
> **[T3 · Stance]** — Ink vs. people: *trust the paper / trust the men / trust neither, watch both.* (Remembered: her doctrine — Trelawney's counsel adjusts.)
> **[T4 · Tone]** — "Thursday, then": *brisk / solemn / with appetite.* (Remembered: the clerk hears; Bath reads her walk home.)
> **[T5 · Look]** — The strongbox's lock: *watch it turn / look away / note the sound.* (Remembered: small truth — she is learning the banker's theater.)
> **[T6 · Choice]** — Stay longer among the ledgers, or go: *stay / go.* (Converges: the plan is drawn. Remembered: her hunger for the paper — Trelawney offers more, or guards more.)
> **[T7 · Maneuver]** — The laugh, answered: *with warmth / with gravity / with a banker's nod.* (Remembered: how she meets unbanked men — his nerve steadies or wavers.)

scenes.synopsis: Beat B3 — the nerve: in public, in daylight, at the assembly. The only way that counts.
scenes.prose:
> They walked out together into the Milsom Street lamplight, and Trelawney — who had spent the day being brave in a counting-house — chose the pavement to be frightened on.
> "Miss Hartwell." He stopped under a lamp. "I have lent nerve to a great many enterprises. Canals. Turnpikes. A balloon venture I prefer not to recall. But this — to stand in the assembly rooms, before the houses, and declare that the Network's front has been outbid — by a young lady — "
> "By a Hartwell," Rose corrected.
> "By a Hartwell," he allowed, "in daylight, with their credit on parade — it is not banking, Miss Hartwell. It is — "
> "War." She said it plainly, because plainly was the only way it could be said on a public pavement. "And I know it is not banking, Mr. Trelawney. Banking is what we did this afternoon — the dates, the sums, the draft. The assembly is what the banking is *for*. Augusta's condition, and she is right: if we buy this paper in a solicitor's office, the Network tries again somewhere darker. If we buy it in the room, before the houses — "
> "The room recalculates."
> "The room recalculates." She smiled. "You said it yourself, about the ton in Bath: they cannot decide whether my muslins are propriety or poverty. After the assembly they will not have to decide. They will have *seen*."
> Trelawney was quiet a moment. Then: "My father banked through the '97 panic. He used to say: nerve is the only asset that compounds. I never understood him until this week."
> "Then compound it, Mr. Trelawney." Rose offered her hand, and the banker — after the faintest hesitation, the last of the day's fright — shook it, there on the pavement, in the lamplight, where anyone might see.
> Anyone did. Bath would talk about the handshake by morning — which, Rose reflected, walking on alone, was rather the point.
>
> **[T1 · Tone]** — "War": *plain / gentle / with relish.* (Remembered: the word's weight — Trelawney carries it to the bankers.)
> **[T2 · Maneuver]** — The handshake, public: *offered / waited for / seized.* (Remembered: who saw — Bath's talk is the point, or the price.)
> **[T3 · Stance]** — Correcting "young lady" to "a Hartwell": *pride / strategy / habit.* (Remembered: the name's use — the houses will hear it.)
> **[T4 · Look]** — His fright, on the pavement: *name it / let it pass / borrow it.* (Remembered: how she steadies frightened men.)
> **[T5 · Choice]** — Walk on alone, or let him see her home: *alone / escorted.* (Converges: she reaches the lodgings. Remembered: her independence — the town reads it.)
> **[T6 · Tone]** — "Compound it": *as counsel / as command / as a joke.* (Remembered: the line — his father would have liked it; he tells the bankers.)
> **[T7 · Micro]** — The lamp-post: *pause under it / walk past / turn back once.* (Remembered: small theater — someone is always watching in Bath.)

scenes.synopsis: Beat B6 (texture) — the arithmetic of nerve: what the win costs, what losing costs more.
scenes.prose:
> That night Rose did the other arithmetic — not the bankers' sums, but the nerve's.
> *(System: the pocketbook, the candle, the two columns: what the win costs, what losing costs more.)*
> What the win costs: Augusta's war chest, spent — the draft drawn, the trust named a loan, the repayment a debt she would carry for years. Trelawney's nerve, spent — a good man's peace, compounded into a war he did not start. The bankers' nerve, to be spent Thursday. Julian's timetable, whatever it cost him to get it. Her own name — on the purchase, in daylight, before the houses — spent most of all: after the assembly, the principal would know her, and knowing is the first half of hunting.
> What losing costs more: the Park. The mortgages called at once, the forced sale, the Hartwells in the churchyard watching the house go to the de Valcourt interest — the hand behind the glove, the name Augusta wrote like a relative's. The servants' hall scattered. Honoria's sponsorship a bad joke. Drummond's second installment named over a ruin instead of a restoration. And the money — the money would have won, again, the way it won thirty years ago when it was bundled against her grandfather, the way it wins whenever no one drags it into the light.
> She ruled off the second column. It was longer.
> "There," she told the pocketbook. "That is the arithmetic. The win is expensive. The losing is ruinous. Between the two, there is no decision — there is only the price, and the paying of it in daylight."
> She blew out the candle. In the dark, the sums glowed a moment behind her eyes — and then went out, like lamps along a road she had already decided to walk.
>
> **[T1 · Stance]** — The two columns: *ruled off / left open / burned.* (Remembered: how she closes accounts — the pocketbook keeps the habit.)
> **[T2 · Look]** — The longer column: *study it / refuse it / accept it.* (Remembered: whether she flinches — the nerve's true measure.)
> **[T3 · Micro]** — The candle: *blown out / left burning / carried to bed.* (Remembered: small truth — the maid notes it.)
> **[T4 · Tone]** — "There is only the price": *resigned / resolved / exhilarated.* (Remembered: her private register — it leaks into Thursday's dinner.)
> **[T5 · Choice]** — Count Augusta's money as debt or trust: *debt / trust / both, in order.* (Converges: the draft is drawn. Remembered: the word she uses with herself — Augusta will ask.)
> **[T6 · Look]** — The servants' hall, in the losing column: *linger / skip / underline.* (Remembered: what she fears losing most — it seeds Ch20's reward.)
> **[T7 · Maneuver]** — The dark, addressed: *to the pocketbook / to the room / to no one.* (Remembered: her solitude's audience — someone always hears in Bath.)

scenes.synopsis: Beat B4 — the bankers, enlisted: Bath's nerve, pooled. Trelawney convenes the houses.
scenes.prose:
> Trelawney convened them the next morning — three houses besides his own, in his private parlor above the counting-house: the Milsom Street house, the Queen Square house, the old Bath bank that had survived two panics by the simple expedient of never once being surprised.
> *(System: four bankers, one heiress, a pot of coffee gone cold — the war council of Bath, convened over ledgers instead of maps.)*
> Rose stood while Trelawney laid it out — the obligations, the front's offers, the block, the assembly — and watched the four faces do the arithmetic. Bankers, she was learning, had a particular expression for *risk priced and found acceptable*: a slight lift of the eyebrows, a settling of the shoulders, the look of men who have decided to be brave before lunch.
> "The front's credit," said the Queen Square man, "is good. Voss & Hallett pay promptly."
> "The front's credit," said Rose, "is *spent* — on our paper, at our expense, to bury us politely. Gentlemen, you are being asked to choose between the credit that pays promptly and the house that has banked here for forty years." She let that sit. "I am not asking you to lend. I am asking you to *stand* — at the assembly, in the room, where the front can see you standing. Nerve, pooled, is the only asset that compounds. Mr. Trelawney's father said so in '97."
> Trelawney blinked. The Milsom Street man laughed — once, surprised. The old Bath bank said nothing, which was its entire method, and nodded — once, which was its entire verdict.
> "We will stand," said the Queen Square man, and the eyebrows lifted, and the shoulders settled, all round the table.
>
> **[T1 · Tone]** — "Nerve, pooled": *as doctrine / as a plea / as a fact.* (Remembered: the phrase — Bath's bankers will quote it.)
> **[T2 · Maneuver]** — Standing while they sit: *kept / sat early / stood only to speak.* (Remembered: her theater — the wives hear of it.)
> **[T3 · Look]** — The four faces: *read each / read the room / read Trelawney.* (Remembered: what she watches — men or sums.)
> **[T4 · Choice]** — Name the de Valcourt interest, or "the front": *the name / the glove.* (Converges: they understand. Remembered: who hears the name spoken — it travels.)
> **[T5 · Stance]** — Not asking to lend: *pride / strategy / truth.* (Remembered: her ask's shape — the houses price it.)
> **[T6 · Micro]** — The cold coffee: *drunk / left / remarked upon.* (Remembered: small truth — the parlor maid retails it.)
> **[T7 · Tone]** — The nod, received: *with thanks / with gravity / with a smile.* (Remembered: how she takes allies — they remember the taking.)

scenes.synopsis: The pooling, in detail — what each house stands behind, and what Rose promises in return.
scenes.prose:
> "What do you promise us, Miss Hartwell?" The Milsom Street man asked it bluntly, as bankers do when the coffee is cold and the decision is warm. "Nerve is all very well before lunch. What stands behind it?"
> "Augusta's draft," said Rose. "The Dowager's war chest, drawn and in Trelawney's hands by tomorrow's post chaise. The Hartwell name on the purchase" — she paused, because the purchase's face was her choosing, and the room deserved the truth of it — "in whatever face the plan requires. And one thing more, which is not money."
> "Which is?"
> "That the front will not try this again." She looked round the table. "Gentlemen, you discount their notes. You have all handled émigré paper with the de Valcourt endorsement. You know what that paper buys — ruin, bundled and sold as credit. If we take this block in the room, before the houses, the front's credit in Bath is *finished*. Not dented — finished. Your streets will be cleaner for it. That is what stands behind my nerve: your own interest, properly understood."
> The old Bath bank spoke — its second utterance of the morning. "The assembly is a week hence."
> "A week," Rose agreed. "Time enough for the front to grow confident. Time enough for us to be ready." She rose. "Gentlemen — Thursday, Trelawney's dinner. You will look me in the eye, as promised. And the week after — you will stand where the room can see you."
> They rose with her — four bankers, four nods, the war council adjourned. On the stairs, the Queen Square man said to Trelawney, just loud enough to carry: "She does not bank like a young lady."
> "No," said Trelawney. "She banks like a Hartwell."
>
> **[T1 · Tone]** — "Your own interest, properly understood": *as counsel / as a goad / as a promise.* (Remembered: how she moves bankers — the sting may quote it.)
> **[T2 · Maneuver]** — The pause on the purchase's face: *let them see the choosing / smooth past it / name it outright.* (Remembered: what the houses know of the plan — it colors the assembly.)
> **[T3 · Look]** — The old bank's silence: *court it / respect it / test it.* (Remembered: how she handles the quiet ones.)
> **[T4 · Choice]** — Promise the front's finish, or only the block: *the finish / the block / neither, let them infer.* (Converges: the plan stands. Remembered: the size of her promise — it binds her.)
> **[T5 · Stance]** — "She banks like a Hartwell," overheard: *acknowledge it / let it pass / correct to "Rose."* (Remembered: the name's use — again.)
> **[T6 · Micro]** — The stairs, descended: *first / last / beside Trelawney.* (Remembered: small theater — the clerks below watch.)
> **[T7 · Tone]** — The adjournment: *brisk / grave / warm.* (Remembered: the war council's aftertaste — the bankers carry it to dinner.)

scenes.synopsis: Beat B5 (romance: Julian) — Julian brings the front's timetable: his exposure, engineered; trust, rebuilt, in action.
scenes.prose:
> Julian came at dusk, unannounced, with the look of a man who had ridden hard on someone else's errand and arrived with the dust still on him — which, Rose gathered within a minute, was exactly what he had done.
> *(System: the lodgings' sitting room — Letitia tactfully elsewhere; the timetable in Julian's hand, copied fair, the figures in his own neat, tired writing.)*
> "The front's timetable." He laid it on the table without preamble. "Their man places the offers Thursday. The assembly's credit — Voss himself comes down for it, which tells you how much of the front's pride is riding on the parade. The offers are to be *announced* in the room, Julian — not made, announced. They mean to buy your ruin the way other men buy a horse: publicly, with witnesses, to show they can."
> Rose stared at the paper. "How did you get this?"
> "I asked." At her look, he smiled — the old charm, arriving on time for once. "I have been paying my brother's debts all season, Rose. One learns things, settling accounts — who holds what, who is buying, who is *selling*. A clerk in the front's London office sells information the way other clerks sell sealing-wax. I bought some." The smile faded. "It cost me. Not money — " he glanced away — "exposure. I let him see that Lord Julian Ashcombe is interested in the Hartwell obligations. By tomorrow the front will know I am watching."
> "Julian — "
> "It is done." He met her eyes. "You needed the timetable more than I needed the cover. That is the arithmetic. Do not argue with the arithmetic."
>

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — JULIAN'S TIMETABLE. Trust it fully, verify it first, or keep him out of the room.
scenes.prose:
> The timetable lay between them like a drawn sword — useful, and dangerous to pick up by the wrong end.
> *(System: three ways to take it. The front's man places the offers Thursday; Voss comes down for the assembly; the offers are to be announced in the room. If the timetable is wrong — or planted — the block fails in public, in daylight, before the houses.)*
> Trust it fully: take Julian's figures as gospel and move without looking back. The trust would be the point — after a season of refusals, to take his word whole would be the thing the romance has been building toward. The risk would be equally whole: if the clerk sold him a pretty lie, she would walk into the assembly on false ground.
> Verify it first: run the dates past Trelawney and Quill's man — two days of checking, the block laid on confirmed ground. The cost: the insult — to check his gift would be to tell him that his exposure bought only a draft, not a deed.
> Keep him out of the room: take the timetable, thank him, and see that he is nowhere near the assembly — protected from the front's notice, from the ruin of being seen as her creature. The cost: his pride, and the look on his face when he understands he has been managed.
> Julian watched her weigh it, and said nothing — his way of leaving the sword where she could reach it.
> *(System: the choice is Rose's. The timetable must be taken before Thursday.)*

scenes.synopsis: Texture — Julian's fear, one line; the cost of the timetable, carried lightly.
scenes.prose:
> After the decision, there was tea — Letitia's doing, arriving with the tray and the tact of a woman who has managed worse evenings — and for a little while the war was only a paper on the table, and they were only two people who had known each other a long time.
> "You are afraid," Rose said. It was not a question.
> "Terrified," said Julian, with the cheerfulness of a man discussing someone else's funeral. "The front knows my name now. Whatever happens at the assembly, I have spent my cover — the one thing a younger son with debts cannot afford to spend, which is why I spent it." He poured — badly, the tea sloshing. "Do you know what frightens me, Rose? Not the ruin. I have been ruined before, in smaller ways, and it is survivable. What frightens me is that you will *win* — in the room, in daylight, with everyone watching — and I will have watched it happen from the edge, having contributed a timetable."
> "A timetable," said Rose, "is not nothing."
> "It is not nothing," he agreed. "It is simply not *enough* — not for the arithmetic I do at night, which is the arithmetic of whether I am the man in this story or the footnote." He set down the cup. "Forgive the self-pity. It is the exposure talking. I am not used to being seen spending."
> "Then get used to it," said Rose, and refilled his cup herself, precisely, without sloshing — a small, exact kindness. "The footnote does not ride through the night with timetables."
>

scenes.synopsis: Beat B7 — the front's confidence: Voss & Hallett's credit on parade, unknowing. Voss in Bath — sly, never overt.
scenes.prose:
> She saw Voss the next day at the Pump Room — there was no avoiding it, and no wanting to: the front's man, in Bath, drinking the waters with the air of a man sampling a vintage he already owns.
> *(System: Mr. Voss — Voss & Hallett's front man; silver watch-chain, easy laugh, the particular confidence of credit that has never once been called.)*
> He was holding court by the King's Bath — three Bath wives, a nodding husband, the whole small theater of a man spending confidence like coin. "The London houses," he was saying, just loud enough, "take a *personal* interest in Bath paper. We find the provincial obligations — charming things, old families, old names — quite sound. Quite *sound*."
> Old families. Old names. *Hers.*
> Rose took her glass of the waters and drank it where he could see her — plain muslin, perfect manners, the second self at its most underestimated — and let him see her seeing him. He bowed — the shallow bow of a man who has already discounted you. She curtsied — the exact curtsy of a girl who has already bought the rope.
> "Miss Hartwell," he said, coming over with his glass. "Bath agrees with you. Though one hears — " the smile, the pause, the practiced intimacy of the well-informed — "one hears the Hartwell obligations are coming to market. A pity. Old names. One would hate to see them — scattered."
> "Would one?" said Rose. "I find scattered things have a way of being gathered. Like watercress. Like gossip."
> He laughed — delighted, unthreatened, utterly sure. "Charming. Do take care of yourself, Miss Hartwell. Bath can be — expensive — for the unwary."
> She watched him rejoin his court, confidence on parade, unknowing — and felt, for the first time all week, the particular pleasure of a secret kept in public.
>

scenes.synopsis: Overheard — the front's men at the assembly rooms; Rose listens, underestimated.
scenes.prose:
> That evening she walked past the assembly rooms — not in, past; the second self does not enter where it is not expected — and the evening air carried voices through the open doors of the card room.
> "— the Hartwell block," a voice was saying — London vowels, a clerk's precision. "Voss wants the offers placed Thursday, announced at the assembly. The girl hasn't the money to contest it. Trelawney hasn't the nerve."
> "The girl," said a second voice, amused, "is drinking the waters in a plain muslin. I saw her at the Pump Room. She curtsied to Voss."
> Laughter — the easy laughter of men who have already spent the victory.
> Rose walked on, past the doors, past the lamplight spilling onto the pavement, past the whole unknowing confidence of it — and smiled, there in the dark, where no one could see her not underestimating herself.
> *The girl hasn't the money. Trelawney hasn't the nerve.* They had priced her — and mispriced her — the way the ton had priced her muslins all season: propriety or poverty, never *war chest*. Augusta's draft was on a post chaise somewhere between London and Bath. The bankers' nerve was pooled. Julian's timetable was in her pocketbook.
> She stopped at the corner and looked back at the lit rooms — the rooms where, in a week, the money would change masters in daylight — and made herself memorize the laughter. It would be useful, later, to remember exactly how sure they had been.
>

> Élise's letter came with the morning's second post — half business, half intelligence, the way all her letters were now.
> *Chérie — the board is kind to you this week. Three standing orders completed: the widow's silk softened, the debutante's ball gown fitted, the riding habit remade (she changed her mind back, as foretold). The coins are in your purse — spend them on the war, not on ribbons.*
> *The Bath clients gossip while pinned, as always. Two wives of bankers, one widow of a banker, all having gowns altered for "the assembly" — everyone is dressing for something, chérie, and no one will say what. The widow said the front's man has ordered a new coat. Vanity, before a victory. Remember this.*
> *The masterwork for your assembly gown waits on my word — say when, and Bath's plain-clothes are retired forever. — É.*
> Rose counted the coins into the purse — the slow, honest engine of the season, turning thread into money while she turned money into standing — and smiled at the postscript about Voss's new coat. Vanity, before a victory. The front was dressing to be seen winning. So, she reflected, folding the letter, was she — except that she meant to do it in a gown, and he meant to do it in a coat, and only one of them knew which of the two was the costume.

scenes.prose:
> *(System: the occasion brief is published.)*
>
> **Occasion brief — A Banker's Dinner**
> *Trelawney's table, Thursday. Four banking houses. The brief: dress to be taken seriously by men with ledgers — morning dress with an affidavit's gravity. Judged on one question: does it say* solvent, exact, and unafraid *without a word about money?*
>
> Élise has sent the Bath dresser with three directions:
>
> **A. The Counting-House** — slate-grey merino, high collar, silver buttons; severity as solvency.
> **B. The Hartwell Ledger** — deep burgundy jaconet, jet trim, cameo at the throat; the house's signature.
> **C. The Quiet Capital** — ivory cambric, dove-grey shawl, pearl buttons; the negotiator's dress.
>
> *(System: commit to a direction — remembered for the dinner. Then the pins: 5 coins each from play earnings; no Crown SKUs.)*
>
> **Pin 1 — Ground:** merino, jaconet, or cambric — the fabric carrying the argument. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 2 — Collar:** to the jaw (fortress), the throat (parley), eased (confidence). *5 coins.*
> **Pin 3 — Sleeves:** plain and narrow — no flourish where figures are discussed. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 4 — Bodice:** seamed severity or quiet drape. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 5 — Waist:** belt, sash, or the cut alone. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 6 — Skirt:** walking length — a woman heard standing. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 7 — Shawl or spencer:** dove-grey wool, or none — bare shoulders are not banked. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 8 — Button's statement:** silver (precision), jet (gravity), pearl (peace). *5 coins.*
>
> *(Story morsel: the dresser pins the collar. "Bankers look first at your hands. They check for the tremor.")*
>
> **Pin 9 — Glove's fit:** kid, exact — no tremor visible, none felt. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 10 — Glove's color:** grey, black, or ivory — three different sentences. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 11 — Heel:** low and certain. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 — Stockings:** silk, clocked or plain. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 13 — Hair's severity:** coiled plain, or one curl at the temple. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 — Hairpiece:** none, a comb, or a simple pin — restraint, graded. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 — Earrings:** small, and still. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 16 — Pendant:** a cameo, or nothing — the throat, unadorned. *5 coins.*
>
> *(Story morsel: "The Queen Square gentleman says a lady's brooch tells him her debts. He collects them.")*
>
> **Pin 17 — Reticule:** small enough to prove she hides nothing — yet holds the pocketbook. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 — Handkerchief's edge:** hemstitched plain, or the Hartwell oak-leaf worked at the corner — gold, silver, steel, or black silk thread; a banker notices needlework and prices it. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 19 — Scent:** nothing — the boldest choice; or orange water. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 20 — Final mirror:** the whole gravity, judged on the brief's single question. *5 coins.*
>
> *(Story morsel: the dresser steps back. "There, miss — a woman the ledgers would lend to. Mr. Trelawney's clerk has been downstairs twice — anxious, miss, in the way of men brave before dinner.")*
>

scenes.prose:
> *(System: reveal coda — the ritual's payoff. Rose descends to Trelawney's dining room in the full chosen direction, gravity complete to the last pin.)*
> Trelawney's dining room was everything the counting-house had promised: mahogany, candlelight, the faint smell of polish and prudence — and four bankers rising as she entered, with the particular courtesy men extend to a ledger they have decided to trust.
> *(System: the room reads the look — solvent, exact, unafraid. The Queen Square man notes the brooch, or its absence; the Milsom Street man notes the gloves; the old Bath bank notes everything and says nothing.)*
> Dinner was served — soup, fish, the removes — and between the courses, the war was discussed the way bankers discuss everything: in sums, in dates, in the conditional perfect. The draft would arrive Saturday. The holders had Rose's word. The front's man would place his offers Thursday and find — if the week went as planned — the shelves empty and the room watching.
> "Miss Hartwell," said the Queen Square man over the fish, "I have lent to a hundred enterprises. I have never lent my *presence* to one." He lifted his glass. "To the block."
> "To the block," said the table — four bankers, one heiress, the candles burning steady.
> And Rose, in her gravity of merino or jaconet or cambric, looked round the table and understood that she had done the thing Trelawney had said took a particular art: she had been taken seriously by men with ledgers. The collar stood. The gloves were exact. The throat showed bone, not blood.
> The room, she thought, had recalculated early.
>

> **[T2 · Maneuver]** — The toast, answered: *standing / seated / with a look round the table.* (Remembered: how she takes the room — the assembly will recall it.)

scenes.synopsis: After dinner — Trelawney's nerve: the banker, frightened and game.
scenes.prose:
> They were the last two in the dining room — the bankers gone into the night with their pooled nerve, the candles burned low — and Trelawney poured the last of the wine with the care of a man performing a rite.
> "They will stand," he said. "The Queen Square man will stand because he hates the front's manners. The Milsom Street man will stand because he smelled a profit in your certainty. The old bank will stand because it has never once been surprised, and does not intend to begin now." He set down the decanter. "And I, Miss Hartwell — I will stand because you shook my hand on the pavement, in the lamplight, where anyone might see. A banker does not get many moments like that. We are not, as a profession, given to pavements."
> "Are you frightened, Mr. Trelawney?"
> "Terrified." He smiled. "It is the '97 panic, my father's story, all over again — except that this time I am the one telling it, and the child listening is myself. Do you know what he told me, that winter? *Nerve is the only asset that compounds.* I have compounded caution for thirty years, Miss Hartwell. This week I am compounding something else, and it feels — " he searched for the word — "like being young."
> "Then be young, Mr. Trelawney." Rose rose. "And thank you — for the dinner, for the houses, for the nerve."
> "Thank me at the assembly." He walked her to the door. "In daylight. When the money changes masters and the room recalculates — thank me then, where the front can see you doing it."
>

> **[T2 · Look]** — The rite of the wine: *watch it / join it / let it pass.* (Remembered: her patience with frightened, game men.)
> **[T3 · Choice]** — Thank him now or at the assembly: *now / then / both.* (Converges: the thanks are real. Remembered: the promise — Ch21 will collect it.)
> **[T4 · Maneuver]** — "Be young": *as counsel / as a gift / as an order.* (Remembered: the line — he will quote it to his clerk.)
> **[T5 · Stance]** — The pavement handshake, recalled: *owned / laughed at / honored.* (Remembered: how she holds shared history — his loyalty deepens.)
> **[T6 · Micro]** — The door, reached: *a curtsy / a handshake / a nod.* (Remembered: small ceremony — the footman sees.)

scenes.synopsis: Texture — the walk home from the dinner; Bath at night, holding its breath decoratively.
scenes.prose:
> She walked home — it was not far, and the night was fine, and a general does not always require a carriage — through Bath at its most beautiful and most watchful.
> *(System: the Crescent by lamplight; the assembly rooms dark across the square; a cat on a wall, philosophical; the town's windows lit like a ledger's ruled lines.)*
> Every window she passed was a small, lit calculation: who had been at Trelawney's dinner, what had been decided, what Miss Hartwell had worn and what it had meant. Bath was holding its breath — decoratively, the way Bath did everything: the breath held behind a fan, behind a teacup, behind the Pump Room's morning small talk. By tomorrow the dinner would be retail gossip. By Thursday the whole town would know the bankers had pooled something, though no one would know quite what.
> Let them. The breath-holding was the point — or part of it. A town holding its breath is a town *watching*, and a town watching is a town that will *see*: the assembly, the daylight, the money changing masters, the front's credit on parade and then — not on parade. Augusta's condition, kept the way Augusta kept everything: exactly, and in public.
> At the lodgings' door she paused and looked back at the dark assembly rooms — one week. One week of breath-holding, of dinners and timetables and drafts on post chaises. One week, and then the room.
> "Soon," she told the dark rooms, very quietly. "Dress well, Voss. Wear the new coat. We are all of us dressing to be seen winning."
>

scenes.synopsis: The plan's traces, hidden — the servants' hall begins its work; loyalty, earned, not bought.
scenes.prose:
> Mrs. Pye's letter arrived with the Saturday post — Hartwell House to Bath, the housekeeper's upright hand, the paper smelling faintly of the stillroom.
> *Miss —*
> *The draft's coming was noted below stairs before it was noted above — the post chaise is a loud conveyance, miss, and the strongbox has opinions. I have told the hall: nothing said, nothing seen, nothing carried. The footmen understand. The maids understand. Marlow understands best of all, which is saying a great deal.*
> *Coin buys hands, miss. You bought none of us. That is why the hall is yours — the London front's man tried a footman last month, with money, and was refused. I thought you should know that the refusal happened, and that it will happen again.*
> *The house is quiet. The Park is quiet. We are all of us, miss, holding our breath — though not decoratively, like Bath. Plainly, like people.*
> *— E. Pye*
> Rose read it twice, and folded it into the pocketbook — with Quill's list, with Augusta's letter, with the whole growing archive of the war.
> Below stairs, the hall was holding its breath — plainly, like people. The plan's traces were being hidden by hands she had never paid to hide them. Loyalty, earned, was doing the work that coin could only rent.
> "Plainly, like people," Rose repeated, and felt the week's arithmetic shift: the nerve had another column now, one the bankers' sums had not included — the servants' hall, standing where the room could not see it, hiding a war's traces because the house was theirs too.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE ASSEMBLY. Force the confrontation there, find a quieter venue, or let the front choose the ground.
scenes.prose:
> Sunday. The draft had arrived — Augusta's war chest, in Trelawney's strongbox, counted and receipted. The holders had Rose's word. The bankers had pooled their nerve. Julian's timetable was in the pocketbook. And the assembly — announced, placarded, the talk of Bath — was six days off.
> *(System: three ways to meet the front; the week will shape itself around the choosing.)*
> Force the confrontation at the assembly: lay the block in the room, in daylight, before the houses — Augusta's condition, kept exactly. The front's credit on parade becomes the front's credit on trial. The risk: everything, in public — if the block falters, it falters where everyone can see.
> Find a quieter venue: settle the purchase solicitor-to-solicitor, declare it by letter, let the assembly be merely a ball. The risk managed, the exposure limited — and Augusta's condition broken, the statement unmade, the Network free to try again somewhere darker.
> Let the front choose the ground: hold the block ready and let Voss's Thursday offers set the terms of the meeting — react, don't dictate. The most patient course. The most *passive* — and passivity, Rose had learned all season, was the one luxury the money never permitted its opponents.
> Rose stood at the window, watching the Sunday promenade — Bath in its best, strolling as though no war were being planned in its counting-houses — and chose the ground the way she had chosen everything that week: in daylight, without flinching.
> *(System: the choice is Rose's. The week takes its shape from it.)*

Everywhere, the breath-holding: decoratively, as always. > "The arithmetic of a man dividing by a number he did not expect to find in the equation." Trelawney permitted himself a smile. "You, Miss Hartwell. You are the unexpected number."

scenes.synopsis: ★ FASHION-SELECTION — no coin cost, remembered. The week's discretion: how the campaign dresses its face between the dinner and the assembly.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: fashion-selection — diegetic, no coin cost. Remembered: the callers will comment, and the Gazette will judge.)*
> "Between the dinner and the assembly," Letitia said, laying three options across the bed, "you must be seen, and be seen *not* to be dressing for anything. The town is watching. Dress the watching."
>
> **A. The Plain Campaign** — the second self, perfected: rose-white muslin, a blush of pink barely there, ivory whitework sprigs at the hem — the motif small enough to miss, exact enough to remember; hair dressed plain with a single pearl pin; grey kid gloves, a straw bonnet with blush ribbons, her mother's ring and no other jewels. Let them go on underestimating her until the room.
> **B. The Quiet Ledger** — dove-grey silk, the dinner's gravity softened for daylight: a narrow oak-leaf border worked up the hem in silver thread — prosperity with roots, whispered; a steel-grey spencer, silver-grey gloves, a dove bonnet; hair coiled smooth; the cameo at the throat, or nothing. Solvency, worn lightly.
> **C. The Hartwell Colors** — burgundy jaconet, worn unapologetically: wheat-ears climbing the skirt in gold thread — the Park's harvest, declared; a copper-brown spencer, gold kid gloves, a burgundy velvet bonnet with a gold wheat-ear pin; hair dressed high with the silver oak-leaf comb. The house that is buying, dressing like it means it.
>
> Rose chose, and Letitia nodded — slowly, the plan's last piece fitted. "Well chosen. The town will read it — propriety, poverty, or war chest. The beauty of it, my love, is that all three readings are true."
> "The whole truth," said Rose, "is reserved for the assembly. In daylight. Where everyone can see it."
> "Spoken like a woman with a war chest." Letitia folded the rejected silks away. "Your grandmother would be proud. I am terrified, and proud — the two are not incompatible."

scenes.synopsis: Quill's second letter — the London front's schedule confirmed; the paper's last word before the assembly.
scenes.prose:
> Quill's second letter arrived Thursday evening — the solicitor's hand, the Lincoln's Inn seal, the particular brevity of a man who bills by the quarter-hour and has decided this one is worth it.
> *Miss Hartwell —*
> *The front's offers were placed today, as your timetable foretold. The shelves, I am told, were empty — the holders having had your word first. Voss & Hallett's man has written to London in some haste; the haste, my clerk informs me, is visible in the hand.*
> *The assembly will therefore find the front embarrassed before it is bloodied — a pleasing order of operations. My clerk — Alder, dismissed, you recall — has been seen in London in company I do not like. Watch my office, not my clients; but watch, also, the road between.*
> *The de Valcourt papers continue to surface. One endorsement, new to me: "to be settled against the Hartwell account" — in a hand I take to be the principal's own. He is closer to this paper than we knew, Miss Hartwell. He wants the Park the way a man wants a debt repaid — personally.*
> *Burn this. — Q.*
> Rose read it twice, and held it to the candle — and watched Quill's hand blacken and curl, the de Valcourt endorsement and all, into ash.
> Personally. The principal wanted the Park *personally*. The war had a face behind the glove now — not seen, never seen, but *felt*: a hand on the paper, a want with a name, a London financier who meant to finish what Rackham started and take the house as well as the money.
> "Burned," she told the ash. "As instructed. And noted — " she touched the pocketbook, where the unburned truths lived — "as well."
>

scenes.synopsis: The week's campaign, reviewed — Letitia's courage, building; the aunt, steady.
scenes.prose:
> "The draft is in Trelawney's strongbox," Letitia recited, counting on her fingers — the household book's discipline applied to war. "The holders have your word. The bankers have pooled their nerve. The front's man has written to London in a hasty hand. Julian's timetable was — " she glanced up — "was it right?"
> "To the hour."
> "Then the timetable is *trusted*." Letitia set down her mending. "Rose. I have been the comic aunt all season — the chocolate, the cushions, the cowardice as a domestic art. I want you to know: I am frightened, and I am *steady*. They are not incompatible. I have tested the theory — "
> "Extensively," Rose finished, and took her aunt's hands. "I know, Aunt. I have always known. The comedy was never the cowardice — it was the cover. Like my muslins."
> Letitia's eyes shone — briefly, fiercely, the way they had shone once before, the night before the Last Assembly. "They won't know what hit them, darling."
> "No," said Rose. "They won't. They have priced us — propriety or poverty, the girl in the muslin, the bankers' nerve a finite asset. They have mispriced everything, the way the money always misprices people: as sums. We are not sums, Aunt. We are — " she searched for it — "we are the unexpected number."
> "The unexpected number," Letitia repeated, savoring it. "I shall have that embroidered on a cushion. After the assembly. In daylight."
>

scenes.synopsis: Henry's steadiness — the dispatch system's last word; the Horse Guards whisper, steady.
scenes.prose:
> Henry's letter came Friday — the soldier's hand, the Bath postmark, the particular brevity of a man who writes the way he stands: straight.
> *Miss Hartwell —*
> *The dispatch roads are as we mapped them. The front's money moves like supply — by timetable, by route, by men who believe a schedule is a kind of armor. Your block, laid across their route at the assembly, is the correct maneuver: cut the supply line in daylight, where the whole army can see it cut.*
> *I will be in Bath for the assembly. Not in the room — on its edge, where I can be useful if the useful is required. You will not see me unless you need to. That is the whole of the offer, and the whole of the man.*
> *Stand steady. The uniform will be somewhere behind you, even if the man is not beside you.*
> *— H. Beaumont*
> Rose read it standing at the window, and felt the week's last piece settle — not the bankers' nerve, not Augusta's draft, not Julian's timetable, but this: the quiet certainty of a man who offered position instead of flattery, and meant it the way he meant everything.
> "On its edge," she repeated. "Where he can be useful." She folded the letter — into the pocketbook, with the rest of the war's archive. "That is the whole of the offer, and the whole of the man. And it is — " she considered the phrase the way one considers a jewel — "it is *enough*. More than enough. It is exactly enough."
