scenes.prose:
> Saturday. The assembly five days off. Rose sat with the pocketbook open and did the week's reckoning — the final column, ruled off fair.
> *(System: the archive — Quill's list, Augusta's letter, the timetable, Henry's letter, Mrs. Pye's letter, Élise's postscript about the coat. The war, in paper.)*
> What the win would cost, tallied true: Augusta's draft — spent, and to be repaid. Trelawney's peace — spent, and not repayable. The bankers' nerve — pooled, and to be honored. Julian's cover — spent, and the front knew his name now. Her own name — on the purchase, in daylight — spent most of all: after the assembly, the principal would know her, personally, the way he wanted the Park personally.
> What losing would cost: the Park. The hall scattered. Honoria's sponsorship a joke. Drummond's second installment named over a ruin. The money winning again, the way it won thirty years ago.
> She ruled off the column — the win's, the longer in cost and the shorter in ruin — and wrote beneath it, in the margin, the week's whole doctrine in four words: *In daylight. At the assembly.*
> Then she closed the pocketbook, and went down to dinner, and ate with an appetite that surprised Letitia — because the reckoning was done, and the only thing left was the doing, and the doing, she had learned all season, was the part she was good at.

scenes.synopsis: The front's men, confident — the date set; Voss's credit on parade, unknowing, one last time.
scenes.prose:
> She saw them Sunday on the Crescent — Voss and his London clerk, taking the air with the particular stride of men whose Thursday had gone better than it had.
> *(System: the new coat — Élise's postscript, confirmed; vanity, before a victory, cut in the first style of London.)*
> They did not see her — the second self, the plain muslin, the bench by the elm where she sat with her mending like any Bath widow's companion. They talked, as confident men do, just loudly enough.
> "— the assembly," the clerk was saying. "The offers announced in the room. Voss & Hallett's name on the Hartwell paper — the ton will see the front's credit, and the houses will — "
> "The houses will follow," said Voss. "They always follow credit. Credit on parade, my boy — that is the whole of banking. Show them the money, and they will show you their throats."
> *Show them the money, and they will show you their throats.* Rose's needle paused — one stitch, unmade, in the mending. Then resumed. The mending was Letitia's, the bench was public, the muslin was plain, and the two men walked on, confident, unknowing, discussing the parade of a credit that was about to be called in daylight by a girl with a pocketbook.
> She finished the row — neat, exact, the stitches even — and thought: *dress well, Voss. Wear the new coat. We are all of us dressing to be seen winning.*

> "It is done," Trelawney said, laying the instruments before her — the draft, the holders' acceptances, the solicitor's forms with the chosen face written fair. "The block settles solicitor to solicitor, as planned. At the assembly, the declaration — in the face you have chosen." He looked at her over his spectacles. "Miss Hartwell. Are you certain of the face?"
> Rose looked at the forms — at the name written there, whichever name her choosing had put — and thought of Augusta's condition: *in the open*. Of Voss's new coat. Of the room, recalculating. Of the principal, who wanted the Park personally and would know her name after this, personally, whatever face the paper wore.

scenes.synopsis: Augusta's war chest — the draft, counted; the trust, named a loan, carried like a standard.
scenes.prose:
> The draft itself she saw only once — Trelawney brought it up from the strongbox, laid it on the parlor table between them like a relic, and watched her look at it.
> *(System: Augusta's hand — the sum, the signature, the Dowager's seal. Forty years of counsel and funds, drawn against exactly this week.)*
> It was, Rose thought, the most beautiful piece of paper she had ever seen — not for the sum, though the sum was handsome, but for what it said without saying: *I have kept my own counsel and my own funds for forty years against exactly this week. Spend them.*
> "It is a loan," she said — to Trelawney, to the room, to the ghost of Augusta's expectations. "Until the paper is ours. A gift only if I fail to repay it — which I do not intend."
> "The Dowager," said Trelawney carefully, "did not name it a loan."
> "The Dowager," said Rose, "did not need to. I named it." She looked at the draft a moment longer — the seal, the hand, the forty years. "A Hartwell does not win a war on her grandmother's pin money and call it victory. She wins it on a loan, and repays it, and calls *that* victory."
> Trelawney returned the draft to the strongbox — the lock turning with its period-at-the-end-of-a-sentence sound — and said, very quietly: "Your grandmother chose well, Miss Hartwell. In the granddaughter, I mean. Not the draft."

scenes.prose:
> Tuesday brought rain — the soft, deliberate rain of Bath in autumn, washing the Crescent's stone to the color of old silver.
> *(System: the town in the rain — the Pump Room's talk gone indoor and therefore louder; the assembly placards damp at the edges; the Crescent empty of promenaders, full of purpose.)*
> Rose watched it from the lodgings' window, the pocketbook closed on her lap, the week's machinery wound and ticking: the draft in the strongbox, the holders' word given, the bankers' nerve pooled, the front's man writing hasty letters to London, Voss's new coat hanging somewhere in readiness for a parade that was about to become a trial.
> The rain, she thought, was the town's last ordinary weather. After this week, nothing in Bath would be ordinary again — not the assembly rooms, not the banking houses, not Miss Hartwell in her plain muslin, about whom the ton could no longer decide. The revision was coming: upward, in daylight, before the houses.
> Letitia came in with tea, looked at the rain, looked at Rose, and said: "You are thinking something formidable."
> "I am thinking," said Rose, "that rain is the only thing in Bath this week that is not holding its breath."
> "Then let us drink to the rain." Letitia poured. "The one honest thing in the county."
> They drank to the rain — decoratively, like everything in Bath, except that this time they meant it.
>

scenes.synopsis: The assembly announced — placarded, proclaimed; one week; Voss & Hallett will be there, credit on parade.
scenes.prose:
> Wednesday. The assembly was announced — not whispered, *announced*: placards on the Pump Room's board, the news in the Bath paper's society column, the whole town informed, in print, that the assembly rooms would open Tuesday next for an evening of dancing, cards, and — though the placards did not say so — the money changing masters in daylight.
> *(System: the announcement — the town's machinery engaging; the bankers' wives ordering final fittings; Voss's name on the patrons' list, credit on parade.)*
> Rose read the placard at the Pump Room with the second self's perfect composure — plain muslin, attentive manners, the girl the ton could not decide about — and felt the week's shape lock into place around her like the last pin in a gown.
> One week. The draft in the strongbox. The holders' word. The bankers' nerve. Julian's timetable. Henry on the edge. Augusta's condition. Voss's new coat. The front's hasty letters. The room, waiting to recalculate.
> "Miss Hartwell." The Bath paper's society man, bowing — the shallow bow of a man who writes what he is told. "Will you be attending Tuesday?"
> "I will be attending," said Rose. "I would not miss it. I understand — " she let the pause do the work — "I understand the credit on parade will be *exceptional*."
> He wrote it down. Of course he wrote it down. By evening, all Bath would know that Miss Hartwell had smiled at the placard, and the smile would be retail gossip by morning — interpreted, misinterpreted, and entirely beside the point, which was the placard itself: *one week*.
>

scenes.synopsis: "Buying the rope" — the chapter's title, named aloud; the doctrine stated before the week.
scenes.prose:
> "Buying the rope," Letitia said that evening, turning the phrase over like a new gown. "That is what we are doing, isn't it? Not buying the paper. Buying the *rope*."
> "Drummond lent us rope once," said Rose. "Public credit, when the ruin was at its worst. We paid her price for it — Honoria, the afternoons, the dances. This is different. This rope we are buying for *them* — the front, the Network, the hand behind the glove. We are buying it in daylight, at the assembly, with their credit on parade."
> "And then?"
> "And then," said Rose, "we let them hang themselves with it. Politely. In public. The way they meant to hang us — with paper, and witnesses, and the room recalculating."
> Letitia was quiet a moment. Then: "Your grandmother's condition. Your bankers' nerve. Julian's timetable. Henry on the edge. The servants' hall, holding its breath plainly, like people." She counted them off — the household book's discipline, applied to war. "It is a great deal of rope, Rose."
> "It is exactly enough rope." Rose stood, and went to the window, and looked out at the Crescent where the lamps were coming on. "The money has hanged people with paper for thirty years, Aunt — my grandfather, the émigrés, Julian's brother. On Tuesday, the paper hangs the money. That is the whole of the doctrine. That is the whole of the week."
> "In daylight," said Letitia. "At the assembly."
> "In daylight," Rose agreed. "At the assembly. Where everyone can see."
>

scenes.synopsis: Texture — Rose alone: the nerve arithmetic, closed; the week before the assembly, held.
scenes.prose:
> Thursday. The front's man placed his offers — Julian's timetable, to the hour — and found the shelves empty. Friday. The bankers dined at the White Hart and were seen to be cheerful. Saturday. The draft slept in the strongbox. Sunday. The rain. Monday. The placard. And now — the week itself, the last whole week before the assembly, held in Rose's hands like a thing with a pulse.
> *(System: the pocketbook, the candle, the week's last arithmetic — closed, ruled off, the doctrine in the margin: In daylight. At the assembly.)*
> She had bought the rope. The purchase had a face — her choosing, worn by the week. The bankers had pooled their nerve. The hall was hiding the traces. The town was holding its breath, decoratively. Voss was dressing to be seen winning, in the new coat, unknowing.
> There was nothing left to do but wait — the hardest maneuver in the book, the one no pin could buy and no draft could fund. Waiting, in daylight, where everyone could see her waiting: the plain muslin, the perfect manners, the girl the ton could not decide about, sitting on the war like a hen on an egg, hatching — what? First blood. Drawn in public. In daylight. At the assembly.
> She closed the pocketbook. She blew out the candle. She lay in the dark and listened to Bath breathe — decoratively, all around her — and thought, with the week's last clear thought: *we are ready. The rope is bought. On Tuesday, the money hangs.*
> The town breathed on. The week held. The doctrine glowed behind her eyes until sleep came — *in daylight, at the assembly, where everyone can see.*
>

scenes.synopsis: ★ GAZETTE STING — the paper's verdict on the week: the bankers' dinners, the held breath.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: the Gazette sting — delivered as the paper itself, the chapter's public verdict.)*
>
> *From the Gazette, under Mrs. Nance Bell's imprint:*
>
> *"Miss Hartwell dines with bankers. Bath holds its breath, decoratively.*
>
> *The Hartwell heiress — so long the ton's puzzle in her plain muslins, propriety or poverty, never quite decided — has been seen at Trelawney's table, and at the White Hart after it, in company no heiress keeps by accident. Four banking houses, one young lady, and a gravity of manner the ton has not previously had the pleasure of pricing.*
>
> *What is pooled at a banker's dinner? Nerve, one hears. Miss Hartwell's gown spoke of solvency; her gloves were exact; the Queen Square gentleman is said to have studied her brooch the way other men study their ledgers.*
>
> *Bath holds its breath — decoratively, of course. But held it is, and the assembly is a week hence, and Voss & Hallett's credit will be on parade there, exceptional, as Miss Hartwell herself remarked, with a smile the society man wrote down.*
>
> *The ton awaits the exhale."*
>
> *(System: the sting lands — no cruelty, no mercy. Bell inquires; she never asserts. The week is priced in public.)*
>
> Rose read it at breakfast, twice, and set it down beside the placard's clipping with unusual care. Bell had priced the week to the pin: the gravity, the gloves, the brooch studied like a ledger, the smile the society man wrote down. The paper had not named the war — Bell never named what she could inquire about — but the inquiry was the whole of it: *what is pooled at a banker's dinner?*
> "Well," said Letitia, pouring, "she has priced the gloves. She has priced the brooch. She has even priced your smile, which the society man wrote down, the traitor."
> "She has priced everything," said Rose, "except the rope." She folded the paper. "The rope is not yet for sale. On Tuesday, the ton will see what the rope was for."
>

scenes.synopsis: ★ CLIFFHANGER — the assembly announced: one week; Voss & Hallett will be there, credit on parade.
scenes.prose:
> The final placard went up Tuesday morning — the assembly, announced for the Tuesday after, the patrons' list printed fair — and Rose walked down to the Pump Room to read it with the town.
> *(System: the patrons' list — the banking houses of Bath, the county families, and there, in the first rank of the commercial names: Voss & Hallett, London. Credit on parade.)*
> One week. She stood among the morning crowd — the wives, the widows, the water-drinkers, the whole decorative held breath of Bath — and read the list the way she had read Quill's list, the way she had read Augusta's letter: as a warrant.
> Voss & Hallett would be there. Voss himself — the new coat, the silver watch-chain, the easy laugh, the confidence of credit never once called — would be there, announcing his offers in the room, publicly, with witnesses, to show he could. And she would be there — in whatever the week required, the plain muslin retired or not, the purchase's face worn like a gown — and the money would change masters in daylight, before the houses, where everyone could see.
> The crowd thinned. The placard stayed — damp at the edges, the ink still fresh enough to smudge. Rose touched one corner — *Voss & Hallett, London* — with the tip of her glove, lightly, the way one touches a fuse.
> "One week," she said — to the placard, to the town, to the war. "Dress well, Voss."
> She walked home through the waking town, and Bath — decoratively, as always — held its breath a little tighter.
>
> *(System: Chapter 19 ends. The assembly is announced — one week; Voss & Hallett will be there, credit on parade. The rope is bought. On Tuesday, it is used.)*
>

scenes.synopsis: Open from Chapter 19's cliffhanger — the plain clothes retired. The second self, folded away with honors.
scenes.prose:
> The muslins came down from the peg on Sunday morning, and Rose folded them herself.
> *(System: the second self — the plain muslins, the perfect manners, the girl the ton could not decide about. Worn all season as camouflage, as doctrine, as armor.)*
> She folded each gown the way one folds a flag after a campaign: slowly, exactly, without ceremony and without haste. The grey, gone soft at the elbows from a season's wear. The dove, with the mended hem no one had ever noticed. The white, yellowing a little at the seams — the one she had worn to Trelawney's table, to the White Hart, to the reading of the placard.
> "You are sure?" Letitia asked from the doorway.
> "The town has decided what the muslins meant," said Rose. "Propriety or poverty — the ton's little puzzle, solved to everyone's satisfaction and nobody's. Tomorrow the puzzle changes." She laid the last fold flat. "They were never a disguise, Aunt. They were a *doctrine* — be underestimated, and be exact. The doctrine stands. Only the cloth retires."
> Letitia came and laid her hand on the folded stack. "They served well."
> "They served *exactly*." Rose closed the trunk. "And now — " she turned to the window, where Bath lay in its Sunday best, the assembly one week closer than the placard had promised — "now we dress to be seen winning."
> The trunk's lock clicked. Somewhere below, the house went on with its morning — the servants' hall, the kitchen, the whole loyal machine that had hidden the war's traces all week. The second self was retired. The first self — the Hartwell, the unexpected number — was about to be dressed.
>

scenes.synopsis: Élise's Bath masterwork arrives — the assembly gown, the season's first signature: "dressed to be seen winning."
scenes.prose:
> The gown arrived Monday at noon, in a trunk the size of a small boat, with Élise's letter on top and the Bath dresser standing guard over it like a grenadier.
> *(System: the masterwork — the season's first signature gown. Emerald silk, the exact green of Hartwell Park's beech avenue in high summer; silver embroidery climbing the skirts in wheat and oak — harvest and home, prosperity with roots; the bodice cut to say* solvent *in a language the banking houses speak fluently.)*
> Élise's letter was short, for Élise: *Rose — I have dressed duchesses for coronations and I tell you plainly, this is the best thing I have made in Bath. The wheat is for the Park — what you are fighting for. The oak is for the house — what you are. Silver thread, the new approved — I insisted. Wear it like a standard. Burn the muslins. — É.*
> "Burn the muslins," Rose read aloud. "She has been talking to my aunt."
> The dresser unpacked it fold by fold — the emerald silk catching the noon light, the silver wheat-ears climbing from hem to waist, the oak leaves worked so fine they seemed to move — and Rose stood looking at it the way one looks at an army one has raised: with pride, with terror, and with the absolute certainty that it was too late to raise any other.
> "Well," said Letitia faintly, from the doorway. "Well."
> "Well," Rose agreed. "Dress me, if you please. The standard is to be worn."
>

scenes.synopsis: Letitia's courage — "They won't know what hit them, darling." The aunt, steady, before the fitting.
scenes.prose:
> Letitia walked around the gown three times without speaking — the way she had once walked around a horse she meant to buy, checking its legs.
> "Well?" said Rose.
> "Emerald," said Letitia. "Gold wheat. Oak leaves." She stopped, facing her niece. "Rose. I have been the comic aunt all season — the chocolate, the cushions, the cowardice as a domestic art, and you have been kind enough to let me. But I want you to know what I know: I am frightened, and I am *steady*, and I have been steady since the night your grandfather's ledgers came out of the strongbox."
> "I know, Aunt."
> "Do you?" Letitia's eyes were bright — fierce, the way they had been the night before the Last Assembly. "Then know this too: when you walk into those rooms tomorrow in that gown — in *that*, with the silver wheat and the oak and the whole of Hartwell Park climbing your skirts — they won't know what hit them, darling."
> Rose laughed — startled, delighted, the week's first true laugh. "Say it again."
> "They won't know what hit them, darling." Letitia took her hands. "The bankers will recalculate. Voss will reach for his watch-chain. And the principal — wherever he is, whatever glove he is wearing — will learn, the way one learns an enemy's name, that the Hartwell girl in the muslins was never the whole of it."
> "The muslins are retired," said Rose.
> "The muslins are *honored*," Letitia corrected. "And now, my love — shall we see whether the standard fits the soldier?"
>

scenes.synopsis: Mrs. Pye's letter — the servants' hall loyalty: the staff hid the plan's traces; they are an asset, not merely staff.
scenes.prose:
> Mrs. Pye's letter came with the Monday post — the housekeeper's hand, the Hartwell Park seal, the particular gravity of a woman who has managed a great house through a ruin and means to manage it through a war.
> *Miss Rose —*
> *The hall has had its orders and kept them. The footman Jem refused the gentleman's money — the second gentleman, the one with the clerk's manners, who offered a crown for news of your comings and goings. Jem told him the household's business was the household's, and the gentleman went away empty, which is more than he deserved.*
> *The maids have said nothing to the Bath girls about the bankers' dinners, though the Bath girls have asked, as girls will. The kitchen has fed double and asked half. The whole hall knows something is afoot — servants always know — and the whole hall has decided, without being told, to be the floor you stand on rather than the floor that gives way.*
> *They are not staff, Miss Rose. You know it, and now I am telling you I know you know it. They are the house. Reward them as such, or I shall be cross, and you know what that means.*
> *— E. Pye*
> Rose read it twice, and felt the week's foundations settle a fraction deeper — the bankers' nerve, Augusta's draft, Julian's timetable, and under it all, this: the floor that would not give way.
> "The house," she said softly. "She is right. They are the house."
>

> **[T2 · Look]** — Jem's refusal: *linger / savor / note the crown.* (Remembered: the footman's price — and his refusal of it.)
> **[T3 · Choice]** — The letter's keeping: *pocketbook / with the war's archive / framed in the hall.* (Converges: the letter is kept. Remembered: where loyalty lives — in paper.)
> **[T4 · Maneuver]** — "I know you know it": *answered in kind / with a laugh / with gravity.* (Remembered: her correspondence with power — below stairs.)

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE SERVANTS' HALL. Reward the household's loyalty openly, quietly, or with the Park's future.
scenes.prose:
> Monday afternoon. Mrs. Pye's letter lay open on the desk, and Rose did the arithmetic no ledger could do for her: the price of loyalty, and the manner of its paying.
> *(System: three ways to reward the hall. The household hid the war's traces — Jem's refused crown, the maids' silence, the kitchen's double feeding. The reward must match the service; the manner will be remembered below stairs for a generation.)*
> Reward them openly: a gift for every servant, given by her own hand in the hall, named and thanked before them all. The honor would be public, the gratitude unmistakable — and the talk, inevitably, would travel: a household rewarded on the eve of the assembly invites the town to ask *what for*.
> Reward them quietly: the gifts distributed by Mrs. Pye, with Rose's thanks carried privately — no assembly of the hall, no speeches, no audience. The dignity of discretion — and the risk that quiet gratitude reads, below stairs, as the gratitude of those who are embarrassed to be grateful.
> Promise the Park's future: no gifts now, but a promise — restoration, security, a place in the Park's future for every servant who stood the war. The grandest reward, and the cheapest in the present — a promise is only as good as the assembly, and the hall knows it.
> Rose looked at Mrs. Pye's last line — *or I shall be cross, and you know what that means* — and smiled, and chose the way she had chosen everything that season: exactly, and in the knowledge that the manner would outlive the money.
> *(System: the choice is Rose's. The hall will remember the manner for a generation.)*
>

The maids went about their work with the particular brightness of people whose silence has been priced correctly. The kitchen fed double and asked half, as before — but now with the air of shareholders rather than servants.
> Mrs. Pye reported it all in three lines: *The hall is yours, Miss Rose. It was always yours. Now it knows it.*

> "Ours," she corrected softly — to the corridor, to the house, to no one and everyone. "The hall is *ours*, Mrs. Pye. You taught me the grammar."

scenes.synopsis: Julian's warning — his one-line "be careful": fear, spoken plainly.
scenes.prose:
> Julian came Tuesday at dusk — not announced, not expected; the drawing room, the rain beginning, the timetable between them now a trusted thing.
> *(System: Julian — exposed, rebuilding, witnessed. His cover is spent; the front knows his name. He came to say one thing.)*
> "The assembly is tomorrow," he said. "Voss will be there with his credit on parade, and the room will recalculate, and you will walk in wearing — " he gestured at the trunk upstairs — "a standard. I know the plan. I gave you the dates. I am not here to unmake it."
> "Then why are you here?"
> He was quiet a moment — the old silence, the one she had learned to read like a letter. Then: "Be careful."
> It was not counsel. It was not strategy. It was fear — plain, unadorned, the fear of a man who has spent his cover and his brother's memory on a woman's war, and who cannot bear the arithmetic of what it might cost her. *Be careful.* Two words, and in them everything he could not say: *do not be ruined; do not be hurt; do not make me watch.*
> Rose crossed to him — and did not touch him, quite; the room was not the place, the week was not the time. "I am always careful," she said. "It is my least attractive quality. The ton finds it tedious."
> "The ton," said Julian, "is not the one who — " He stopped. "Be careful," he said again. And left, before the second saying could become a third.
>

scenes.synopsis: Laurent's warning — his one-line "be careful": charm, worn lightly over something real.
scenes.prose:
> Laurent arrived Wednesday morning with flowers — jasmine, white, the stems still wet — and the particular brightness of a man who has decided to be charming about something serious.
> *(System: Laurent — the charm, the Frenchman's ease, the suitor who flirts with the war the way he flirts with everything. Under it, something real.)*
> "For the eve of the battle," he said, presenting the jasmine. "The flower of — what is it the English say? — amiability. One must be amiable before one ruins people. It is in the regulations."
> "There are no regulations, Laurent."
> "There are *always* regulations, chérie. They are simply written afterward, by the victors." He set the jasmine down — gently, for all the lightness. "Tomorrow you walk into the rooms in emerald and silver, and the banking houses recalculate, and Voss reaches for his watch-chain. It will be magnificent. It will be *terrible*. And I am here to say the thing no one in this town says plainly — " his smile thinned, just for a moment, and the real thing showed through — "be careful."
> Charm, worn lightly over something real: the fear, translated into French, into flowers, into regulations written afterward. *Be careful* — which meant: *come back from the rooms the same woman who walked in.*
> Rose took the jasmine. "Amiability," she said. "I shall wear it with the emerald. The ton will be confused, which is half the battle."
> "Confuse them all," said Laurent. "Only — " the smile, the real one — "come back."
>

scenes.synopsis: Henry's warning — his one-line "be careful": steadiness, the soldier's version.
scenes.prose:
> Henry came Wednesday at noon — on foot, in uniform, the Bath street stopping a little to watch him pass, the way streets do for soldiers.
> *(System: Henry — the uniform, the man, the position, no flattery. He will be on the edge of the rooms tomorrow, where he can be useful.)*
> "Miss Hartwell." He bowed — the soldier's bow, exact. "I have walked the dispatch roads once more. The front's money moves as the timetable said. Voss comes down tonight; his credit will be on parade by morning. The room will be — " he considered — "receptive to arithmetic."
> "You have a gift for understatement, Major."
> "It is the army's gift. We understate everything except the casualty lists." He was quiet a moment. Then, with the particular steadiness of a man stating a fact rather than a feeling: "Be careful."
> Steadiness, not fear: the soldier's version. *Be careful* — which meant: *the maneuver is sound; see that the soldier executing it comes home.* No plea in it. No charm. An order, almost — given by a man who had no right to give her orders, and who knew it, and who said it anyway because some things are more important than rights.
> "I will," said Rose. And then, because steadiness deserved an answer in kind: "The maneuver is sound, Major. And the soldier — " she met his eyes — "the soldier intends to come home."
> "Good." He bowed again. "On the edge of the rooms, then. Where I can be useful."
>

scenes.synopsis: Octavia's warning — her one-line "be careful": clarity, the friend's version.
scenes.prose:
> Octavia came Wednesday afternoon — without ceremony, without flowers, with the particular directness of a woman who has never in her life said anything decorative.
> *(System: Octavia — the friend, the clarity, the one person in Bath who has never underestimated Rose and never will.)*
> "I have come to say one thing," she said, "and then I am going to drink your tea and tell you about the Millersons' card party, because the eve of a battle should have at least one ordinary hour in it."
> "One thing."
> "Be careful." Octavia set down her cup — precisely, in the center of its saucer. "Not because the plan is unsound — the plan is *sound*, I have checked the arithmetic myself, which is more than the banking houses have done. Not because Voss is dangerous — he is a fool with a watch-chain, and fools are only dangerous when they are desperate, which he is about to be. Be careful because — " she looked up — "because you are my friend, and I am not in the habit of losing friends to arithmetic."
> Clarity, the friend's version: *be careful* stripped of romance, of charm, of command — down to the plain fact underneath. *Do not be lost. Not to this. Not to them.*
> Rose felt something loosen in her chest — the week's fourth warning, and the first that asked for nothing but her safety. "The Millersons' card party," she said. "Tell me everything. Spare no detail. I want one ordinary hour."
> "The Millersons," said Octavia, pouring, "are the most ordinary people in Bath, and I say that with affection."
>

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE WARNINGS. Four people said "be careful" — each in their own language. Heed Julian, heed Henry, or heed none and trust the plan.
scenes.prose:
> Wednesday evening. Four warnings, four languages — and Rose weighed them the way she had weighed Quill's list: as intelligence, not orders.
> *(System: three ways to carry the warnings into tomorrow. Each names whose voice walks into the rooms with her.)*
> Heed Julian: take his fear as the truest counsel — the man who spent his cover knows the cost of exposure better than anyone. Let his *be careful* temper the plan: keep him out of the room, soften the declaration, guard the flanks. The romance would feel the sheltering — and resent it, or bless it.
> Heed Henry: take his steadiness as the order it almost was — the soldier's *be careful* means the maneuver is sound and the soldier must come home. Let his voice set the tempo: no improvisation, no flourish, the block laid exactly as mapped. The safest course — and the one that leaves no room for the daring the rooms may require.
> Heed none, trust the plan: thank them all, carry none of them — walk in with the plan as the only voice, the way she has walked all season. The warnings were love, not intelligence; the plan is intelligence. The risk: to seem — to *be* — unmoved by the people who love her, on the eve of needing them most.
> Rose stood at the window — the Wednesday dark, the rooms lit across the town like a promise — and chose whose voice would walk beside her tomorrow.
> *(System: the choice is Rose's. The warnings are carried, or set down.)*
>

- **Heed none, trust the plan** — *The plan as the only voice.* The warnings were love, not intelligence; she walks in with the plan alone — and risks seeming unmoved.

scenes.synopsis: Texture — Bath before the assembly: the rooms lit, the banking houses arriving; the town dressed for the exhale.
scenes.prose:
> Thursday. Bath put on its evening face early — the assembly rooms lit from within like a lantern, the Crescent's windows catching fire one by one, the whole town dressed for the exhale it had been holding all week.
> *(System: the town, the day before — the banking houses arriving: Trelawney's partners from Bristol, the Queen Square gentleman's cousins from London, Voss's clerk seen at the White Hart with the new coat brushed and the watch-chain polished. The ton's carriages out in force, the wives in their assembly silks a day early, the Pump Room's talk at full boil.)*
> Rose walked through it in the afternoon — not the muslin now (retired, honored, folded), but the dove-grey silk of the banker's dinner, worn like a flag of truce before the standard was unfurled. Everywhere, the reading of her: *Miss Hartwell, out walking. Miss Hartwell, calm. Miss Hartwell — what is she planning?*
> She let them read. The town's reading was the town's business; hers was the rooms, tomorrow, the recalculation. She stopped on the Crescent and looked down at the lit rooms — the windows blazing, the chandeliers being raised, the whole bright machine of Bath society winding itself for the evening it had been promised.
> "They are lighting the lamps," said Letitia, coming up beside her. "For us, my love. Whether they know it or not."
> "For us," Rose agreed. "Whether they know it or not."
>
> **[T1 · Tone]** — "For us": *as a vow / as a joke / as a fact.* (Remembered: the claim — the rooms will test it.)
> **[T2 · Look]** — The lit rooms: *study the windows / the chandeliers / the crowd.* (Remembered: what she hunts — the machine, winding.)

scenes.synopsis: Voss's credit on parade — the front's confidence, seen plainly; the parade before the trial.
scenes.prose:
> She saw him Thursday evening on Milsom Street — Voss, with his clerk, with two London gentlemen she did not know, walking the town the way a general walks a battlefield the night before: proprietorially.
> *(System: the parade — the new coat (Élise's intelligence, confirmed), the silver watch-chain, the easy laugh; the confidence of credit never once called, on display in the lamplight.)*
> "— the assembly," Voss was saying, just loudly enough, "the offers announced in the room, publicly. Voss & Hallett's name on the Hartwell paper — the houses will see the front's credit, and the houses will follow. They always follow credit."
> *They always follow credit.* The clerk nodded; the London gentlemen nodded; the lamplight nodded. It was, Rose thought, the most complete sentence of confidence she had ever overheard — and the most completely wrong, because it assumed the shelves would be full, the holders willing, the Hartwell paper unguarded, and the girl in the dove-grey silk merely out walking.
> She walked on — past them, unseeing, unseen, the second self's manners outliving the second self's muslins — and thought: *dress well, Voss. Parade well. Tomorrow the credit is called, in daylight, where everyone can see.*
> Behind her, the laugh rang out — easy, unknowing. She did not turn. Turning was for people who had not already won the only part of the war that mattered: the knowing.
>
> The clerk glanced her way — once, incurious, the way clerks glance at widows' companions. Voss did not glance at all. Men on parade never see the audience; they see only the parade.
>
> **[T1 · Tone]** — "Dress well, Voss": *as irony / as courtesy / as a vow.* (Remembered: the line — it will be spoken in the rooms.)
> **[T2 · Look]** — The watch-chain: *study it / the coat / the gentlemen.* (Remembered: the parade's details — the trial will inventory them.)
> **[T3 · Maneuver]** — Unseeing, unseen: *performed / natural / savored.* (Remembered: her camouflage's last use — the muslins' ghost.)

> **[T6 · Choice]** — Report to Trelawney, or keep it: *report / keep / tell Letitia.* (Converges: the parade is noted. Remembered: her intelligence habits — to the end.)
> **[T7 · Tone]** — The laugh, behind her: *left ringing / answered / filed.* (Remembered: the sound — tomorrow it stops.)

scenes.synopsis: Drummond's letter — "The second installment will be named. Not yet." The old debt, the eve.
scenes.prose:
> Drummond's letter came Thursday night — the heavy paper, the Vienna seal, the particular hand of a woman who writes as though every sentence were a contract and every contract had a price.
> *Miss Hartwell —*
> *I have watched your week with interest. The bankers' dinners. The pooled nerve. The gown — emerald, I hear, which is bold, and silver, which is approved. You have played the money's game with the money's own pieces, and I find I do not dislike the sight.*
> *The second installment will be named. Not yet.*
> *Tomorrow, the rooms. I shall not be there — I dislike assemblies, and I dislike being seen to dislike them even more. But I shall read Bell's paper on Saturday, and I shall read it the way I read contracts: for what is not said.*
> *Do not disappoint me, Miss Hartwell. I have so few investments that interest me.*
> *— V. Drummond*
> Rose read it standing by the fire, and felt the old debt settle around her shoulders like a shawl she had forgotten she was wearing: Honoria's sponsorship, the afternoons, the dances — the rope Drummond had lent when the ruin was at its worst, and the price still unnamed, still hanging, still *not yet*.
> "Not yet," she said to the fire. "Everything in this town is *not yet*. The assembly. The recalculation. The installment." She folded the letter. "Well. Tomorrow, several things become *yet*."
>
> She set the letter with the others — the archive's dread, filed between the warnings and the gown. The Vienna seal seemed to watch her as she folded it.
>
> **[T1 · Tone]** — "Several things become yet": *as wit / as defiance / as a vow.* (Remembered: how she meets the unnamed price.)
> **[T2 · Look]** — "Emerald, which is bold": *savored / noted / underlined.* (Remembered: Drummond's eye — the ton's best-informed.)
> **[T3 · Choice]** — The shawl, shrugged off or worn: *shrugged / worn / folded.* (Converges: the debt stands. Remembered: how she carries old debts — into battle.)
> **[T4 · Maneuver]** — "I shall read Bell's paper": *noted / used / feared.* (Remembered: the Saturday paper — a second audience.)
> **[T5 · Stance]** — "So few investments": *as flattery / as threat / as both.* (Remembered: how she prices Drummond's interest.)
> **[T6 · Micro]** — The fire, read by: *standing / sitting / pacing.* (Remembered: small truth — the letter's theater.)
> **[T7 · Tone]** — The folding: *precise / brisk / twice.* (Remembered: how she files dread — with the war's archive.)

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — DRUMMOND'S LETTER. Answer it, ignore it, or let Augusta answer it.
scenes.prose:
> The letter lay on the desk — *the second installment will be named. Not yet* — and Rose weighed the three ways of carrying an unnamed price into the rooms tomorrow.
> *(System: three answers to Drummond. The old debt is real; the naming is hers to hasten, delay, or delegate.)*
> Answer it: write tonight — coolly, exactly, the way one writes to a creditor one respects and does not fear. Name her own terms for the naming: after the assembly, at Drummond's convenience, in the open. The risk: to negotiate on the eve of battle is to divide the mind — and Drummond negotiates the way she plays cards, which is to say, to win.
> Ignore it: let the letter lie unanswered until Saturday's paper — fight tomorrow's war with today's mind undivided. The dignity of it — and the danger: Drummond does not like to be unanswered, and a woman who names installments does not forget the silence.
> Let Augusta answer it: send the letter on to the Dowager by express — the rear guard dealing with the old creditor, the two powers settling the price between them. The relief of delegation — and the cost: to hand Drummond to Augusta is to admit, however privately, that the debt is bigger than the debtor.
> Rose took up her pen — or set it down, or reached for the express seal — and the eve took its shape around the choosing, the way the week had taken its shape around every choosing before it.
> *(System: the choice is Rose's. The installment waits — but not, after tonight, unnamed in her mind.)*
>
> **[T1 · Look]** — "Not yet," weighed: *as a threat / as a courtesy / as a clock.* (Remembered: how she reads delay — Drummond's whole art.)
> **[T2 · Stance]** — The debt's size: *owned / minimized / priced.* (Remembered: her honesty — Augusta will test it.)
> **[T3 · Tone]** — The choosing: *swift / savored / with dread.* (Remembered: the decision's manner — the eve's last.)
> **[T4 · Micro]** — The pen: *taken up / set down / cleaned.* (Remembered: small truth — the desk's theater.)
> **[T5 · Choice]** — Show Letitia the letter, or not: *shown / kept.* (Converges: the house knows enough. Remembered: trust's measure — to the end.)
> **[T6 · Maneuver]** — The express seal, considered: *reached for / set aside / weighed.* (Remembered: how she uses Augusta — as shield, or not.)
*★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — Drummond's letter:*
- **Answer it** — *Respect, divided mind.* Write tonight, coolly, exactly; name her own terms for the naming — and negotiate on the eve of battle.
- **Ignore it** — *Dignity, danger.* Let it lie till Saturday's paper; tomorrow's war with today's mind — and Drummond does not forget silence.
- **Augusta answers** — *Delegation, admission.* The Dowager settles with the creditor; relief — and the quiet admission the debt is bigger than the debtor.

scenes.synopsis: Texture — the eve, Rose alone: the nerve arithmetic, closed; everything assembled but the morning.
scenes.prose:
> Thursday night. The house asleep — all but Rose, all but the candle, all but the pocketbook open on the desk like a patient etherized upon a table. (She had read too much modern poetry; Letitia had warned her.)
> *(System: the archive, complete — Quill's list, Augusta's letter, the timetable, Henry's letter, Mrs. Pye's letter, Élise's postscript, Drummond's letter, the warnings in four languages. The war, in paper.)*
> She did the eve's arithmetic — the last column, ruled off fair. The draft: in the strongbox, the face chosen, the solicitors briefed. The holders: word given, shelves emptying. The bankers: nerve pooled, the White Hart dinner a memory of cheer. The hall: rewarded, the floor firm. The gown: fitted, the silver wheat climbing. The warnings: weighed, the voice chosen. The installment: answered, or ignored, or delegated — named in her mind, whatever the paper said.
> Everything assembled but the morning. And the morning — the rooms, the parade, the recalculation — was the one thing no arithmetic could rule off. It would be what it would be: daylight, witnesses, the money changing masters where everyone could see.
> She closed the pocketbook. She wrote in the margin, under *In daylight. At the assembly*, four new words: *Dressed to be seen winning.*
> Then she blew out the candle, and slept — the sleep of a general the night before the battle, which is to say, badly, and then all at once, like a stone dropped in a well.
>

> **[T2 · Look]** — The archive, spread: *read as a story / as sums / as people.* (Remembered: what the war is — paper, money, or hands.)

> **[T6 · Maneuver]** — The stone in the well: *savored / laughed at / kept.* (Remembered: the image — the morning will recall it.)

scenes.synopsis: The final fitting — gown, jewels, nerve assembled; the standard, worn.
scenes.prose:
> Friday morning. The fitting — the final one, the dresser had said, though dressers always say that, the way solicitors always say *one last point*.
> *(System: the masterwork, worn — emerald silk, silver wheat-and-oak climbing the skirts; the bodice's line exact; the candlelight version tested Thursday, the daylight version now. Hair, beauty, accessories: the full instrument.)*
> The gown went on like weather — all at once, and changing everything. The emerald deepened in the morning light; the silver wheat caught it and threw it back; the oak leaves at the waist seemed, absurdly, *proud*. The dresser pinned the last pin and stepped back, and said nothing — which, from a dresser, is the highest praise in the language.
> Then the jewels — from the open shelf, her own, no ritual, no scoring: the emerald and diamond pendant (her mother's), the gold wheat-ear earrings (Augusta's gift, that morning, by express — *for the harvest*, the card said), small and still against the emerald. The hair coiled plain, softened by one curl at the temple; a silver comb, oak-leaf worked, at the crown.
> Rose looked in the glass — the whole gravity, head to heel — and saw not the girl in the muslins, not the puzzle the ton had failed to solve, but the answer: *dressed to be seen winning.*
> "There," said the dresser softly. "That is a woman the rooms will recalculate around."
>
> The mirror gave her back the answer; the dresser gave her back the silence. Both, she decided, were the same thing: *ready*.
>

> *Letitia's table, Friday. Eight covers, no bankers, no ton. The brief is* calm: *dress as still water before the rooms — judged on one question: does it say* steady, loved, and unafraid *without a word about tomorrow? Serene is everything; splendid permitted, if quiet.*
>
> Élise has sent the Bath dresser with three directions:
>
> **A. Moonflower** — pale lavender silk, silver thread moonflowers; serenity as strength.
> **B. Jasmine** — ivory crape, ivory whitework at the hem; Laurent's flowers, worn back.
> **C. Still Water** — dove-grey satin, a single silver comb; the eve's muslin, grown up.

scenes.synopsis: The private dinner — the calm, worn; eight covers, the heart's own; the eve's ordinary hour, kept.
scenes.prose:
> The dinner was eight covers — Letitia, Octavia, the dresser sent home with thanks, the household's best silver, the jasmine in water at the table's center — and it was, by design and by grace, the most ordinary extraordinary evening of the season.
> *(System: the ritual's direction, worn — lavender, ivory, or dove; the moonflowers or the whitework or the plain made perfect; the calm, visible. The table reads it the way the table reads everything: with love, and without mercy.)*
> They talked of everything but tomorrow — the Millersons' card party (finished properly, with all details), the Bath girls' latest bonnets, Mrs. Pye's three lines (*the hall is yours* — Letitia quoted them, and Octavia nodded as though they were scripture). The food was plain and perfect. The wine was poured like a benediction.
> "You look," said Octavia, studying her over the rim of her glass, "like still water."
> "Still water," Letitia repeated, "runs deep, my love. It is the deep ones you watch." She raised her glass. "To the eve."
> "To the eve," said Octavia.
> "To the eve," said Rose — and drank, and felt the calm settle over her like the Kashmir shawl: warmth, offered, against the evening's chill and the morrow's. Tomorrow the emerald, the silver wheat, the rooms, the recalculation. Tonight — the lavender, the pearls, the jasmine, the people she loved, the ordinary hour kept like a sacrament.
> Eight covers. No bankers. No ton. The heart's own. *Calm.*
>

scenes.synopsis: Élise's letter — the atelier's pride; the dressmaker's eve word.
scenes.prose:
> Élise's letter came with the dessert — the dresser having carried it back to the shop and returned with it, the atelier's seal, the particular ink Élise uses for occasions of state.
> *Rose —*
> *The dresser has reported the fitting. She used the words* the highest praise, *which from that woman means she wept, though she will deny it. I believe her.*
> *I have dressed duchesses for coronations, and I have dressed you for tomorrow, and I tell you there is no difference in the work — only in the woman. The emerald will hold. The silver will catch the chandeliers and throw the light back at them, which is precisely what one wants to do to chandeliers on such evenings.*
> *One instruction, from the atelier to the standard-bearer: when Voss reaches for his watch-chain — and he will — do not smile too soon. Let the room recalculate first. Then smile.*
> *Burn nothing. Keep everything. — É.*
> Rose laughed — the eve's second true laugh — and read the instruction twice: *do not smile too soon.* The atelier's tactics, to set beside the bankers' arithmetic and the soldiers' dispatch roads: *let the room recalculate first. Then smile.*
> "Élise sends tactics," she told the table.
> "Élise," said Octavia, "is the only general in Bath who has never lost a campaign."
> "To Élise," said Letitia, raising her glass. And the table drank — to the atelier, to the standard, to the woman who dressed battles and called them fittings.
>

scenes.synopsis: Texture — the ton's reading: the bankers' wives, the assembly silks, the town's last guesses before the rooms.
scenes.prose:
> Saturday morning. The Pump Room — the wives in their assembly silks a day early, the bonnets at their most architectural, the talk at full boil.
> *(System: the town's last guesses — Miss Hartwell's emerald (seen at the fitting, reported by the dresser's girl), Miss Hartwell's calm (seen at the dinner, reported by no one, felt by all), Miss Hartwell's plan (guessed at by everyone, known by no one).)*
> "Emerald," said Mrs. Alderton, loud enough. "With *silver*. Very — decided."
> "Very *Hartwell*," said Mrs. Pye's cousin, who knew things. "The Park's colors, the house's nerve. Mark me — the girl means something by it."
> "Girls always mean something by it," said Mrs. Alderton. "The question is whether the something is a husband or a — " she lowered her voice — "a *position*."
> Rose, taking the waters at the far end of the room in the dove-grey (the last wearing before the emerald — the truce before the standard), heard every word, and smiled into her glass, and thought: *a position, Mrs. Alderton. You have no idea how right you are.*
> The town would guess till midnight. The town was very good at guessing, and very bad at knowing — which was, she reflected, precisely the arrangement the week required.
>
> She finished the waters — tepid, sulfurous, medicinal — and set down the glass with the particular finality of a woman who has drunk worse things for strategy. The Pump Room's talk boiled on without her; it would boil till midnight, and none of it would matter.
>

scenes.synopsis: Trelawney — the last check: the draft, the face, the solicitors; the banker's nerve, holding.
scenes.prose:
> Trelawney's parlor, Saturday noon — the strongbox open, the draft on the table, the solicitors' instruments laid out like surgical tools.
> *(System: the last check — the purchase's face (Rose's choosing, from Ch19), the holders' acceptances, the solicitor's forms written fair; the block, ready to fall solicitor-to-solicitor, the declaration for the rooms.)*
> "The draft," said Trelawney, touching it the way one touches a sleeping dog — respectfully, and ready to withdraw the hand. "The face. The forms. The holders." He looked up. "Miss Hartwell — is there anything I have forgotten?"
> "Your nerve," said Rose. "Have you forgotten that?"
> He laughed — the unbanked sound, the week's second hearing of it. "I mislaid it on Milsom Street, on the pavement, under a lamp-post. You handed it back to me, if you recall."
> "I recall. I am asking whether it has held since."
> "It has held." He closed the strongbox — the lock's period-at-the-end-of-a-sentence sound. "Miss Hartwell. My father banked through the '97 panic on the principle that nerve is the only asset that compounds. I have compounded all week. I am — " he permitted himself the ghost of a smile — "I am *solvent* in nerve, for the first time in my life."
> "Then we are ready." Rose rose. "Tomorrow, Mr. Trelawney. In daylight. Where everyone can see."
> "Where everyone can see," he agreed. And bowed her out — the bow of a banker to a client, and of a soldier to a general.
>

scenes.synopsis: Augusta's eve word — the Dowager's letter: the war chest, the condition, the grandmother.
scenes.prose:
> Augusta's letter came Saturday afternoon — by express, the Dowager's seal, the upright hand that never hurries and never waits.
> *My dear Rose —*
> *The draft is spent, or about to be. The condition stands: in the open. I have kept my own counsel and my own funds for forty years against exactly this week, and I do not propose to have spent them on a solicitor's office.*
> *The earrings are wheat, because you are the harvest. Wear them tomorrow, and think of me when Voss reaches for his watch-chain — I shall be thinking of you, which is the same thing at our age, only warmer.*
> *One thing more, and it is not counsel but grandmother: whatever the rooms do tomorrow — whether they recalculate or merely stare — you are my granddaughter, and the Park is your home, and no paper in Bath can unmake either of those things. The money can take the mortgages. It cannot take the blood.*
> *Win beautifully. — A.*
> Rose read it three times — the way she had read the first one, with hands not quite steady — and then she did something she had not done all season: she pressed the letter to her cheek, briefly, fiercely, the way one presses a hand.
> "Grandmother," she said — to the letter, to the room, to the forty years. "I will win beautifully. It is the only way I know how."
>

> Saturday evening. The pocketbook, open for the last time before the rooms — the archive, complete, the war in paper.
> *(System: the papers — Quill's list (burned, memorized), Augusta's two letters, the timetable (trusted), Henry's letter, Mrs. Pye's letter, Élise's letter and postscript, Drummond's letter (answered, ignored, or delegated), the warnings in four languages, the sting's clipping. The margin's doctrine:* In daylight. At the assembly. Dressed to be seen winning.*)*
> She read them once more — not for information (she knew them by heart) but for company: the voices, on paper, of everyone who had stood the week with her. Quill's haste. Augusta's forty years. Julian's dates. Henry's steadiness. Mrs. Pye's crossness. Élise's tactics. Letitia's courage, between every line.
> Then she closed the pocketbook — the clasp's small, final sound — and tied it with the ribbon, and set it in the drawer, and locked the drawer, and put the key in the workbox, and closed the workbox.
> "There," she said to the empty room. "The war is filed. Tomorrow, it is *worn*."
> The room — the lodgings' little parlor, the week's headquarters — seemed to exhale. The candle burned steady. Outside, Bath held its breath, decoratively, one night more.
>
> The drawer locked with a sound like a secret being kept. The workbox closed. The key — small, brass, warm from her hand — went into the pocket of her dressing gown, to be carried tomorrow with the jewels.
>

scenes.synopsis: Letitia, the eve — courage, complete; the aunt and niece, before the rooms.
scenes.prose:
> "I have laid out your things," said Letitia — the Saturday-night ritual, the week's last: the emerald in its press, the silver comb, the wheat-ear earrings in their box, the pendant, the gloves, the slippers. "And I have written to your grandmother — *win beautifully*, I told her, *is the family motto now* — and I have eaten an entire box of chocolate, in the interests of courage."
> "In the interests of courage," Rose repeated. "Did it work?"
> "It worked *beautifully*." Letitia sat — suddenly serious, the comedy set down like a fan. "Rose. Tomorrow you walk into those rooms, and the money changes masters, and the principal learns your name. I want you to know — whatever the rooms do, whether they recalculate or merely stare — that I have never been prouder of anything in my life than I am of you, tonight, in this room, before any of it."
> Rose crossed to her — and knelt, quite suddenly, and put her head in her aunt's lap, the way she had as a child. "I am frightened, Aunt."
> "I know, my love." Letitia's hand on her hair — steady, warm. "I am frightened too. We are frightened together, which is the only way anyone has ever been brave."
> "They won't know what hit them, darling," Rose whispered.
> "No," said Letitia. "They won't. *Darling*."
>
> The chocolate box stood empty on the table — the interests of courage, served. Letitia's hand was warm on her hair; the week's last comfort, given and taken without ceremony, the way the house did everything that mattered.
>

scenes.synopsis: Henry, confirmed — on the edge of the rooms, where he can be useful; the soldier's eve word.
scenes.prose:
> Henry's note came Saturday night — by his own hand, delivered by a soldier-servant, the particular brevity of orders.
> *Miss Hartwell —*
> *The dispatch roads are walked. Voss is in Bath; his credit parades at the White Hart as I write. The room tomorrow will be receptive to arithmetic — I have seen the guest list, and the houses are all coming, which means the recalculation will have its full audience.*
> *I will be on the edge of the rooms, where I can be useful. You will not see me unless you need to. That is the whole of the offer, and the whole of the man — unchanged from Wednesday, and unchanging.*
> *Stand steady. — H. Beaumont*
> Rose read it by the last candle — and felt the week's last piece settle into place, the way the last pin settles a gown: not the bankers' nerve, not Augusta's draft, not the warnings weighed, but this — the quiet certainty on the edge of the rooms, the uniform behind her even if the man was not beside her.
> "Unchanged," she said softly. "And unchanging." She folded the note into the workbox — with the key, with the archive's sleep. "That is the whole of the offer. And it is — " she considered the phrase the way one considers a jewel — "exactly enough."
> The candle burned down. The rooms waited, lit, across the town. On their edge — somewhere, unseen — the soldier waited too.
>
> **[T1 · Tone]** — "Exactly enough": *said softly / with warmth / with finality.* (Remembered: how she receives steadiness — to the end.)

Not dressed to be admired — though you will be. Not dressed to be married — though the ton will try. Dressed to be *seen winning*."

> "No," said Letitia — and laughed, and cried, a little, both at once, the way brave people do. "They won't. scenes.synopsis: [C] RITUAL — "The Triumph Change": the season's second signature gown; the brief is triumph. Twenty micro-decisions — amethyst silk, laurel motif in silver — 5 coins each, 100 coins. The supper interval, the private parlor, Élise in attendance.
scenes.prose:
> *(System: [C] ritual — the season's second signature. The morning's emerald is retired; the evening requires triumph. Élise has brought the gown to the private parlor, with the atelier's whole art and opinions. Each pin costs 5 coins from play earnings; no Crown SKUs touch the ritual. Jewels come from owned pieces only — the jewel shelf is always open but never a ritual step. Each pin releases one story morsel — the plot breathes between the pins.)*
> Élise's instruction, pinned to the parlor's glass: *"Chérie — this morning you dressed to be seen winning. Tonight you dress as the woman who has won. Amethyst, laurel, silver — and stand like the morning."*
> The transformation — the full building of the triumph — is the ritual: twenty decisions, each one a layer of victory.
> **Pin 1 — The silk:** the amethyst bolt — deep violet silk, the evening's whole depth; chosen over the sapphire and the peach Élise unrolls beside it. Amethyst: triumph's own jewel, unworn all season. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 2 — The bodice:** the triumph's architecture — boned, exact, the posture built into the seams; stand like the morning, the silk insists. *5 coins.* — *Morsel: from below, the ball's musicians tuning; the evening, preparing its applause.*
> **Pin 3 — The motif:** the laurel — victory's own leaf, chosen over the rose and the wheat-ear; the triumph, named in embroidery. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 4 — The thread:** silver for the laurel — the thread library open (gold, copper, ivory whitework, steel, black silk, polychrome), the silver chosen: moonlight on victory. *5 coins.* — *Morsel: Élise, pinning: "Silver, chérie — gold shouts, silver reigns."*
> **Pin 5 — The sleeves:** the amethyst, slashed to show the silver — the triumph's generosity, glimpsed. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 6 — The skirt:** the fall of it — amethyst silk, the laurel climbing in silver from the hem; victory, ascending. *5 coins.* — *Morsel: a note, slipped under the parlor door — Trelawney's hand: "The houses are still turning. — T."*
> **Pin 7 — The overskirt:** silver-shot gauze over the amethyst — the triumph's shimmer, the candlelight's accomplice. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 8 — The neckline:** the triumph's line — high enough for battle, low enough for ball; the posture, framed. *5 coins.* — *Morsel: Letitia at the door, breathless: "Darling — the rooms are filling. They are all asking for you."*
> **Pin 9 — The hair:** dressed high, the triumph's crown — the silver laurel pin for the hairpiece, the morning's comb retired with honors. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 10 — The eyes:** the beauty, built — the kohl, the steadiness; the gaze that bought a morning, kept for the evening. *5 coins.* — *Morsel: from the corridor, Henry's voice, low: "...on the edge, where I can be useful."*
> **Pin 11 — The cheeks and lips:** the color, the calm — triumph, worn lightly; the flush of victory, not the paint of it. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 — The earrings:** the owned pieces, chosen — the amethyst drops, the shelf open, the choice ordinary, no scoring edge; the stones, answering the silk. *5 coins.* — *Morsel: Élise, stepping back: "The stones have waited all season for this silk."*
> **Pin 13 — The necklace:** the silver chain, the single amethyst — the throat, the triumph's signature. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 — The bracelets:** the silver bangles, stacked — the wrists, the morning's work remembered in metal. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 — The brooch:** the laurel brooch, owned — silver, the motif doubled; the triumph, pinned. *5 coins.* — *Morsel: the Gazette's man, glimpsed below through the parlor's glass — Bell's eyes, everywhere, taking notes.*
> **Pin 16 — The fan:** painted, the triumph's instrument — amethyst silk, the laurel in silver; the fan that speaks victory, fluently. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 17 — The reticule:** the evening's one — the morning's papers filed, the evening's empty; triumph carries nothing but itself. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 — The shoes:** the silver slippers — the triumph's footing, exact; the floor, hers. *5 coins.* — *Morsel: the ball's first set, called below; the rooms, ready; the town, waiting.*
> **Pin 19 — The wrap:** the amethyst velvet — the triumph's cloak, for the stairs and the entrance; the reveal, staged. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 20 — The final pin:** the last look — the glass, the woman who has won; the posture, the morning's; the triumph, complete. *5 coins.*
> *(System: 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins from play earnings. The gown is remembered — the ball's scenes react to it. Reveal coda: the mirror moment — Rose in amethyst and silver laurel, the lighting changed, Élise applauding once, sharply; the look saved to the season lookbook — built for screen recording.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE ROOM. Under the chandeliers, in triumph: address the banking houses, let the money speak, or withdraw at the triumph.
scenes.prose:
> The applause faded into the music — the ball, turning, the triumph's hour — and Rose stood at the floor's center with the banking houses of Bath around her: the Queen Square gentleman, the Bristol brothers, the county's chorus, all watching the woman of the morning in the gown of the evening.
> *(System: the decision — three uses for a triumph. The morning's arithmetic is proved; what remains is the evening's statement. Each use is a different doctrine — and the town will repeat whichever she chooses.)*
> Address them: speak to the houses plainly, under the chandeliers — the credit, the arithmetic, the future; the triumph, annotated; declaration as doctrine. The houses would quote her for a generation; the ton would call it bold; the principal would read the report.
> Let the money speak: no speech — the block, the figures, the recalculation, unadorned; restraint as doctrine; the triumph, needing no annotation. The houses would respect the silence; the ton would supply its own words; the principal would read the figures.
> Withdraw at the triumph: leave at the height — the exit, staged; the triumph, unannotated and unexplained; mystery as doctrine. The town would talk for a month; the houses would wonder; the principal would receive a report with no speech in it at all.
> Rose looked at the room — at the houses, the chandeliers, the amethyst and silver laurel she wore like armor — and made the evening's great decision the way she had made the morning's: in public, and without flinching.
> *(System: the choice is Rose's. The town will repeat it; the Gazette will score it.)*

scenes.prose:
> The houses gathered — the Queen Square gentleman foremost, the Bristol brothers flanking, the county's chorus behind — and the evening's statement, whichever she had chosen, landed among them like the morning's figures had: stones, in still water.

> "Miss Hartwell." The Queen Square gentleman bowed — the deepest yet, the bow of a house revising its whole book. "This morning's business — the Hartwell obligations, settled as you settled them — " he paused — "the houses have done their arithmetic."
> "And?" said Rose.
> "And the houses find," he said, "that Bath has been banking with the wrong front." The words, spoken plainly under the chandeliers, traveled the ballroom like weather. "Voss & Hallett's credit — called. The Hartwell interest — " he bowed again — "solvent, and nerve to spare."
> The Bristol elder laughed — the blunt laugh, the prizefight's — and the chorus took it up: the recalculation, complete, spoken aloud, in the evening's ballroom, before the ton. The morning's private arithmetic was now the town's public knowledge.
> Rose received it — the verdict, the bows, the laughter — in amethyst and silver laurel, the triumph's posture, and understood that the day had done what the chapter had promised: the Network had lost money and a mask, and Bath had finished the accounting out loud.

- **Absolve him** — *Romance+, Laurent's trust deepens.* "There is no shame in relief, Laurent. Your family's money was never the enemy — the men who move money like weapons are. Be relieved. Be ashamed. Be both, and be honest about it, which is more than the polish usually permits."
- **Use it** — *Intrigue+, Laurent uneasy.* "Then let the shame work. Your family's bankers are untouched, which means they are *credible* — with the houses, with Trelawney, with me. If the de Varenne name stands apart from the Network's money, say so where it matters. Relief is a position, Laurent. Occupy it."
- **Name it plainly** — *Respect+, the route sharpens.* "You are ashamed because you know the relief is bought with other people's risk — mine, last night, in a lit room. Do not apologize for it. *Choose* instead. The polish is not a position, Laurent. It is a postponement. I am done postponing things."

She thinks of the principal, learning her name, writing his first sentence with it — and of what it would mean to answer a whisper with conduct, with money, with silence.)*

*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The whisper's seed:*
- **Stamp it out now** — *Boldness+. The ton sees nerve; the planter learns she bites.* Confront the talk wherever it surfaces — the Pump Room, the callers, the carriers — and kill the whisper with daylight before it roots.

> *(Letitia holds court at breakfast the next morning — the triumph has gone to her head the way champagne goes to the heads of the virtuous: completely, and with moral uplift.)*
> *Turn 1 — Stance:* laughter — genuine / surprised / needed. *Remembered: the first real laugh since the post — taken.*
> "I have decided," she announces, "that the assembly was won by the gown."
> *Turn 2 — Look-closer:* gown / genius / money's cowardice. *Remembered: the theory — examined for truth.*
> "The gown?" — Rose
> *Turn 3 — Maneuver:* question — played / answered / volleyed. *Remembered: the rally — enjoyed with the aunt.*
> "The Bath masterwork. Élise's genius. Dressed to be seen winning — and you *were* seen, my love, by everyone, winning. The money merely followed the silk. It always does. Money is a coward; it goes where it is best dressed."
> *(Rose laughs — genuinely, for the first time since the post — and Letitia beams, and pours more chocolate, and theorizes on.)*
> "And I have decided something else. We are going home. Augusta says so, the Season says so, and I say so — three authorities, and I am the most reliable. Bath has been delightful, Bath has been victorious, Bath is now *boring*, and I refuse to be bored in a town famous for its waters. Pack the muslins, Rose. The plain-clothes are retired. We go home to be priced properly."

*★ Choice (remembered — no coin cost; Bath will remember the morning's dress):*
- **The Triumphant Burgundy** — *Presence+. The assembly's color, worn again deliberately.* Deep burgundy merino; climbing-rose motif in gold, silver, or copper thread; grey kid gloves, pearl drops, tortoiseshell hairpins, the assembly fan. Bath will read confidence; the Gazette will read nerve.

scenes.prose:
> *(The Crescent, late morning — the chosen dress, the chosen walk, the town performing its favorite occupation: talking of nothing else. Rose takes the long way to the Pump Room, and the long way takes her past everything: the assembly rooms, lit and empty in daylight, the banking houses with their brass like mirrors, the bookseller's window where the Gazette's morning edition is already pasted up for the passers-by.)*
> *Turn 1 — Look-closer:* assembly rooms / banking houses / bookseller's window. *Remembered: the walk's stations — noted in order.*
> *(She stops at the bookseller's window. There it is, in Bell's inquiring type: the assembly, the money, the nerve, scored. A knot of readers stands before it — a clergyman, two spinsters, a young officer — and they read, and they murmur, and one of the spinsters says, quite audibly, "Nerve, scored. Well. I always said the Hartwell girl had *something*," and her companion says, "Something is not a dowry, Eliza," and the first says, "It is better than one, these days," and they move on, still murmuring.)*
> *Turn 2 — Micro:* stopping — deliberate / indulged / brief. *Remembered: the verdict, read in public — permitted.*
> *Turn 3 — Stance:* overhearing — savored / noted / smiled at. *Remembered: *better than a dowry* — kept as the spinsters' crown.*
> *(Rose walks on, and lets the town look. This is the victory's second half — not the buying, which was last night's work, but the *being seen to have bought*, which is this morning's. The plain-clothes taught her the value of being underestimated. The triumphant morning is teaching her the value of the opposite: being estimated, exactly, and found sufficient.)*
> *Turn 4 — Choice:* lesson — learned / applied / banked. *Remembered: estimation — wielded as strategy.*
> *Turn 5 — Stance:* opposite lesson — savored / applied / owned. *Remembered: the underestimation's opposite — learned.*

> *Turn 7 — Micro:* smile — kept / spent / filed. *Remembered: the smile — spent on no audience, banked for herself.*

> **Occasion brief — A Triumphant Bath Morning**
> *The last morning in Bath: calls, the Pump Room, the road. The plain-clothes are retired with honor. The brief is victory, worn lightly — triumph without swagger, nerve without noise. Criterion: every choice must say* I won *without saying* look at me winning.
>
> *Rose reads the brief twice, and chooses a direction — remembered for the morning's calls:*
>
> **A. The General, At Ease** — burgundy and grey; the win, worn like a uniform after the battle.
> **B. The Heiress, Composed** — pearl and ivory; triumph as composure, the hardest kind to argue with.
> **C. The Wit, Triumphant** — jonquil and slate; the win, worn the way she won it — cleverly, in daylight.
>
> *(System: the player commits to a direction — remembered for the morning. Each pin costs 5 coins from play earnings; no Crown SKUs touch the ritual.)*
>
> **Pin 1 — Ground:** merino, lutestring, or jaconet. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 2 — Color:** burgundy, pearl, or jonquil. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 3 — Bodice:** seamed precision or draped ease. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 4 — Neckline:** high or softened. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 5 — Sleeve:** fitted plain, or one flounce. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 6 — Skirt:** walking length. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 7 — Spencer:** grey wool or ivory silk. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 8 — Buttons:** silver or covered silk. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 9 — Gloves:** kid, exact. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 10 — Glove color:** grey, black, or ivory. *5 coins.*
>
> *(Story morsel: the maid pins the collar. "The Pump Room will be watching, miss." Rose smiles into the glass. "Then let it watch something worth the effort.")*
>
> **Pin 11 — Bonnet brim:** wide or close. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 — Bonnet trim:** ribbon, feather, or bare. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 13 — Hair:** coiled precise, or one curl. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 — Shoe:** low heel, certain. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 — Stockings:** silk, clocked or plain. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 16 — Reticule:** letters-sized; nothing to hide. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 17 — Motif:** climbing rose, laurel, or thornless stem — victory embroidered at hem and cuff. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 — Thread:** gold, silver, copper, ivory whitework, steel, black silk, or polychrome. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 19 — Posture:** the room's length — chin, shoulders. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 20 — Mirror:** *victory, worn lightly?* *5 coins.*
>
> *(System: 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. The completed direction is remembered — Bath will react.)*
*Pins 1–20 — all remembered (5 coins each). The pins are the ritual's entire turn budget.*

> *Turn 1 — Look-closer:* thin light / daylight truth / rehearsed line. *Remembered: the glass — faced honestly.*
> *(The light in the lodgings' bedroom is thin and honest, and it does the look no favors — which is the point. This is not candlelight flattery; this is daylight truth. The gown falls in its rehearsed line. The bonnet sits at the rehearsed angle. The glove fits like a second skin. And the woman in the glass — Rose looks at her for a long moment — the woman in the glass is not the underestimated girl in the plain muslin. She is not the desperate heiress of September, either. She is something the season has not yet named: a woman who buys, in daylight, and wears the buying lightly.)*
> *Turn 2 — Stance:* naming — accepted / tried / owned. *Remembered: the unnamed thing — recognized at last.*
> "Well?" — Letitia, from the doorway, where she has been hovering since Pin 12.
> *Turn 3 — Maneuver:* doorway — welcomed / answered / performed. *Remembered: the aunt, hovering since Pin 12 — admitted.*
> "It says I won," says Rose. "Without saying look at me winning. I think. The brief is a hard master."
> *Turn 4 — Choice:* brief — satisfied / questioned / restated. *Remembered: the argument — made to the aunt.*
> "The brief," says Letitia, coming to stand beside her at the glass, "is the easy part. The hard part is the wearing — all morning, in a town that talks of nothing else, with the whisper going round below stairs and the principal learning your name in London. Can you wear it?"

*Turns: 8 — all remembered.*

scenes.synopsis: Trelawney's terror returns — the front's London men ask after Hartwell obligations. The banker needs his officer. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Trelawney comes again at dusk — no grin, no triumph; the terror has eaten the morning's brightness the way the sea eats a sandcastle.)*
> *Turn 1 — Look-closer:* standing / tidal fear / dusk. *Remembered: terror's return — read in the doorway.*
> "Miss Hartwell." — he does not sit, which tells her everything. "A London man was at the counting-house today. Not Voss — a new man, younger, politer. He asked after the Hartwell obligations. Not to buy — to *understand* them. Who holds them now. On what terms. Whether they might — his word — *travel*."
> *Turn 2 — Look-closer:* word / politeness / youth. *Remembered: *travel* — parsed for politeness.*
> *(Rose is very still. The principal's second sentence: first the whisper, now the inquiry. They are learning her ground, obligation by obligation.)*
> *Turn 3 — Stance:* held / used / owned. *Remembered: second sentence — received standing still.*
> "What did you tell him?" — she asks.
> "Nothing." — Trelawney's jaw sets. "I told him the Hartwell obligations are Hartwell's, and that the house of Trelawney does not discuss its clients' paper with strangers, however polite. He smiled — the young, polite smile — and left his card." *(He produces it. The card bears no name Rose knows — a London direction, an agency's address.)* "I have put the ledgers where he cannot find them. But Miss Hartwell — " he looks at her, and the fear in his face is honest, and therefore honorable — "I am a Bath banker. I am not built for this."
> *Turn 4 — Maneuver:* witnessed / encouraged / ordered. *Remembered: officer's work — done and named.*
> "None of us are built for it, Mr. Trelawney." — Rose takes the card, studies it, and slips it into her workbox — not hidden, filed. "We are built for it *by* it. You stood in a lit room and bought. You told a polite young man nothing. You are being built, sir, at an admirable rate."
